author: Sarah Raymundo
title: On liberal opportunism and the “purity” smear
content:
Photo from Naga City Tourism Facebook page

Accusing leftists and activists of demanding a “useless politics of purity” is a classic liberal defense mechanism designed to shift the burden of moral failure onto the critic.

Why did former Vice President and now Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo roll out the pink carpet for the Zionist war machine? When Robredo hosted Israeli Ambassador Dana Kursh for an official courtesy visit, she was not merely performing the routine gestures of local hospitality. She was actively welcoming and legitimizing representatives of the US-Israeli genocidal apparatus. This intervention centers an anti-imperialist analysis to dismantle the liberal apologetics surrounding this act. Rather than an isolated error in judgment, this diplomatic encounter exposes the persistent, foundational tension within the Philippine political landscape: the contradiction between liberal reformism and anti-imperialist national liberation.

Dismissing progressives’ critique of Robredo’s hosting of the Israeli envoy as mere “political purism” is politically and morally impoverished. The underlying mechanism demands a total, systematic critique. To understand why her defenders deploy the “politics of purity” accusation, and why that defense completely falls apart when examining real power dynamics and economic interests, we must lay bare both the liberal class position and the ideological sleight of hand at work.

To make sense of Robredo’s pivot toward imperial hospitality, we must look directly at the liberal class position. Her stance is neither an accidental misstep nor a personal failure of political intelligence but the direct expression of her class character and political alignment. Liberal reformism in the global periphery operates strictly within the legal, institutional, and geopolitical framework dictated by US imperialism.

While Robredo served as a focal point against the overt state terrorism of the Marcos-Duterte dynasties, her opposition was strictly intra-class—a feud over how to manage the neocolonial state, pitting rule-of-law decorum against autocratic violence.

Because her political legitimacy rests upon acceptance by the global capitalist order, her opposition stops at the border of imperial interest. When forced to choose between international solidarity with an anti-imperialist national liberation movement and alignment with the Washington-Tel Aviv axis, liberal reformists invariably side with the imperial core. They cannot critique the drain of value, the extraction of labor, or the military hegemony of US imperialism because their entire political project depends on remaining within that very apparatus.

This structural subservience explains why defenders deploy the “purity politics” weapon whenever that alignment is exposed. Accusing leftists and activists of demanding a “useless politics of purity” is a classic liberal defense mechanism designed to shift the burden of moral failure onto the critic. From a materialist standpoint, this argument relies on three ideological fallacies:

First, it replaces a materialist baseline with ideological absolution. Opposition to active genocide, ethnic cleansing, and imperialist aggression is not a performative or elevated ideological standard; it is the absolute baseline of human solidarity and anti-imperialist struggle. Labeling principled opposition to mass slaughter as “purity” redefines baseline morality as an unreasonable demand, attempting to pass off complicity as pragmatic maturity.

Second, it operates on the logic of liberal idealism, which treats political stances as abstract moral choices made in a vacuum. Political actions reflect concrete class interests. Shielding a public figure from accountability for legitimizing a settler-colonial state serves a specific political function: it conditions the middle forces to accept imperial violence as a routine, acceptable feature of global diplomacy.

Third, it trades scientific alignment for unprincipled unity. Transformative praxis distinguishes between principled unity—built on anti-imperialist struggle and mass interest—and unprincipled unity, which colludes with reaction to preserve electoral coalitions. Demanding that the progressive movement remain silent on international solidarity to protect a liberal politician’s image trades human rights and anti-imperialist consciousness for temporary electoral expediency.

This dynamic reveals the distinct role of the middle forces—segments of the …

author: M. Reza Behnam
title: The Imperial Pen: Geopolitical Vandalism in West Asia
content:
For centuries, the lands stretching from the Levant to the Persian Gulf have been subjected to a strange form of conceptual alchemy. Driven by Western Orientalist scholarship, colonial cartography and modern geopolitical agendas, the dynamic, pluralistic mosaic of West Asia has been systematically reduced to a monolithic caricature, defined by violence, archaic fundamentalism, and in need of rescue.

These mutations are more than mere scholarly failures; they represent a destructive erasure of history. By denying complex societies their natural path toward modernity and stripping them of historical agency, these misrepresentations serve to validate existing systems of oppression.

To truly understand contemporary Arab West Asia, one must recognize that its political boundaries and power dynamics are essentially an imperialist artifact; and that it remains shackled to a modern version of the colonial 1916 Sykes-Picot ghost: artificial borders drawn by foreign pens, hyper-economies addicted to petrodollars, governance models built and local rulers chosen to appease external patrons and crush internal dissent.

British and French colonialists, Mark Sykes and Francois Georges Picot, engineered the systemic underdevelopment of West Asia, through calculated geopolitical vandalism. By secretly carving up Ottoman lands into European spheres of influence during World War I, with total disregard for demographic, tribal and economic realities, they deliberately trapped millions within artificial borders designed explicitly to facilitate trade routes and resource extraction at the expense of organic state-building and stability.

To maintain control and to serve the industrial demands of London and Paris, these external brigands thwarted local independence, weaponized sectarian and religious divisions, and essentially reduced entire societies into fractured resource-milked protectorates.

The Sykes-Picot Agreement and sibling treaties did more than redraw a map, they locked the region into ongoing instability. Imperial powers carved out unnatural states and installed local satraps—chronically fragile in legitimacy—willing to repress their own populations to stay in power and to carry out the bidding of their colonial overlords. This has left a consequential foundational legacy that the region’s people are forced to navigate today.

Even the conventional designation “Middle East” is a colonial byproduct; not born of indigenous geography. The imperialist term originated within the British India Office in the 1850s and gained public attention in 1902 when American naval strategist, Alfred Thayer Mahan, used it to describe the area around the Persian Gulf as a middle zone between the Near East and the Far East.

The Eurocentric label became official terminology during World War II after the British Armed Forces set up their Middle East Command in Cairo. In the 1950s, the United States integrated the term into official foreign policy, transforming a strategic naval calculation into a commonly accepted and used geopolitical descriptor.

Beyond the physical lines on a map, the legacy of imperialism endures in how borders drawn more than a century ago are understood and interpreted today.

When violence erupts in these states, Western discourse routinely defaults to essentialist tropes. They attribute the instability to “ancient ethnic, tribal or religious animosities” or an “inherent inability to govern,” rather than looking at the real roots of the conflicts.

Such oversimplified stereotypes are convenient fiction that absolve colonial powers of their historical responsibility. They conceal the ways in which modern authoritarian regimes, sectarian conflicts, religious factions and state collapses were systematically engineered, armed and manipulated by foreign powers seeking resource dominance and geopolitical control.

In his foundational critique of Orientalism, Palestinian-American scholar, Edward Said, demonstrated how Western academia, literature and media manufactured a false binary, framing the West as rational, logical and progressive, while painting the East as emotional, static and despotic.

In this construction, the people of West Asia are rarely permitted complexity as historical actors pursuing their own liberation, economic self-determination or social reform. Instead, they are filtered through reductionist archetypes; such as:

The fanatic: Driven solely by ancient grievances or religious dogma, entirely divorced from …

author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: From Haile Selassie to Abiy Ahmed: the Human Cost of Imperial Nostalgia
content:
The irony is difficult to escape. Haile Selassie became a symbol of resistance to foreign aggression while denying Eritreans the right to self-determination. Abiy Ahmed was rewarded for accepting Eritrea’s internationally recognized border, yet within a few years his government began advancing claims to sovereign access to the Red Sea. The very territorial settlement that helped earn him the Nobel Peace Prize now stands in tension with his maritime ambitions.

Both men benefited enormously from international recognition. Their reputations gave them prestige and influence, but those reputations have too often overshadowed the suffering of the people under their rule. Haile Selassie’s imperial government suppressed resistance in Tigray and annexed Eritrea. Under Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopia has endured devastating wars, while his government’s Red Sea rhetoric has renewed Eritrean fears of territorial aggression.

I have written about the dangers of romanticizing Ethiopia’s imperial past, most recently in Imperial Nostalgia: History, Sovereignty, and the Unfinished Work of Decolonization in the Horn of Africa. What concerns me today is that this nostalgia is no longer confined to history books or monuments. It has returned to contemporary politics, and the consequences could be catastrophic for another generation of Ethiopians and Eritreans.

Haile Selassie’s reputation rests heavily on his resistance to Italian fascism. His appearance before the League of Nations in 1936 became one of the defining moments of his international career. But the familiar account gives the emperor far more prominence than the people who actually fought the occupation.

Haile Selassie left Ethiopia in 1936 and spent the following years in Britain. Meanwhile, Ethiopian patriots remained behind, fighting a brutal occupation. They lived in the mountains, organized resistance, endured enormous hardship and risked their lives. The emperor became the international face of their struggle, but he was not the one carrying its daily burden.

Consider Belay Zeleke, one of the patriots who fought the Italians. After the emperor returned to power, Belay came into conflict with the imperial government. In January 1945, he was executed alongside his brother and other associates. Think about the irony. A man who had fought foreign occupation was hanged under the authority of an emperor celebrated around the world for resisting that same occupation.

The emperor’s record in Tigray reveals another contradiction. In 1943, when people in Tigray rose against imperial authority during the first Woyane uprising, Haile Selassie turned to Britain for military assistance. British Royal Air Force aircraft bombed Mekelle and other locations. As Human Rights Watch documented, British air power helped suppress resistance to the imperial government.

Here was an emperor celebrated for standing against European aggression using European aircraft against people resisting his own rule. How does that fit the image of a champion of freedom?

Haile Selassie’s reputation as a Pan-Africanist also deserves scrutiny. His role in establishing the Organization of African Unity in Addis Ababa in 1963 was important. But diplomatic achievement should not be confused with a consistent commitment to African freedom.

Haile Selassie and his foreign minister, Ketema Yifru, worked to establish Ethiopia as a center of African diplomacy. Hosting the OAU gave the emperor enormous prestige. Yet the same government was denying Eritreans the right to determine their future.

Eritrea’s federal autonomy had been systematically dismantled before Haile Selassie annexed the territory in 1962. While the emperor was celebrated as a defender of African independence, Eritreans were beginning a liberation struggle that would last thirty years.

The OAU largely treated Eritrea as an internal Ethiopian matter. Its silence is especially striking when compared with Western Sahara. The organization admitted the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic despite Morocco’s fierce opposition. It was prepared to confront one African government over self-determination but failed to extend comparable recognition to Eritreans struggling against Ethiopian rule.

The romanticization of Haile Selassie reached extraordinary heights through the Rastafari movement. Emerging from racial oppression in Jamaica, the movement invested in the Ethiopian emperor with immense spiritual and political significance. For some Rastafarians, he became a …

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Housing, homelessness in focus in Ottawa’s Rideau-Vanier race
content:
Six candidates are vying to represent Ottawa’s Rideau-Vanier ward ahead of next week’s municipal election, with housing, homelessness and support for the Inuit community among campaign issues.


Ottawans are set to elect ward councillors Monday to a four-year term. Rideau-Vanier includes Vanier, sometimes called “Little Nunavut,” home to an urban Inuit community.


Statistics Canada counted 1,270 Inuit in Ottawa in the 2021 census.


Lyra Evans, Julie Fiala Chartrand, Brian Paquette and Michael Karl Sewanaku spoke with Nunatsiaq News about issues that could impact Inuit residents in the ward.


Evans, a former Ottawa-Carleton District School Board trustee and chair, said residents have raised concerns about homelessness, addiction, poverty and food insecurity.


“Pushing people out of a park and destroying all their belongings doesn’t stop them from being homeless,” Evans said, criticizing the city’s approach to encampments.


For more than 30 years, the Rideau-Sussex pedestrian underpass has served as a gathering place for unhoused Inuit. Police patrols, tickets and removals over the summer have

scattered

 people throughout the city.

Evans, who experienced homelessness as a teenager, said Ottawa needs more supportive housing.


“I was fortunate enough to get the resources and support from the system to move from homelessness into a transitional housing program,” Evans said. “But those resources and that support should exist for everyone.”


Chartrand, an artist and community organizer, said she has friends in the Ottawa Inuit Circle, a mutual aid group, and has advocated for it when she was co-chair of a safety committee with the Vanier Community Association.


Her great-uncle, Cst. Albert “Frenchie” Chartrand, was an RCMP officer who spent years in the Arctic, spoke Inuktitut and had family ties to Gjoa Haven.


She has proposed a permanent intercultural gathering space in Rideau-Vanier guided by Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, or Inuit cultural values. She said she also hopes to address safety concerns about aggressive dogs and the sexual exploitation of Inuit women, if elected.  


Paquette, an entrepreneur, martial arts instructor and youth worker, said he has not directly approached Inuit organizations during the campaign. He said he wants to support residents facing homelessness, addiction or mental-health crises.


Paquette said he would donate at least 20 per cent of his councillor’s salary annually to food banks and homeless shelters. He also proposed more proactive overnight police patrols.


Sewanaku, who holds law and medical degrees and is training as a family medicine resident,

argued the city should not displace people without offering alternatives or addressing why they are homeless.


His platform proposes a housing first approach and a public report on the costs of homelessness.


While he has not spoken with Inuit organizations and residents as much as he should have during the campaign, he said he was open to hearing their concerns.


Incumbent Coun. Stéphanie Plante did not respond to an interview request.


During her term, she supported

renaming

 Sandy Hill Park to Annie Pootoogook Park after the Inuk artist and Emond Park in Vanier to Mary Papatsie Park to honour an Inuk woman whose remains were found in Ottawa in 2022.


Eric Smith’s nomination information did not include contact details.

author: James Crump
title: Berlin’s Plan to Take Back Homes Will Cost Europe’s Biggest Landlord £7bn
content:
Europe’s largest residential landlord is set to lose €8.4bn (£7bn) as a result of plans by leftwing political party Die Linke to bring more than 140,000 Berlin flats into public ownership.


The real estate company Vonovia, which owns roughly 130,000 apartments in the city and

528,000

 across Europe, would be the most affected by the plans, with 120,000 of its apartments set to be put into public ownership. Real-estate giant Heimstaden would also be hit hard with a projected loss of $1.5bn (£1.26bn), according to the

Financial Times.


Die Linke, which won Berlin’s state elections in September, has agreed to talks with the city’s Greens and Social Democrats as part of plans to transfer ownership of flats from companies that own more than 10,000 apartments, with the legislation scheduled to be brought forward in 2028.


Any apartments owned above that 10,000 threshold would have to be transferred into public ownership as part of the policy, with Die Linke proposing an average compensation of around €100,000 per apartment – around 40% below the market value.


Vonovia’s 130,000 Berlin properties have an average market value of $130,000, meaning the company would lose a projected $8.4bn if the legislation becomes law. The company’s chief executive Luka Mucic has labelled the plans as “unconstitutional”, adding that the country needs “reliability, legal certainty and a stable investment environment.”


Housing was a

key factor

in September’s Berlin elections and has been growing in importance over the last half-decade, with 10% of the city’s residents currently living in

housing poverty

and 160,000 reported to have

left the

 capital in 2025. In 2021, Berlin’s residents voted in favour of the city’s government seizing privately-owned flats from large corporate landlords, although that vote was not legally binding.


In order to govern in Berlin, Die Linke has had to form a three-way coalition with the progressive Greens and centre-left Social Democrats, leading to potential political concessions from the leftwing party. The Greens came fourth in September’s election on a commitment to push the property law through, but the Social Democrats’ leader publicly

opposed the policy

 en route to a fifth place finish.


Support for Israel is also a sticking point between the three coalition parties, with the Greens and Social Democrats insisting that “Israel’s right to exist” be non-negotiable if they are to govern together. The parties rejected general boycotts against Israel and did not state whether Palestine has a

right to exist

 in a joint document announcing the talks.

author: Marianne Dhenin
title: Tenants Unions Anticipate Housing Policy Gains After Progressives Win in RI
content:
Reclaim Rhode Island demonstrates the power of tenant organizing to effect change in local politics.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The housing crisis emerged as a central issue last month in Providence, Rhode Island, as Democratic socialist David Morales unseated incumbent Brett Smiley in the Democratic primary for mayor and a slate of progressives won their city council races in primaries throughout the Ocean State’s largest city.

In April, Smiley vetoed a rent stabilization ordinance passed the day before, and a month later the city council came up one vote short of overriding his veto.

“The campaign for rent stabilization and Brett Smiley’s veto of it laid the whole framework and groundwork for both David Morales’s race and the council slate,” said Daniel Denvir, co-chair at Reclaim Rhode Island, a member-led housing justice and progressive organizing group that is driving the growth of the Rhode Island Tenants Union. “It was a race around rent stabilization and with a clear mandate to pursue social housing — and we won every single contested race in the city. Now, Providence will be really an unparalleled site for innovative progressive solutions to the housing crisis.”

Reclaim grew out of connections organizers made working on the 2020 Bernie Sanders campaign in Rhode Island and has had some major successes organizing tenant unions across Providence County and in fighting to ban practices that drive rent hikes and profit for landlords, like algorithmic rent setting. One of its biggest wins in the tenant organizing sphere came this June when residents at Charles Place launched their union with supermajority support, becoming the largest chapter of the Rhode Island Tenants Union. The 200-unit apartment block is home to Section 8 tenants, many of whom are aging or disabled. The union has forced the building’s landlord to the table to negotiate an agreement expected to fix persistent problems, including broken air conditioners, an unreliable elevator, and absent management.

After the rent stabilization ordinance in Providence was quashed and an earlier Reclaim-backed effort to protect tenants from unreasonable evictions by codifying just-cause eviction at the state level failed, the organization shifted some of its efforts to organizing around progressive candidates who could help overcome institutional barriers to its just housing agenda in the legislature.

The City of Providence is among the nation’s least affordable for renters. Last year, the city council’s housing crisis task force found that almost half of the city’s renters are spending beyond their means on housing.

“It’s a working-class city, it’s a diverse city, it’s a young city, it’s an artistic and bohemian city, and the unaffordability of housing threatens all of those things that make Providence special,” Denvir told Truthout. “That’s an objective social and economic reality, [and] the role of political organizations like Reclaim Rhode Island is to organize the objective crisis into a collective political response that brings people together to exercise collective power to solve that crisis.”

With progressives expected to hold a majority, if not a supermajority, on Providence City Council after the general election, local organizers are looking forward to implementing the solutions they fought for on the campaign trail.

While candidates were campaigning ahead of Providence’s September 9 primaries, Reclaim fielded about 200 volunteers who knocked on thousands of doors on joint canvasses for Morales and progressive city council candidates. “We won this on the doors,” said Miguel Martínez Youngs, who defeated incumbent John Goncalves by 68 votes in the Democratic primary in Ward 1. Youngs will run unopposed in the general election on November 3.

Ward 1 includes downtown Providence and historic neighborhoods where residents have faced waves of gentrification and displacement. It also includes College Hill, home to Brown University and one of the city’s most affluent neighborhoods. Goncalves has represented the district since 2020 and bills himself as a progressive. But he was also a deciding factor that saw Smiley’s veto of the rent stabilization ordinance stand when he opted not to show up for the vote to override it. “I got good on the campaign trail saying, ‘It wasn’t a no vote, it was a no show — which is worse,’” …

title: Navigieren auf einer neuen Welle von Unruhen
content:
Jetzt ist es wieder soweit, europäische Regierungen zucken zusammen vor Tausenden Randalierer*innen die in den Metropolen auf die Straße gehen, ohne das sie von den Polizeikräften in Schach zu halten sind.


Macron tönt, nicht zum ersten Mal in seiner Amtszeit:

"Wer zerstört hat, muss dafür bezahlen. Wer geplündert hat, muss den Schaden ersetzen. Wer versucht hat, die Republik zu stürzen, wird dafür zur Rechenschaft gezogen."


Die Papageien der Medien schäumen vor Wut, wie immer wenn die Ohnmacht die Seiten wechselt, und auch die freiwilligen Putzkräfte, die im Sommer 2017 beim G20 in Hamburg mit Bürsten die Bordsteine des Schanzenviertels von Krawallspuren beseitigten sind am Start. Jetzt kratzen sie in Paris geschmolzene Leihräder aus dem Asphalt oder sortieren Mülltonnen in Mailand.


Aber wo sind wir? Überrascht von diesen Wutexplosionen, zu deren entstehen wir wie so oft, nicht viel beitragen konnten. Um nicht den Überblick zu verlieren, eine unvollständige Zusammenfassung der letzten Events,


Brüssel


Am 9. Oktober folgten 30.000 Menschen den Aufrufen von Gewerkschaften gegen die antisozialen Maßnahmen der Regierung. Schüler*innen und Student*innen blockierten Bildungseinrichtungen. Von morgens bis abends kam es im Zentrum, im Bereich der Bahnhöfe zu Zusammenstößen mit den Bullen. Unterbrechung des Konsums, statt die wie eine Pest verbreiteten E-Scooter für eine leicht zu trackende Fortbewegung zu nutzen, werden sie heute von Jugendlichen massenhaft ins Feuer geworfen. Die Spannungen hatten sich schon an den Vortagen und auch in anderen Städten angekündigt.


Am 17. Oktober weitere Krawalle in Brüssel und Lüttich, 195 Festnahmen bei einer Demo gegen die Sparmaßnahmen im frankophonen Bildungswesen, gegen die Polizei und gegen die aktuelle belgische Regierung.


Paris


Nachdem letztes Jahr eine Alles Blockieren Bewegung im September an vielen Orten eskaliert war, wurde deren vermeintliches Ende mit einer lahmen Stimmung eines müden Generalstreiks Anfang Oktober 2025 besiegelt. Um plötzlich mit den diesjährigen Bildungsprotesten und Schulblockaden in eine neue Runde zu gehen. Seit Wochen tut die CRS das, was sie immer macht, sie schießen Demonstrant*innen mit Flash-balls die Augen raus und sprengen Jugendlichen mit Granaten die Hände weg. Aber offenbar war am 17. Oktober die Wut größer als die Angst und Frankreichweit wurden Bullen angegriffen, Geschäfte geplündert, Symbole des Staats zerstört. Trotz jahrzehntelanger Erfahrung mit Aufstandsbekämpfung, gelingt es Politik und Verwaltung bisher nicht, die Allianzen von Schüler*innen, Überresten der Gelb Westen, Banlieue Bewohner*innen, Linken und anderweitig Angepissten zu spalten. Macron, der seine Truppen von Kanaky bis Erbil kämpfen lässt und momentan besonders die Golf Monarchien verteidigen will, kündigt Verhaftungswellen und Ausgangssperren an.


Barcelona


Lange blieb es ruhig in Barcelona aber am 5. Oktober kam es wegen der Wohnungsproblematik zu Riots im Zentrum. 100.000 Menschen beteiligten sich an einer Demo, zu der die Sindicat de Llogateres tenants' union aufgerufen hatte, danach Unruhen im Bereich Plaça Catalunya und La Rambla. Bullen setzten wie immer Gummigeschosse ein, 30 Mossos wurden verletzt, Stadtmobiliar lieferte an 28 Stellen das Barrikadenmaterial. Die Sprecherin des Sindicat erklärte als Ziel, das Land zu paralyzieren. Die Regierung hat nach dem Tod von Maricarmen Abascal aufgrund der Zwangsräumung und ihrem Scheitern in der Wohnungspolitik Neuwahlen für den 29. November angekündigt. Anarchist*innen verteilen ein Flugblatt während der disturbios:


"Möge die Wut über alle hinwegfegen. Politische Parteien, Gewerkschaften, Parlamente, alle Organisationen links von der PSOE, Polizei, Richter, Journalisten, Faschisten, jeder einzelne von ihnen ist Teil desselben Apparats zur Kontrolle und Bewältigung unseres Elends. ... Unser einziges Ziel ist es, Bündnisse im Kampf und auf der Straße zwischen Gleichen zu knüpfen, unsere Klassenfeinde zu identifizieren und sie mit allen Mitteln anzugreifen."


Mailand


Am 17. und 18. Oktober erlebte Mailand in seinem kommerziellen Zentrum die Ausschreitungen, die es verdient. Dort drehte sich die Demonstration um die für viele nicht mehr zahlbaren Lebenshaltungskosten. Wie in den anderen Städten auch wurden Bullen angegriffen, Geschäfte geplündert, Banken zerstört und überflüssiges Zeug den Flammen übergeben. Der Bürgermeister Giuseppe Sala befand:

title: Fırat: Cem Foundation seeks to appoint trustee to Kıraç Cemevi
content:
A vigil launched in protest against the eviction order to transfer Kıraç Cemevi, which was built through the collective efforts of local people in Esenyurt and has served the community for nearly 20 years, to the Cem Foundation has achieved its first result. The eviction has been postponed for one month. Those demanding the complete cancellation of the transfer decision are determined to continue their vigil outside the cemevi until their demand is met. Celal Fırat, Istanbul MP for the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), spoke to ANF and said, “The Cem Foundation, which operates according to the government's mentality, is seeking the support of the government-appointed trustee who took control of Esenyurt Municipality to effectively impose a trustee on Kıraç Cemevi as well.”


‘The walls of this cemevi were built through the people's labour!’


Celal Fırat, MP for the DEM Party, brought the decision to transfer Kıraç Cemevi to the Cem Foundation on the grounds that it stands on Treasury-owned land before parliament and met with the Interior Minister to seek its cancellation. Fırat stressed that the cemevi had been built over the years through the collective efforts of the Alevi community.


Fırat explained that Alevis from Yozgat and Ordu, as well as Turkmen and Çepni Alevis, live in the area surrounding Kıraç Cemevi. He said, “Around 20 years ago, Turkmen Alevis from Yozgat and Ordu, together with our Çepni community members, came together in Kıraç, Esenyurt, and established a place of worship using their own resources. Some contributed their labour, others their earnings, and some donated an entire day's wages. The walls of that cemevi contain more than stone and concrete. They hold the memory of a neighbourhood, the sweat of its people, the prayers of mothers, the breath of pirs and the collective labour of generations. In the 1990s, when Alevi institutions had limited opportunities to obtain legal status and organise, many cemevis began operating under foundations recognised as serving the public interest. Kıraç Cemevi also began providing services under the Cem Foundation during this period. However, this did not change the fact that Kıraç Cemevi is a place of worship built and managed through the collective efforts of local people, where cem ceremonies have been held, lokma offerings shared and funeral services carried out for years. The Kıraç Cemevi Cultural Association, made up of local residents, has been responsible for running the cemevi for years. There had been no problems until now. However, problems have continued for the past year because the Cem Foundation has attempted to remove the existing local management and replace it with its own appointees, relying on the authority to make appointments granted by its statutes. Alevis are standing up against this imposition by the Cem Foundation, which refuses to recognise the will of the people. The community does not accept this system of appointed management.”


‘The Cem Foundation sought control of the cemevi from the trustee who seized Esenyurt Municipality’


Fırat pointed out that the Cem Foundation had claimed the land on which Kıraç Cemevi stands belongs to the Treasury and had requested its allocation from the Ministry of Environment and Urbanisation and Esenyurt Municipality, which is under the control of a government-appointed trustee.


Fırat said that the dispute had led to legal proceedings between the parties. Although the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association filed a lawsuit seeking to suspend the eviction decision issued by Esenyurt Municipality, Istanbul's 3rd Administrative Court rejected the request for a stay of execution. He explained that Esenyurt Municipality's Municipal Police Directorate served an eviction notice on the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association on 6 October 2026, ordering it to vacate the cemevi. Fırat said, “Citing the decision of Istanbul's 3rd Administrative Court dated 10 September 2026, which rejected the request for a stay of execution, Esenyurt Municipality's Municipal Police Directorate claimed that the Kıraç Cem Cultural Association was occupying the premises unlawfully. The directorate notified the association that it must vacate the building and hand over the keys to the Istanbul Provincial Directorate of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change under the Istanbul Governor's Office. The Municipal Police Directorate gave the association 15 days from the date of notification to vacate the premises and …

author: Wir bleiben alle Friedrichshain
title: Protestkundgebung gegen Wohnraumzerstörung und Vertreibung in der Gürtelstraße 39-41
content:
Mehrere Jahre standen die beiden ehemaligen Hotels in der Gürtelstraße 39-41 leer. In den letzten Jahren sind dort Menschen eingezogen, die auf den überteuerten Berliner Wohnungsmarkt keine Chance gehabt hätten. Sie nannten das von ihnen besetzte Gebäude Hugo-Haus. Ende September wurden die Bewohner*innen mit einem großen Polizeiaufgebot auf die Straße gesetzt. Aber sie verschwanden nicht einfach. Direkt gegenüber dem


geräumten Haus errichteten sie ein Zeltdorf. So konnten sie zusammenbleiben und sich gegenseitig beim Leben auf der Straße unterstützen. Gleichzeitig konnten alle sehen, wie in der Gürtelstraße 39-41 Wohnraum vernichtet wird. Fenster und sanitäre Anlagen wurden herausgerissen, Mauern zerstört.Das Hugo-Dorf, wie die Bewohner*innen ihre Zeltstadt nannten, war ein im Straßenbild sichtbares Zeichen. In Berlin wird weiter Wohnraum vernichtet, werden weiter Menschen auf die Straße geworfen. Am 14. Oktober musste auch diese Zeltstadt verschwinden. Eine weitere Genehmigung hatten die zuständigen Ämter verweigert. So wurden die Bewohner*innen zum zweiten Mal innerhalb weniger Wochen vertrieben und zerstreut. Wir sehen es auch als große Schwäche, dass es nicht gelungen ist, mehr Druck von unten aufzubauen, damit die Bewohner*innen nicht vertrieben werden. Jahrelang wurde darüber diskutiert, ob es nicht an der Zeit wäre, wieder Häuser zu besetzen. Wo blieb dann die Unterstützung für die Besetzer*innen in der Gürtelstraße? Diese Frage stellen wir auch selbstkritisch an uns. Blicken auch wir schon zu viel auf angeblich „progressive“ Senatsmehrheiten, die Berlin bezahlbar machen wollen?


Haben wir dabei vergessen, dass es ohne Widerstand von unten keine Verbesserung in unserem Sinne geben wird? Wir verstehen unsere Kundgebung gegen Wohnraumzerstörung und Vertreibung von Menschen auch als einen kleinen Beitrag, diesen Widerstand wieder sichtbar zumachen. Nicht nur in der Gürtelstraße wurden zu Beginn der kalten Jahreszeit Menschen auf die Straße gesetzt. Auch in Habersaathstraße 40-48 wurden am 13. Oktober Menschen mit einem großen Polizeiaufgebot geräumt und aufdie Straße gesetzt. Dort hatten vor 5 Jahren wohnungslose Menschen mit Unterstützer*innengruppen leerstehende Wohnungen besetzt. Sie konnten sogemeinsam mit einigen Altmieter*innen verhindern, dass der


Eigentümer die gut erhaltenden Gebäude abreißt, um Luxuswohnungen zu errichten. Genau das droht auch in der Gürtelstraße Überall werden Menschen vertrieben für das Privatinteresse von Wohnkonzernen.


Wir sind wütend, dass zu Beginn der kalten Jahreszeit erneut Wohnraum vernichtet wird und Menschen auf die Straße geworfen werden. Wir hoffen, wir sind nicht die Einzigen, die dagegen protestieren. Kommt am zur Kundgebung in die Gürtelstraße 39-41!

title: #UnisRetten! – Alarmstufe Rot: Studierende und Lehrende in Österreich protestieren gegen Kürzungen bei den Universitäten sowie den Zukunftsperspektiven
content:
„

Am Donnerstag gehen wir unter dem Motto „Alarmstufe Rot – #UnisRetten!“ gemeinsam auf die Straße – gegen die Unterfinanzierung unserer Universitäten und für ein gutes und gerechtes Studium. Denn statt der mindestens notwendigen 18 Milliarden Euro plant die Bundesregierung für 2028 bis 2030 nur rund 16 Milliarden Euro für die Universitäten ein. Zwei Milliarden Euro fehlen – mit verheerenden Folgen für den Lehrbetrieb, Betreuungs- und Beschäftigungsverhältnisse. Wir haben es satt, dass unsere Zukunft aufs Spiel gesetzt wird! Gemeinsam fordern wir eine abgesicherte und langfristige Finanzierung der öffentlichen Universitäten ein. Denn gute Lehre, Forschung und faire Arbeitsbedingungen gibt es nicht zum Nulltarif. Bis zum 31. Oktober kann die Bundesregierung das Budget noch nachbessern. Wir machen Druck und zeigen gemeinsam: Unsere Zukunft ist nicht verhandelbar!

…“

Aufruf der ÖH

„

Unter dem Motto „No Cuts! Weder durch Staat noch Rektorat!“,


sind wir heute gemeinsam mit tausenden anderen auf die Straße gegangen! Es war ein starkes Zeichen des Unterbau! Nächstes Treffen: 27.10., 16 uhr votivpark.

Post von Unterbau Uni Wien vom 22.10. auf bsky

Warum gehen Wissenschaftler*innen auf die Straße? Laut


@bundesoeh.bsky.social demonstrierten gestern 50.000 Menschen in Wien gegen Kürzungen der Universitätsbudgets. BOKU-Wissenschaftler*innen erzählen, warum sie dabei waren. #UnisRetten @n-roux.bsky.social @boku-ihg.bsky.social

“

Post von BOKU University vom 23.10. auf bsky


 mit Video


Österreich: Zehntausende bei Studentenprotesten in Wien


„

Neben der Hochschulfinanzierung ging es auch um Arbeitslosigkeit und fehlende berufliche Perspektiven


Die Studentenproteste erreichen Österreich: Unter dem Motto „Alarmstufe Rot – #UnisRetten!“ versammelten sich die Demonstranten am Nachmittag vor der Technischen Universität Wien am Karlsplatz und zogen anschließend durch die Innenstadt. Zu dem Protest hatten die Österreichische Hochschülerinnen- und Hochschülerschaft (ÖH), Universitäten und Hochschulvertretungen aufgerufen. Beteiligt waren neben Studierenden auch Lehrende, Forschende und andere Universitätsbeschäftigte.


Zur Größe der Demonstration gibt es unterschiedliche Angaben. Die ÖH bezifferte die Beteiligung auf rund 50.000 Menschen.  (…)


Ein wesentlicher Teil des Protests galt den sozialen Folgen des Sparkurses für Beschäftigte. Universitäten und Arbeitnehmervertreter befürchten den Abbau zahlreicher Stellen, wobei insbesondere junge Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler betroffen sein könnten. Auf Transparenten wurde unter anderem vor Arbeitslosigkeit und fehlenden beruflichen Perspektiven gewarnt. Auch der Gesundheitsbereich spielte eine Rolle. Universitätskliniken sind zugleich Teil der medizinischen Versorgung. An der Medizinischen Universität Wien wird vor möglichen Auswirkungen der geringeren Finanzierung auf ärztliche Stellen und den Klinikbetrieb gewarnt. Der Betriebsrat am Wiener Allgemeinen Krankenhaus erklärte vor der Demonstration, Einsparungen könnten die Zahl verfügbarer Ärzte und damit auch die Zahl möglicher Operationen reduzieren. Dabei handelt es sich um eine Warnung der Arbeitnehmervertretung, nicht um bereits beschlossene Kürzungen im Krankenhausbetrieb.


Die soziale Dimension zeigte sich zudem an der Zusammensetzung des Protests: Neben Studierenden nahmen Universitätsbeschäftigte aus Wien und anderen Bundesländern teil. Die Gewerkschaft Öffentlicher Dienst organisierte nach Angaben der APA auch die Anreise von Hochschulpersonal sowie Ärztinnen und Ärzten aus anderen Universitätsstädten. (…)


Für die Hochschulen und Studierendenvertretungen ist der Konflikt damit nicht beendet. Die ÖH fordert eine langfristig abgesicherte Finanzierung, die steigende Personal- und Betriebskosten berücksichtigt. Mit der Großdemonstration am Donnerstag verschärfte sich der seit Monaten andauernde Streit über die Frage, welchen Anteil die Universitäten am staatlichen Sparkurs tragen sollen

.“

title: Sırbistan'da 25 Ekim'deki erken genel seçim öncesi partiler son mitinglerini düzenledi
content:
Sırbistan'da 25 Ekim'deki genel seçim öncesi başbakan adayı Aleksandar Vucic ve anketlerde ön sıralarda bulunan "Öğrenci Listesi", bu akşam başkent Belgrad'da kampanya yasağı öncesi son mitinglerini yaptı.

Sırbistan'da 25 Ekim Pazar günü yapılacak seçim çerçevesinde kampanya yasağının başlamasına saatler kala Belgrad'ın farklı yerlerinde binlerce kişinin katılımıyla son seçim mitingleri yapıldı.

Cumhurbaşkanlığı görevinden istifa edip başbakan adayı olan Vucic, başkentteki bir spor salonunda düzenlenen mitingde, Sırbistan'a karşı kapsamlı bir kampanya yürütüldüğünü ve ülkeyi zayıflatmak amacıyla çok para yatırıldığını iddia etti.

Vucic, aday olduğu "Birleşmiş Sırbistan" listesinin temiz bir kampanya yürüttüğünü belirterek, seçilmesi halinde hayata geçirecekleri maddeler üzerinde çalıştıklarını söyledi.

Bu arada, Sırbistan medyası, İslam karşıtı eylem ve açıklamalarıyla tanınan ABD’li Valentina Gomez’in de Vucic'e destek vermek için Belgrad'a geldiğini ve mitinge katıldığını aktardı.

Öğrenci Listesi de son seçim mitingini başkentte yaptı

Başkent Belgrad'daki Slavija Meydanı'nda ise binlerce kişinin katılımıyla anketlerde ön sıralarda bulunan "Öğrenci Listesi" temsilcileri de miting düzenledi.

Geleneksel siyasi parti yapısından farklı olarak üniversite öğrencilerinin öncülüğünde kurulan ve seçime katılan Öğrenci Listesi'nden çeşitli isimler, farklı konular üzerinde söz aldı.

Sırbistan'ın farklı kentlerinden bugün yapılan mitinge katılmak için gelen kalabalık başkent sokaklarında yürüyüşler de düzenledi.

Sırbistan'daki erken genel seçime 18 siyasi oluşum katılıyor

Son yayımlanan anketlerde ise Vucic'in başbakan adayı olduğu "Birleşmiş Sırbistan" ve Öğrenci Listesi'nin yüzdelerinin birbirine yakın olduğu kaydedildi.

Sırbistan'da pazar günü yapılacak erken genel seçime 18 siyasi oluşumun katılacağı bilgisi paylaşıldı. Ülkede kayıtlı yaklaşık 6,5 milyon seçmen seçimde oy kullanacak.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Cecília Melo
title: Aluno da UFRN espancado em protesto envolvendo Girão: “Não tem alternativa senão a luta”
content:
Quando chegou na Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN) no fim da tarde da segunda-feira (19), Henrique Neiva não sabia que terminaria o dia em um exame de corpo e delito, com hematomas pelo corpo e um dente fraturado. O estudante de 28 anos fez parte do grupo que tentou resistir ao avanço de um protesto organizado pelo perfil “Endireita RN” no grupo de WhatsApp “UFRN Anti Lula”, administrado pelo secretário do gabinete do deputado federal

General Girão

 (PL-RN), Allison Lobato. O parlamentar Girão esteve envolvido na ação junto à vereadora de Natal recentemente eleita deputada estadual Camila Araújo (PL-RN).


“Era pra ter quebrado mais uns três”, dizia uma mensagem no grupo, após o fim do protesto. “Apanhou pouco”, completava outro integrante, após as notícias de

agressões

 começarem a se popularizar na Grande Natal. A

Agência Pública

 teve acesso a mensagens trocadas no grupo administrado pelo secretário de gabinete do deputado da extrema direita. O caso foi registrado na 1ª Delegacia de Plantão da Polícia Civil.


A noite que não terminou


Henrique Neiva ainda estava em casa quando começou a ouvir um paredão automotivo reproduzindo: “Um caminho novo pra gente seguir. Agora é Flávio presidente”, parte da letra de um dos jingles do candidato à presidência pelo PL. Por volta das 17h, o universitário chegou à unidade de ensino, onde foi avisado que as aulas estavam sendo interrompidas e os estudantes, liberados, devido à aglomeração que se formava em frente à UFRN.


“Quando eu cheguei, já estava tendo violência, né? Eles já estavam xingando e instigando as pessoas a irem pra cima”, conta o estudante que disse ter acompanhado quando as ofensas passaram de verbais à físicas. “O que a gente tava fazendo era uma corrente humana, dizendo que daquele lado eles não passavam”, disse o estudante.


“Recua, fascista, recua”, gritavam alunos, como pode ser visto em vídeos divulgados nas redes sociais. Em outros registros, o deputado General Girão (PL), cercado por seguranças privados, aparece dizendo: “Avança, avança. Esse ambiente é meu também” e “muitos de vocês ficam na vadiagem vendendo drogas aqui dentro”, acusava.


Henrique conta que o portão do campus estava sendo fechado quando as agressões tiveram início. “Fui segurar o portão. E aí do outro lado a galera estava gritando, xingando e chamando para a violência. Quando eu saio com o meu celular para gravar quem é que estava fazendo isso eu levo um chute na perna. É nesse momento que eu vou atrás de quem me chutou e quando eu vou para cima sou agredido”, narrou o estudante que recebeu chutes e pontapés ao cair no chão, momento registrado em vídeos por colegas.


Após ser submetido por um exame de corpo de delito, Neiva foi para casa, mas não conseguiu dormir direito. “Eu estava sentindo dores e fiquei com uma angústia muito grande do que tinha acontecido, que eu tinha ido pra lá para ser agredido. Fiquei pensando que não vale de nada, né? Nada vai tirar as agressões que eu sofri”, conta. “É necessário ter responsabilização para que isso não volte a acontecer”, opina.


Estou me recuperando física e mentalmente, também temendo pela segurança, mas não tenho deixado esse medo me paralisar. Mesmo eu recebendo esses comentários de ódio nas minhas redes sociais, eu continuo seguindo a minha vida. […] Não acho que é o momento de parar. Eu acho que é na verdade um momento de intensificar, de a gente ocupar mais as ruas, de a gente disputar a consciência das pessoas, de a gente mostrar que não tem outra alternativa senão a luta política”


Henrique Neiva


estudante universitário.


Os lados da moeda


Em sua curta jornada política, Henrique Neiva já vivenciou lados opostos do espectro político e disse ter votado em Jair Bolsonaro em 2018, motivado pelo sentimento antipetista. Foi com a efervescência política de junho de 2013 que Neiva começou a se interessar por política. O jovem contou que começou a buscar na internet informações sobre o cenário político brasileiro, e foi quando teve contato com o pensamento liberal. Foi no MBL que Henrique começou sua trajetória na militância, e chegou a se candidatar a vereador de Natal pelo Novo, mas diz que o sentimento mudou durante o mandato de Bolsonaro.


“Eu vi que não era um governo que tava sendo feito para governar para todas as pessoas, era um governo feito de atacar as instituições públicas e aí essa desesperança começa e se amplifica em 2020”, avalia o jovem, que disse ter sentido na pandemia o divisor de …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "A Spark from the Cockroaches": Arundhati Roy on India's Youth Protests & Modi's Crackdown
content:
A court in India on Wednesday ordered the release of two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, the youth-led movement that has led historic waves of protests in India since the summer. Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained amid massive protests last week after they scaled a barricade to enter a site popular for protest, unfurled the national flag and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar oversaw the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls in India since June of last year. Opposition parties say those impacted are primarily Muslims and other minorities less likely to support the

BJP

, the Hindu nationalist ruling party of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.


“You have a deep and wide — an ideologically wide — historical culture of resistance in India,” says acclaimed writer and activist Arundhati Roy. At the same time, the Modi government “has three things in its playbook: One is false-flag attacks, two is engineering communal riots, and the third is massive repression. And I don’t think we’ve seen its hand yet.”

author: Julius Gavroche
title: The Student Revolt in France Spreads
content:
from the

CrimethInc.

collective, 21/10/2026


Moving Forward with Rage and Solidarity


October 17 marked one of the fiercest days of mass protest in recent French history. Scenes of ferocious resistance unfolded throughout the day, not only in Paris but in

Bordeaux

,

Dijon

,

Marseille

,

Nancy

, and dozens of other cities across the country. Some observers have described the day’s events as

more explosive

 than the

Yellow Vest movement

 of 2018-19—and the rebellion shows no sign of slowing.


How did we get here? Courageous high school students

have been protesting for weeks

 against abominable conditions in schools, the rise of the extreme right, and the bleak prospects they face in a world dominated by technocrats and tech barons. Alongside growing anti-government protests from

Albania

,

Italy

,

Spain

, and beyond in recent days, the French student rebellions may herald the emergence of a new wave of global struggle.


In this article, our correspondent from Paris explains the context behind the youth rebellion, tracks the movement’s growth over the two weeks leading up to October 17 and the government’s failed attempts to repress or to pacify it, and clarifies the stakes moving forward.


Stay tuned for a full report on the uprising of October 17 and the ongoing rebellions across France and beyond.


Thousands gather to protest police violence and support the students in revolt (Nantes, October 6, 2026)


This update on the student unrest in France picks up where we ended

our previous report

, on the eve of the national call to take the streets on October 6, 2026.


The stakes were high on this crucial day of action. It was critical to show massive solidarity with the high school students fighting like hell against the empty future looming on their horizon. The day presented an ideal opportunity to expand the scope of the current movement by joining forces to resist the authoritarian state power that has been growing stronger every day.


The following article provides further context and analysis to understand the current situation in France, along with reports on what went down in the streets over these last rebellious weeks.


Background: The

Banlieues

 and the Enemy Within


When governments or powerful institutions feel threatened, they often strive to reaffirm their authority by inventing scapegoats to hold responsible for all supposed misfortunes. By invoking the menace of an “enemy within,” politicians can shift blame for systemic problems that have resulted from their own actions onto a specific category of individuals. In France, the most common targets are the residents of the

banlieues

, the impoverished suburbs on the outskirts of Paris and other cities.


At the beginning of the student blockades, the movement remained limited to a handful of high schools in these Parisian suburbs. In response, President Emmanuel Macron and his ministers decided to react quickly and do everything in their power to silence this emerging wave of youth protest. Due to the location of the first blockades, authorities believed that they could act more freely and repress the unrest with impunity, since these specific territories have been targeted for generations by all government administrations across political lines.


The condition of the

banlieues

, which remain populated by descendants of the French Empire’s colonized subjects, reflects France’s ongoing role as a

neocolonial power

 that continues to exploit African territories. Consider the disastrous

oil project

 in Uganda orchestrated by the France-based multinational company TotalEnergies, or the

corruption case

 involving the French far-right business tycoon Vincent Bolloré and his bribery and money laundering schemes across West African ports.


French governments and corporations have no scruples about extracting enormous wealth from African countries. This neocolonial pillaging fuels France’s position as the

seventh richest country

 in the world today, according to the IMF. Yet despite these astronomical profits, the nation refuses to address the problems facing its post-colonial population and their descendants within its national territory.


At the twilight of France’s colonial empire, decades of occupation and racist violence had created political and economic instability across northern and western Africa. As a result, waves of migrants began leaving their countries to come to France for work in the 1950s. Upon …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Albania Protests Escalate Over Corruption, Planned Kushner/Trump Luxury Resort
content:
Student-led anti-corruption and cost-of-living protests call for the prime minister’s resignation, among other demands.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Student-led anti-corruption and cost-of-living protests in Albania are calling for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, among other demands. Hundreds of injuries and arrests have been reported amid a violent police crackdown, along with widespread damage to public and private property. The student demands are an outgrowth of the “Flamingo Revolution,” which erupted earlier this year in opposition to a luxury resort being developed on the ecologically sensitive Sazan Island. The planned resort is backed by Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump, President Trump’s son-in-law and daughter, and has been fast-tracked by the Rama government.

“Students find no future in Albania,” says Bora Mema, a founding member of the left-wing political party Lëvizja Bashkë, about the motivations behind the burgeoning pro-democracy movement. “Many of us have to migrate because the only development model that the government proposes is to clean the toilets of the rich and the mafia in luxurious resorts, like the one that Trump and Kushner and the national oligarchs and mafia in Albania are constructing.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: In Albania, student-led anti-government protests have rocked the capital Tirana for more than a week, as thousands have taken to the streets to call for the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama. Last week, the Albanian Student Union called for strikes and demonstrations at the Ministry of Education to protest high tuition costs, poor university conditions, a lack of jobs, and corruption. At least half a million young Albanians have left the country over the last decade in search of better economic opportunities.

Initial protests have escalated into ongoing clashes with police, leading to hundreds of injuries and arrests, widespread damage to government buildings, street lights and private property. Riot police have deployed tear gas, water cannons, sound grenades and rubber bullets against the protesters. These are some of those protesters in their own words.

LULJETA KOLA: [translated] What does Albania want? It wants a revolution, a change, a complete overthrow of the system, because it can’t go on like this, because these people have become billionaires, superbillionaires, and there are very poor people here.

ULIKS SKENDERAJ: The economy, like education, healthcare, everything, has gone downhill since many years. Yeah, basically. But all of the — all of the politicians from both parties, the main parties, should be gone, basically. This is what the new generation wants.

NDERIME VLADI: For us to stop the protests, first of all, Edi Rama should resign, immediately. Like, at the second that he resigns, his whole Cabinet should resign. … They deserve prison for every corruption that they have done. They have done so many. I mean, I cannot begin to, like, count with my fingers what they have done with this country. The corruption is on levels unseen, unseen in any other state of the world.

ANJALI KAMAT: Albania’s protests first began in May, when environmentalists rallied against a luxury resort development on the ecologically sensitive Sazan Island. The project is backed by President Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and has been fast-tracked by the Albanian government. Protests against the development grew into what is known as the Flamingo movement, which has rallied against government corruption for months and has now been joined by students in this latest wave of unrest.

On Sunday, Prime Minister Edi Rama set up chairs outside Parliament in a symbolic gesture for dialogue. Protesters calling for his resignation later smashed the chairs. Rama is leader of the Socialist Party and has a majority in Parliament. He’s been in power for 13 years and has so far refused to resign. The next elections are scheduled for 2029. During a live stream on Sunday, Rama said protests could hurt Albania’s bid to join the European Union by 2030, and claimed protesters were linked to antifa.

title: Öcalan’s book ‘Manifesto of the Democratic Communal Society’ banned in prison
content:
The administration of Siverek No. 1 T-Type Closed Prison in Urfa has prohibited political prisoner Tacittin Kalgı from receiving the book

Manifesto of the Democratic Communal Society

. The decision was justified on the grounds that the book allegedly contains material posing a threat to security. DEM Party MP Newroz Uysal Aslan has therefore appealed to the Human Rights Commission of the Turkish Parliament, calling for an investigation into the ban.


The measure is based on a decision issued by the prison administration on October 8, under file number 2026/390. The decision specifically objects to passages addressing the historical and political dimensions of the Kurdish question, Abdullah Öcalan’s ideas, the history of the Kurdish movement, and the paradigm of a democratic society.


The prison’s Education Board maintains that the book damages the reputation of the state, contains terrorist propaganda, and could incite hatred and hostility.


Even Öcalan’s call for peace is deemed objectionable


In her petition, Uysal Aslan pointed out that even passages concerning Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and Democratic Society were deemed objectionable. The book addresses, among other issues, the transition from armed struggle to democratic politics and perspectives on coexistence within society.


“Banning this content on the basis of a security-oriented assessment contradicts the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process,” Uysal stated.


The MP also emphasized that expressing dissenting political views and criticizing state policies do not, in themselves, constitute sufficient grounds for banning a publication. Furthermore, she said, the prison administration had failed to adequately explain what specific threat the book allegedly posed to the security and order of the prison.


Similar bans in other prisons


Uysal Aslan cited Articles 25 and 26 of the Turkish Constitution, which guarantee freedom of thought and expression, as well as Article 62 of Law No. 5275 on the Execution of Sentences and Security Measures, which regulates prisoners’ access to publications. She also referred to a ruling by the Turkish Constitutional Court that found the denial of access to publications for prisoners to constitute a violation of their rights.


The case in Siverek does not appear to be an isolated incident. Political prisoner Ihsan Kartal, held in Tekirdağ No. 1 F-Type Prison, was also denied access to the same book. Uysal Aslan further called for an investigation into restrictions on access to similar publications affecting Metin Yamalak, who is imprisoned in Bolu F-Type Prison.


The MP urged the parliamentary Human Rights Commission to review the prison administration’s decision, request information from the Ministry of Justice, and initiate measures to protect prisoners’ right to access publications. She also called for an investigation into similar bans in other prisons.

author: Unknown
title: Incendiato il Presidio di Borgone
content:
Questa notte hanno dato fuoco al presidio di Borgone. E la prima cosa che sentiamo è la rabbia.


Da Notav Info


Rabbia per un luogo che fa parte della nostra storia, per uno spazio costruito e vissuto in anni di lotta, per tutto quello che un presidio rappresenta per il Movimento No Tav. Perché questo presidio non è soltanto una struttura, qualche tavolo, delle sedie e un tetto sotto cui ripararsi. È un luogo che abbiamo fatto vivere con la nostra presenza, con le iniziative, le assemblee e le serate trascorse insieme.


Il presidio di Borgone è nato nel 2005. Da allora sono passati più di vent’anni. Generazioni diverse hanno attraversato questo luogo, portandoci pezzi della propria vita e contribuendo a costruire una storia collettiva che non si misura in muri e strutture, ma nelle relazioni che abbiamo saputo creare e nella determinazione con cui continuiamo a difendere la nostra terra.


Ma c’è un elemento che rende questa vicenda ancora più grave: il presidio sorgeva su terreni che devono essere espropriati. Un luogo che, proprio per la sua storia e per quello che rappresenta, si è trovato al centro di interessi e conflitti ben precisi. Per tutto ciò non abbiamo intenzione di far passare quanto accaduto come un “semplice”incendio.


Questi sono modi di fare mafiosi: colpire, distruggere, pensare di risolvere con il fuoco ciò che non si riesce ad affrontare apertamente. È un metodo che conosciamo e che rifiutiamo, tanto più quando viene preso di mira uno spazio collettivo costruito in anni di impegno e partecipazione.


Vedere un luogo così finire in fiamme fa male. E non abbiamo intenzione di nasconderlo dietro parole di circostanza.


Ma sappiamo anche cosa significa appartenere a questo movimento. Sappiamo che i nostri luoghi vivono perché ci siamo noi, perché siamo capaci di prendercene cura, di ricostruire, di ritrovarci e ripartire.


Non è la prima volta che ci troviamo davanti alla distruzione di uno spazio che abbiamo costruito insieme. E ogni volta, quello che conta è la volontà di non lasciare che siano le fiamme a scrivere l’ultima parola.


Il presidio di Borgone è parte della nostra storia. Non lasceremo che questa storia finisca tra le ceneri.


Oggi c’è rabbia, c’è amarezza, ma c’è anche la consapevolezza di quello che siamo e di tutto quello che abbiamo costruito in questi anni.


I nostri luoghi non sono soltanto luoghi: sono il modo concreto in cui una comunità si incontra, si organizza e continua a lottare.


Ci ritroveremo anche a Borgone. Perché quel luogo è parte della nostra storia e di una lotta che, da oltre vent’anni, continua a vivere nelle persone che la portano avanti.

Voilà les quelques infos utiles qu'on donnerait pour soutenir des proches de personnes arrêtées au tribunal et continuer les actions anti-répression suite au mouvement en cours :


•

Écouter, être là, être présent·e

 (les moments au tribunal peuvent être des moments intenses où les gens sont très émus et dans le désarroi).


•

Demander les infos que les proches ont en leur connaissance

 : contexte de l'arrestation, est-ce que la personne a eu un·e avocat·e commis d'office ou une avocat·e désigné·e en GAV, le commissariat où s'est passé la GAV, comment les proches ont été mis au courant de l'arrestation, les liens et les contacts qu'il y a eu avec l'avocat jusqu'ici, quels sont les tarifs de l'avocat (Aide juridictionnelle ou non), etc.


• Une fois la discussion enclenchée avec les proches, si ce n'est pas déjà fait essayer de leur faire

réunir les garanties de représentation

 de la personne arrêtée qui va passer en comparution immédiate : photocopie de pièce d'identité, tout document attestant d'une activité professionnelle (salariée ou non), d'une formation, attestation de France travail et/ou RSA, attestation de paiement de la CAF, photocopie de bail locatif, photocopie de carte vitale/droits à la Sécu et/ou Complémentaire santé solidaire, etc.


 Option 1 : ces garanties peuvent être imprimées et amenées en version papier au tribunal, pour ensuite les transmettre à l'avocat qui défendra la personne en audience.

 Option 2 : ou alors elles peuvent être envoyées directement à l'avocat par mail, qui se chargera de les imprimer.

 Dans le doute, privilégier l'option 1.


• Dans le tribunal et aux abords,

essayer de repérer les avocat·es, d'aller leur parler et de voir quel·les avocat·es ont pris quels dossiers.


 Si le rôle (programme des audiences de la journée) est affiché dans le tribunal, c'est parfois possible d'y voir le nom de l'avocat·e qui défend le dossier.

 Les avocat·es circulent dans le tribunal, aux abords des salles d'audience ou alors dans la salle d'audience même : c'est possible de leur demander à la volée qui ils sont et qui ils défendent.


• Une fois un·e avocat·e capté·e et vu avec lui/elle les dossiers qu'ielle défend,

checker avec l'avocat·e sa stratégie de défense

, et voir si ça vous semble tenir la route. Le conseil de refuser la comparution immédiate est très très souvent un bon conseil, mais au vu de ce qu'il se passe en période de mouvement et de répression intenses, ce conseil est peut-être à moduler, car le risque de détention provisoire en attente de la comparution est assez élévé, il faut voir au cas par cas selon les dossiers et selon le rendu des premières audiences.


• Lors de l'audience :

la personne arrêtée (en décision avec son avocat·e) va alors accepter ou refuser la comparution immédiate.


 Si elle accepte la CI (comparution immédiate) : le jugement a lieu sur le fond et les peines sont souvent lourdes. Amendes et prison ferme (avec départ immédiat en détention) sont très fréquents.

 Si elle refuse la CI : les juges examinent alors le statut de la personne jusqu'à son jugement, qui est souvent fixé à une date comprise entre 3 et 8 semaines plus tard.


• Si la comparution immédiate est refusée par la personne arrêtée, elle aura

soit un contrôle judiciaire en attente de son jugement

 (pointages au commissariat, interdiction de présence dans certains arrondissements ou dans certaines …

author: A Melanie Lübbert
title: Baden-Württemberg: Kettensäge gegen Datenschutz
content:
Bild: Michael Fenton Unsplash-Lizenz; Bearbeitung: Digitalcourage

Wer in Baden-Württemberg wissen will, ob ein Unternehmen oder eine Behörde rechtmäßig mit personenbezogenen Daten umgeht, kann sich an den Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit, Tobias Keber, wenden. Doch ausgerechnet seine Behörde soll massiv Personal verlieren.

Der Entwurf des Staatshaushaltsgesetzes 2027 sieht vor, bis zum Ende der Legislaturperiode (2029) 40 Prozent der Stellen abzubauen. Von derzeit 67,5 Stellen sollen 27 wegfallen. Übrig blieben gerade einmal 42 Planstellen. Für 2027 sind zunächst 5,5 Stellen zur Streichung vorgesehen; weitere Kürzungen sollen 2028 und 2029 folgen.

Eine inhaltliche Begründung für diesen drastischen Einschnitt liefert die grün-schwarze Landesregierung unter Ministerpräsident Cem Özdemir nicht. Auffällig ist zudem: Während für die übrige zentrale Verwaltung fünf Prozent Stellenabbau vorgesehen sind, soll die Datenschutzaufsicht 40 Prozent einsparen – eine achtmal so hohe Kürzungsquote.

Der geplante Kahlschlag steht in krassem Widerspruch zur Entwicklung der vergangenen Jahre. Seit die Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DSGVO) 2018 wirksam wurde, hat sich die Arbeitsbelastung der Datenschutzaufsicht erheblich erhöht. Die Zahl der Beschwerden und gemeldeten Datenpannen ist massiv gestiegen. Zugleich werden Datenverarbeitungen immer komplexer und stellen die Behörde vor neue Herausforderungen.

Quelle: Tätigkeitsberichte des Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg. Auswertung: Redaktion Digitalcourage. [Grafik: padeluun, mit Hilfe von KI erstellt]

Die Zahlen verdeutlichen, wie stark sich die Aufgaben der Behörde verändert haben:

Beschwerden: Seit Einführung der DSGVO wenden sich deutlich mehr Menschen an die Datenschutzaufsicht. Neue Technologien und der zunehmende Einsatz Künstlicher Intelligenz schaffen zusätzliche Konfliktfelder. Im Jahr 2025 erreichte die Zahl der Beschwerden mit 7.673 einen neuen Höchststand – ein Anstieg um rund 90 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahr.

Datenpannen: Mit der DSGVO wurden die Meldepflichten bei Verletzungen des Schutzes personenbezogener Daten erheblich ausgeweitet. Für die Aufsichtsbehörde entstand dadurch ein umfangreiches zusätzliches Aufgabenfeld. Die Zahl der Meldungen stieg deutlich an und erreichte 2025 mit 4.059 einen neuen Höchstwert.

Beratungen: Die Einführung der DSGVO löste zunächst einen enormen Beratungsbedarf aus. Durch standardisierte Leitfäden, Orientierungshilfen und Online-Angebote der Datenschutzkonferenz sowie eigene Praxishilfen und Veranstaltungen konnte die Behörde viele wiederkehrende Fragen beantworten. Auch das Bildungszentrum des Landesbeauftragten übernimmt einen wichtigen Teil der Beratung. Inzwischen entstehen neue Aufgaben, insbesondere durch Künstliche Intelligenz und europäische Regelungen wie den Europäischen Gesundheitsdatenraum. Unternehmen, Behörden und Bürger.innen sind weiterhin auf die fachliche Unterstützung der Datenschutzaufsicht angewiesen.

Kontrollen: Die anlassunabhängigen Vor-Ort-Prüfungen wurden nach 2018 aufgrund begrenzter personeller Kapazitäten deutlich reduziert. Während der Corona-Pandemie waren zusätzliche Einschränkungen notwendig. Nach 2022 konnten die Kontrollen mit einer besseren Personalausstattung wieder intensiviert werden. Die geplanten Kürzungen drohen diese Entwicklung umzukehren.

Personalstellen: Seit Einführung der DSGVO verdoppelte der Landtag die Zahl der Personalstellen bis 2025 schrittweise auf den Höchststand von 67,5 Stellen. Zwischenzeitlich waren es mit befristet zugewiesenen Personalstellen 70,5 Stellen. Bis 2029 ist nun eine Reduzierung um rund 40 Prozent vorgesehen. Am Ende sollen nur noch 42 Planstellen verbleiben, während andere Landesbehörden fünf Prozent einsparen sollen.

Hinweis: In der linken primären Y-Achse finden sich aufsummiert die Ereignisse „Beschwerden, Datenpannen, Beratungen und Kontrollen“; in der rechten sekundären Y-Achse finden sich die Werte für Kontrollen und LfDI-Personalstellen.

Quelle: Tätigkeitsberichte des Landesbeauftragten für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg. Auswertung: Redaktion Digitalcourage. [Grafik: padeluun, mit Hilfe von KI erstellt]

Dabei benötigt die Behörde nicht weniger, sondern mehr Personal. Landesdatenschutzbeauftragter Tobias Keber hat dem Landtag in seiner Stellungnahme zum Haushaltsentwurf dargelegt, dass für eine ordnungsgemäße Aufgabenerfüllung …

author: Τάσος Θεοφίλου
title: Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα


Ο Elton Kalica, διδάκτορας στο Πανεπιστήμιο της Πάδοβα, με προσωπική εμπειρία πολύχρονης κράτησης στις ιταλικές φυλακές, είναι μεταξύ άλλων και ιδρυτής της «Ιταλικής Εγκληματολογίας των Κρατουμένων». Ανάμεσα στα ερευνητικά του πεδία είναι η Κριτική Εγκληματολογία, η Εθνογραφία των Φυλακών, η Εγκληματολογία των Κρατουμένων και ο Καταργητισμός. Από το 2002, είναι μέλος της συντακτικής επιτροπής του περιοδικού

Ristretti Orizzonti

.


Στο πλαίσιο της πλούσιας αρθρογραφίας του υπάρχει

και ένα άρθρο με τίτλο «Υπερπληθυσμός στις φυλακές: παρακαλώ, σταματήστε να μιλάτε για τετραγωνικά μέτρα»

 το οποίο αναφέρεται την κατάσταση των φυλακών στην γειτονική Ιταλία το όχι και τόσο μακρινό 2011. Καθώς είναι επίκαιρο λόγω της διαχρονικότητας του, τα κύρια σημεία του μπορούν τεθούν και στον δημόσιο λόγο για τις ελληνικές φυλακές.


Ο υπερπληθυσμός δεν είναι ένας απλός μαθηματικός υπολογισμός


Το κύριο επιχείρημα του Έλτον Καλίκα είναι, ότι η αναγωγή του προβλήματος του υπερπληθυσμού σε έναν απλό μαθηματικό υπολογισμό της ελάχιστης διαθέσιμης επιφάνειας για κάθε κρατούμενο θα μπορούσε να καταλήξει σε μια άκαρπη διακήρυξη δικαιωμάτων, αντί για μια πρακτική προσπάθεια εξεύρεσης κατάλληλων μέτρων για τη μείωση του κινδύνου υποτροπής.


Ως αφορμή για την ανάπτυξη του επιχειρήματος του, ο Καλίκα παίρνει τον θάνατο ενός κρατουμένου, ο οποίος πέθανε αφού προσπάθησε μάταια να πείσει τον γιατρό ότι είχε συμπτώματα καρδιακής προσβολής, η οποία τελικά τον σκότωσε στον ύπνο του.


«Όταν μιλάμε για υπερπληθυσμό, συζητάμε για τη σχέση μεταξύ του αριθμού των κρατουμένων και της επιφάνειας του κελιού που καταλαμβάνουν, ενώ αυτή η οπτική του υπερπληθυσμού κινδυνεύει να δώσει μια λανθασμένη εικόνα για το τι αποτελεί την πραγματική καταστροφή των σημερινών φυλακών. Ειδικά όταν μιλάμε για θανάτους…»


Ο κρατούμενος που πέθανε εκείνες τις ημέρες δεν ήταν θύμα της ελάχιστης επιφάνειας του κελιού που αναλογεί σε κάθε άτομο. Το ζήτημα είναι πιο περίπλοκο καθώς «το πραγματικό πρόβλημα δεν είναι τα τετραγωνικά μέτρα του κελιού που μειώνονται, αλλά το καθεστώς διαβίωσης που κρατά τους ανθρώπους ξαπλωμένους στα ράντζα τους για περισσότερες από είκοσι ώρες την ημέρα, η μονοτονία της καθημερινότητας που αποβλακώνει τους ανθρώπους και η έλλειψη δραστηριοτήτων».


Κάτι που επισημαίνει ο Καλικά στο άρθρο του είναι ότι η αύξηση του αριθμού των κρατουμένων ακολουθούν, κάθε χρόνο, επαναλαμβανόμενες περικοπές στα κονδύλια που προορίζονται για τις φυλακές. Και δεν ήταν δύσκολο να διαπιστώσει κανείς τις επιπτώσεις αυτού του δραματικού συνδυασμού σε θέματα υγιεινής, διατροφής, καθημερινής διαβίωσης, εκπαίδευσης και προγραμμάτων απεξάρτησης και κοινωνικής επανένταξης…


«Το πραγματικό πρόβλημα της φυλακής είναι τα άτομα με λιγότερα εφόδια, εκείνα που μένουν ξαπλωμένα στα κρεβάτια τους, συχνά γεμάτα ψυχοφάρμακα, απογοητευμένα να περιμένουν το χρόνο να περάσει, σε πραγματικά επισφαλείς σωματικές και ψυχικές συνθήκες. Και η φυλακή κάνει πραγματικά ελάχιστα γι’ αυτό, καθώς δεν υπάρχει κανείς που να αναζητά αυτούς τους ανθρώπους, να τους παρακολουθεί και να τους παρακινεί να βγουν από το κελί τους και να κάνουν κάτι χρήσιμο. Ως εκ τούτου, δημιουργείται σχεδόν φυσιολογικά ένας διαχωρισμός μεταξύ των λίγων που κάνουν πολλά -εργασία, σχολείο, μαθήματα- και των πολλών που δεν κάνουν τίποτα. Αυτό είναι και το πρόβλημα του υπερπληθυσμού».


Λίγα μέτρα από τις φυλακές της Πάδοβας στις οποίες αναφέρεται ο Καλίκα βρίσκεται το προανακριτικό κέντρο, όπου κρατούνται τα άτομα που περιμένουν τη δίκη τους. (Καθώς στη Ελλάδα δεν υπάρχει τέτοια διάκριση μπορούμε να φανταστούμε ότι πρόκειται για έναν τύπο φυλακής μεταξύ των φυλακών Κορυδαλλού και του Τμήματος Μεταγωγών).


Σύμφωνα με την μαρτυρία ενός συμπατριώτη του Καλικά, «οι μέρες περνούσαν ανάμεσα σε μακρές αναμονές για να πάμε στο ντους και αμήχανες σειρές για να μπορέσεις να χρησιμοποιήσεις το μπάνιο. Μέσα σε όλη αυτή την κίνηση ανθρώπων, μέσα σε εκείνο το ποτάμι αγωνίας, δεν υπήρχε χρόνος να σκεφτείς τίποτα. Δεν μπορούσες να επιτρέψεις στον εαυτό σου αδυναμίες και περισπασμούς, έπρεπε να είσαι δυνατός, ακόμα και όταν ένιωθες αδύναμος, έπρεπε να επιβιώσεις.


»Οι μήνες περνούσαν και κάθε μέρα έβλεπα ανθρώπους να τσακώνονται για το ντους, για τη σειρά στο μπάνιο, για το φαγητό, για το τηλεχειριστήριο ή για πολλά άλλα πράγματα που μπορεί να φαίνονται παράλογα σε πολλούς έξω από εκεί. Ήταν μια συνεχής σύγκρουση διαφορετικών …

author: Perseus
title: Αυτό το ζωντανό τίποτα που πετά στα τυφλά δακρυγόνο στο μετρό στην Ομόνοια ενσαρκώνει τη φράση του Χρυσοχοΐδη (Βίντεο)
content:
Αυτό το ζωντανό τίποτα που πετά στα τυφλά δακρυγόνο στο μετρό στην Ομόνοια ενσαρκώνει τη φράση του Χρυσοχοΐδη (Βίντεο)


Με βίαιη καταστολή ολοκληρώθηκε το πανεκπαιδευτικό συλλαλητήριο την Τετάρτη 21 Οκτώβρη 2026 στην Αθήνα, με τις αστυνομικές δυνάμεις καταστολής να εξαπολύουν επιθέσεις με χρήση χημικών και χειροβομβίδων κρότου-λάμψης κατά των διαδηλωτών.


Μάλιστα στα πλάνα που αναρτήθηκαν στο instagram από τον χρήστη pi_kappaa, αστυνομικός των ΜΑΤ πετά στα τυφλά δακρυγόνο μέσα στην είσοδο του σταθμού του μετρό στην Ομόνοια, εν ώρα λειτουργίας, με προφανή σκοπό να τραυματίσει όποιον ή όποια εισερχόταν ή εξερχόταν του σταθμού εκείνη τη στιγμή.


Σε μια επίδειξη προκλητικής αδιαφορίας, ο αστυνομικός εμφανίζεται στη συνέχεια να προβαίνει σε έναν ειρωνικό χαιρετισμό, περήφανος για την εγκληματική του πράξη μπροστά στις κάμερες των φωτορεπόρτερ και των δημοσιογράφων.


Το γεγονός ότι ο αστυνομικός ένιωσε ασφαλής να επιτεθεί έτσι, εν γνώσει του ότι καταγράφεται, αποκαλύπτει και κάτι χειρότερο: ότι δε φοβάται. Δε φοβάται οποιαδήποτε τιμωρία, αλλά υποδηλώνει μια βαθύτερη πεποίθηση ότι μπορεί να ενεργήσει, χωρίς συνέπειες. Αυτή η αίσθηση της ασυλίας είναι το πιο επικίνδυνο στοιχείο της συμπεριφοράς του, γιατί γνωρίζει πως το σύστημα σπάνια αγγίζει τους «δικούς του». Ίσα, ίσα κιόλας που κάθε τρεις και λίγο τον ανταμείβει με νέα επιδόματα. Αυτή η αίσθηση ατιμωρησίας και επιβράβευσης της

βίας

 αποτελεί το υπόβαθρο για την κλιμάκωση της αστυνομικής αγριότητας. Το συγκεκριμένο παράδειγμα ενός ακόμα περιστατικού αστυνομικής βίας, δεν είναι επιβολή της τάξης, αλλά εγκληματική βία στην πιο ξεκάθαρη μορφή της.


 


Το άλλο κρίσιμο ερώτημα όπως και κάθε φορά είναι: αφού δεν είναι όλοι οι αστυνομικοί ίδιοι, τι έκαναν οι συνάδελφοι του όταν είδαν να συμβαίνει αυτό;


 


Και τέλος, το πραγματικό ερώτημα, δεν είναι «ποιος και αν θα τιμωρηθεί», αλλά εμείς τι ανεχόμαστε. Γιατί όσο μένουμε σιωπηλοί, όσο μένουμε σιωπηλές, όσο το βίντεο παίζει για λίγα λεπτά στα social media κι έπειτα χάνεται μέσα στη ροή των ειδήσεων, τόσο θα βαθαίνει το ρήγμα στην αξιοπρέπεια μιας κοινωνίας που έχει πάψει να εξοργίζεται με αυτά που βλέπει, με αυτά που ζει, με την πραγματική απεικόνιση της φράσης Χρυσοχοϊδή “περνούν οι αστυνομικοί και ο κόσμος τους χειροκροτεί”.
