title: Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığı'ndan kritik güvenlik uyarısı
content:
Siber Güvenlik Başkanlığı, dünya genelinde yaygın olarak kullanılan PHP yazılım altyapısında kritik güvenlik açıkları tespit edildiğini belirterek şu açıklamayı yaptı “Dünya genelinde yaygın olarak kullanılan PHP yazılım altyapısında kritik güvenlik açıkları tespit edilmiştir.

Başkanlığımız, söz konusu zafiyetlerin oluşturabileceği risklerin erken tespiti ve olası etkilerinin sınırlandırılması amacıyla ulusal ölçekte güvenlik taramalarını başlatmış, ilgili kurum ve kuruluşlara acil güvenlik bildirimlerini iletmiştir.

Kamu kurumlarımızın, kritik altyapı işletmecilerimizin ve özel sektör kuruluşlarımızın sistemlerini gözden geçirerek gerekli güvenlik güncellemelerini ivedilikle uygulamaları önem taşımaktadır.

Dijital altyapılarımızın güvenliği ve kritik hizmetlerin sürekliliği için ulusal düzeyde koordinasyon ve önleyici güvenlik çalışmalarımız sürmektedir.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Blanca Missé
title: As More Unions Oppose ICE and Israel, the Right Is Cracking Down
content:
The right is trying to gain access to labor unions’ minutes, membership lists, and Zoom chats.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On September 22, The Free Press attacked the California Faculty Association (CFA), which represents about 29,000 faculty, librarians, counselors, and coaches across the California State University (CSU) system. Drawing on private discussions about a proposed Jewish caucus, including communications from a union Zoom meeting, the article accused CFA of antisemitism. How those communications reached the publication remains unclear. Two days later, the Jewish Journal amplified those allegations, urging Gov. Gavin Newsom to consider them as he weighed California Assembly Bill (AB) 2551, CFA-sponsored legislation challenging campus protest restrictions imposed after the 2024 Palestine solidarity encampments. Less than a week after The Free Press story was published, Newsom vetoed the bill.

Pro-Israel and Jewish advocacy organizations had already campaigned against AB 2551 before the union’s internal deliberations were targeted, arguing that greater scrutiny would weaken rules needed to protect Jewish students from harassment and intimidation. Newsom’s veto does not prove coordination, but the campaign portraying CFA as hostile to Jewish students had become entangled with the union’s fight against campus protest restrictions.

The CSU’s systemwide policy prohibits encampments, overnight demonstrations, and unauthorized structures. The CSU Academic Senate immediately condemned the restrictions as undermining academic freedom when it was instituted in 2024, while CFA warned that vague definitions of disruption threatened constitutionally protected speech, assembly, protest, and future strike activity. A major 2026 ACLU-Amnesty study, investigating 80 campuses over two years, documented sweeping repression of Palestine solidarity protests. As the report found, universities “have imposed sweeping restrictions on student speech, initiated disciplinary actions against students, and imposed severe punishments, including expulsions and suspensions.” The ACLU has insisted that even legitimate time, place, and manner restrictions “must leave ample room for students to express themselves.”

The controversy reaches beyond CFA and CSU. Unions and rank-and-file organizations committed to Palestine solidarity have been forced to relitigate, again and again, whether anti-Zionism and solidarity with Palestinians constitute antisemitism — and whether such organizing should be systematically policed, investigated, or surveilled. At stake is a more fundamental right of the exploited: Can workers democratically connect economic struggles with Palestine solidarity, resistance to anti-immigrant and anti-Black racism, and the defense of civil liberties without exposing their organizing and deliberations to external pressure or repression?

We already have a word for the use of legal process as a political weapon: lawfare. You do not necessarily have to win. Investigation, expense, compelled disclosure, and possible sanctions can exact their own price.

Call its media counterpart pressfare: leaked material, selective or doctored quotations, and public identification can turn people into political targets and invite pressure on employers, universities, or government agencies.

The leaked CFA meeting should not be adjudicated through fragments selected for publication, especially when CFA’s statewide record contradicts the portrayal of a union indifferent to antisemitism. During the 2024 encampments, CFA opposed antisemitism and Islamophobia “in all forms” while supporting the encampments. Amid a 2025 federal antisemitism investigation, it stated that “as CFA members, we are united against antisemitism; it has no place in our communities,” while defending members’ academic freedom. CFA’s Palestine, Arab, and Muslim Caucus likewise defines its mission as confronting racism “in all its manifestations,” explicitly including antisemitism. author: Franco Giandana Gigena
title: Openness in AI development: a path to long-term independence
content:
As concerns grow over

deepening dependencies

 on a handful of Big Tech companies and the

outsized influence

 of the U.S. and China, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk used his speech during July’s inaugural

Global Dialogue on AI Governance

 to call on humans to

“take back our agency”

 over AI. But what does agency over AI really mean? What policies and practices can allow people to shape AI in ways that respect, rather than undermine,

human rights

? 


This blog post unpacks concrete initiatives that show how openness in AI development can increase people’s agency over AI and advance the development of public interest technology. At the same time, we reflect on how openness is not the same thing as mere access, and how short-term pragmatism can pave the way toward long-term independence.


Why is AI development so concentrated? 


Last year, the UN formally established an

Independent International Scientific Panel on AI

, intended to “advance scientific understanding and ensure that international deliberations are informed by the best available evidence.” The panel’s

preliminary report

, published this past July, contained a stark warning about the concentration of AI capabilities in a small number of firms and countries, which it says “could enable authoritarian capture and undermine democratic accountability.” But how has this concentration of power come about? 


One of the main reasons is that

building

 a complete, multilayered “

AI stack

” is both an astronomical investment and a complex technical challenge. This technological stack comprises:


The hardware layer, which provides the computing power that AI demands, mainly via advanced chips known as graphics processing units, or GPUs; 


The data layer, used for training and post-training; 


The model layer, which consists of the models themselves, such as GPT-4 or Claude, and the tools to service them; 


And finally, the application layer, which is the interface that users interact with. 


Currently, the U.S. and China are the only two countries realistically capable of building a fully national version of the entire stack, where they build and control all necessary infrastructure within their borders. However, even then, they would continue to depend on other countries for some elements, whether that’s for sourcing the chips or the critical minerals used in the hardware layer. Meanwhile, most other countries’ reliance on U.S. or Chinese companies creates critical safety and accessibility vulnerabilities. 


However, all is not lost for other countries and regions that want to build agency across the stack. There are several parts in the AI stack — notably

the data, model, and application layers

 — where greater openness and geopolitical collaboration could help foster collective agency. In this way, we can work towards what Martin Tisné, founder and CEO of the Collaborative for AI in the Public Interest, calls a “

global, open, resilient, non-aligned stack

” adaptable to local needs. 


How does openness support greater agency over AI? 


When considering how to gain more agency over AI, it’s worth looking at the free and open source software (FOSS) movement; a longstanding and major driver pushing for increased agency over technology, from the software running the internet, to the tools millions of people rely on every day, such as the Firefox internet browser. Although definitions of FOSS vary from

source

 to

source

, the essential principle means ensuring that anyone can access a given technology’s source code, study how it works, modify it, and share modified or unmodified copies with others.


The Open Source Initiative (

OSI

) has already applied this in the context of AI, with their

open source AI definition (OSAID)

 according to which an open source AI system is one that enables four key freedoms:


Use

 the system for any purpose and without having to ask for permission.


Study

 how the system works and understand how its results were created.


Modify

 the system for any purpose, including to change its output.


Share

 the system for others to use with or without modifications, for any purpose.


None of the offerings from major AI tool providers, such as OpenAI or Anthropic, currently enable any of these freedoms. Until now, the overwhelming preference in AI development has been for closed systems, accessible only through online interfaces or

application programming interfaces (APIs)

. This …

author: EDRi
title: EDRi celebrates Global Encryption Day 2026
content:
On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.

On 21 October 2026, we celebrate the Global Encryption Day! Part of EDRi’s KISS campaign, we celebrate this day with our partners, online, in Brussels and in different European capitals.

A recent survey conducted by CDT Europe shows that across several European countries (France, Sweden, Poland, and Ireland), people consistently oppose measures that would compromise encrypted communication platforms. In France, 92% of respondents agree they have the right to have private conversations online, while the figure goes to 94% in Poland, 88% in Sweden and 93% in Ireland.

Encryption is great for protecting the way our messages travel on the internet. Through “end to end encryption”, anyone can make sure that the content of an online conversation can not be intruded upon, not even the server that facilitates the transmission.

This year, we have coordinated several campaign actions to celebrate encryption.

1. Raising awareness in European Capitals through LED “Encryption trucks” driving around Paris, Berlin and Dublin and a metro poster campaign in Prague.

To visibilise people’s support for encryption, we partnered with the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement and Digitale Gesellschaft who are in the streets today, talking to people and press about the “Encryption trucks” and the importance of encryption. In Prague, our partner Iure has been supporting the Metro Posters campaign for the past weeks.

2. Working across silos with groups promoting gender justice, and sex workers rights in the digitalised society.

In the case of women defenders, land defenders from indigenous groups, racial justice activists, sex workers defenders and defenders of migrants, unsafe communications can have life or death consequences. For human rights defenders, secure and trusted communication is often a matter of physical safety and democratic organising.

For 21 October 2026, we have partnered with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement (France) to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. Check ESWA’s Instagram video and

3. Visibilising the testimonials of activists from Privacy Camp and across Europe

During 14th edition of Privacy Camp gathering that happened recently in Brussels, EDRi asked a few participants why encryption mattered for them. The people we interviewed came from a variety of causes: those fighting for a healthy European civic space, and for digital rights in Netherlands, Portugal and Germany. More, we asked EDRi’s over 35.000 supporters why encryption mattered to them too. Their answers inspired us to post some of them, and we will post them during the next couple of weeks. Check the content on EDRi’s social media channels – on Instagram , Mastodon or LinkedIn.

4. Connecting with global experts to advocate for encryption

During the Global Encryption Summit taking place at 4pm CET, EDRi’s expert Chloé Berthélémy will join a panel in an event organised by Internet Society, the Center for Democracy and Technology, Mozilla, and Global Partners Digital.

Europol and law enforcement are pushing to legalise hacking methods that weaken encryption. These methods rely on ordering a service provider (those who develop or maintain the software, computer system, network, or electronic device) to build vulnerabilities in their systems. With this demand, state actors want to enable the police or intelligence agencies to have access to our data and break encryption. Client-side scanning (scanning of all content such as text,images, videos, etc. on a device or shared in a communication channel) is a method proposed under the EU CSA Regulation. Key escrows or “key recovery”, involves placing decryption keys in a “vault” managed by a trusted authority or group of trusted authorities, who can break them out when access to the encrypted data is needed. Finally, ghost proposals refer to the modification of the encryption system to enable a third-party listener to be silently added to encrypted conversations.

In democratic societies, communication systems are vital for our lives and connections with others. Safe and secure communications and devices allow us to work, socialise, organise, express ourselves, and connect …

Les écrans, explique-t-il, feraient des élèves des « zombies », que leur téléphone, « stupéfiant-image », arracherait au monde. Leur confiscation aurait ainsi fait l'effet d'un électrochoc. Privés d'écran, les porcelets auraient enfin levé les yeux au ciel pour y découvrir leur misérable existence, et avec elle, ce que les adultes font de leur monde.


L'hypothèse est sans doute bienveillante. Le professeur précise qu'il écrit « sans aucune agressivité ni mépris envers mes élèves, que j'aime et apprécie ». On le croit, et c'est bien le problème. Le berger peut parfaitement aimer son troupeau : il n'en reste pas moins un berger. Or en matière de pouvoir pastoral, la sollicitude est parfois pire que le mépris.


Il faut en effet comprendre ce que cette hypothèse suppose : qu'avant la confiscation de leur téléphone, les lycéen

Car de porcherie, il est bien question, mais pas de celle du groin dans les réseaux. Ce sont les rats, les chiottes bouchés, les canicules dans les préfabriqués. Ce qu'on regarde et ce qu'on voit


Commençons par rendre aux écrans ce qui leur revient. author: Fundi Skweyiya-Gushu
title: Africa’s Cybersecurity Gap Is Not a Treaty Problem. It Is a Readiness Problem
content:
Africa’s digital economy is expanding faster than its ability to protect it.

INTERPOL’s African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026

, drawing on information from 36 countries, found that artificial intelligence was involved in 55 per cent of reported cybercrimes across the continent. Reported losses rose from $192 million in 2024 to $484 million, while 72 per cent of surveyed countries reported scam centres operating within their borders.


The figures expose a growing vulnerability. Africa’s digital transformation is creating economic opportunities but also expanding the terrain on which criminals operate. The question is whether African institutions can respond collectively when attacks cross borders, exploit financial systems and use AI to target victims at scale.


Morocco Cybersecurity Week

, held in Rabat from 12 to 14 October 2026, placed regional cooperation firmly on the agenda. The emphasis was appropriate. Yet Africa’s challenge extends beyond convening officials and announcing strategies. It is making institutions cooperate effectively under pressure.


Africa does not lack legal frameworks.

The African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection

, known as the

Malabo Convention,

 entered into force in June 2023 after years of delays. Morocco, meanwhile acceded to the

Council of Europe’s Budapest Convention on Cybercrime

 in 2018 and signed its

Second Additional Protocol on electronic evidence

 in 2022.


These instruments provide important foundations for criminal investigations, data protection and cross-border cooperation. But legal commitments cannot, on their own, ensure that investigators obtain evidence quickly, financial institutions exchange actionable intelligence or police services coordinate an effective response.


Cybercrime crosses institutional boundaries. A fraudulent transaction may involve a mobile-money provider, a bank, a telecommunications company, a cryptocurrency exchange and digital infrastructure spread across several jurisdictions. Each holds part of the evidence. When requests are delayed or responsibilities are unclear, investigators lose valuable time while criminals move money and erase their tracks. African institutions must therefore measure cooperation by what they can accomplish together, not by the number of agreements they endorse.


There is evidence that coordinated action works.

INTERPOL’s Operation Serengeti 2.0

, conducted between June and August 2025, brought together law-enforcement authorities from 18 African countries and the United Kingdom. It resulted in 1,209 arrests, the dismantling of 11,432 malicious infrastructures and the recovery of $97.4 million. Private-sector partners contributed intelligence and technical expertise.


The lesson is not that treaties are unnecessary. Investigations still require lawful powers, admissible evidence and safeguards. Rather, Serengeti demonstrates the value of shared objectives, established channels and institutions equipped to act on intelligence together.


This is where Africa should look beyond calls by some of its leaders for a continental equivalent of

NATO’s Article 5

. On 19 May 2025, Rwandan President Paul Kagame made these remarks in his keynote address at the inaugural

International Security Conference on Africa (ISCA)

, held at the Kigali Convention Centre. Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has also raised related questions at the

African Defence Chiefs Conference on Military Operations

. While these calls reflect growing interest in collective African security, NATO’s experience offers a more specific lesson for cybersecurity governance.

NATO recognises cyberspace as an operational domain

, and significant cyberattacks may, in certain circumstances, constitute an armed attack. However, invoking collective defence is not automatic: each case is assessed individually by the North Atlantic Council.


For African governments confronting cyber-enabled fraud, ransomware and attacks on public services, the more immediate lesson is not collective retaliation. It is collective preparedness.


Consider

NATO’s annual Locked Shields exercise

, organised by its

Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence

. The 2026 exercise brought together approximately 4,000 participants from 41 countries to defend simulated digital systems against complex attacks. Participants tested technical responses while confronting the coordination challenges that emerge during a crisis. The …

author: April Holcombe
title: Chinese youth in a very shit time of their lives
content:
Certain quarters of the internet are filling with content lauding contemporary China as an advanced, anti-imperialist, even socialist society. Its unrivalled high-speed rail network and its continued use of Communist jargon have encouraged some disillusioned Western youth to declare themselves in “a very Chinese time of my life”.

State-of-the-art infrastructure and Communist iconography have obvious appeal to a section of people living in decaying, imperialist and increasingly far-right-controlled Western capitalism. But there is a big difference between Instagram China, a Potemkin country showcased by influencers at the invitation of the tourism bureau and marketed to disillusioned Western youth, and the real China, a nuclear superpower ruled by bureaucrat-businessmen.  

Young Chinese people on social media—students, workers and the unemployed—use a very different kind of language than influencers do. Theirs is the language of alienation, exploitation and oppression in a society every bit as capitalist as our own.

“Involution”: an obscure word for a common problem

Ever heard of “involution”? Me neither. This obscure academic term, translated into Chinese (内卷

neijuan

), has entered common parlance among young people trapped in the country’s hypercompetitive economy. Literally meaning “inwardly curling”, anthropologists repurposed the term to describe activities that increase in complexity but lead nowhere. Chinese youth decided it captured their social predicament: instructed to work ever harder to stay ahead of their peers, they end up doing much more without being any better off.

Neijuan

describes many things: the gruelling hours at Big Tech companies; the notoriously competitive university entrance examinations; the apps pushing food delivery workers to ride ever faster; and the impossible social media-influenced beauty standards. The second character is now used as a standalone verb, meaning “to work or try too hard”.

Many young people who reject the

neijuan

 rat race opt instead to “lie flat” (躺平

tang ping

), a vibe somewhere between “quiet quitting” and “bedrotting”. The Ministry of State Security finds it deeply disturbing that anyone would want to lie flat, claiming in a Douyin (like TikTok) video that “an unnamed overseas organisation heavily funds ‘lying flat’ influencers, mass producing short videos promoting ‘anti-involution equals anti-exploitation’”.

Successive surveys show scepticism and pessimism rising sharply. In 2014, 62 percent of 10,000 respondents agreed that “effort is always rewarded in our country”; only 28 percent agreed a decade later. One-fifth blamed “the unfair economic system” for poverty in 2014; more than one-third did a decade later. Two-thirds agreed their families’ lives would improve from 2014-19, but less than half thought so for 2023-28.

“Graduation means unemployment”

University degrees once guaranteed well-paid government or tech jobs, providing the Communist Party’s dictatorship with a large, stable base of middle-class support. But now, often, “graduation means unemployment” (毕业即失业

biye ji shiye

). The gradual slowdown in economic growth has intensified competition for entry-level positions (more than 600 people, for example, applied for one basic Beijing office job in November 2025). Stable employment has given way to job flux. “I have family members who, since the early 2000s, never lost their jobs”, labour researcher Kevin Lin told

Red Flag

. “Last year, my cousin was laid off for the first time. Then he struggled to find another job, got laid off again, and is on to his third job.”

Unemployment is roughly twice the official figure of 5.2 percent, according to estimates by economist Li Daokui. “There are roughly 24 million long-term discouraged unemployed people, which is highly unfavourable for social stability”, the Tsinghua University academic told the China Macroeconomic Forum in July. The youth unemployment rate, officially hitting 17.9 percent that same month, has not included students since it soared past 25 percent in 2024, and hides a vast pool of underemployed youth working as little as one hour per week.

For the first time, the Communist Party’s most recent five-year plan includes no job-creation target. On the other hand, the government has a very clear target of 70 percent AI adoption across key industries by next year, inciting fears of layoffs among many IT workers. “I still can’t shake the feeling that I’m getting closer to being …

author: Tariq Ra’ouf
title: We Beat the Trump Administration in Court. Now We’re Going to the ICC.
content:
I am beginning to see a glimmer of hope that justice will be found for the dozens of family members I have lost in Gaza.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Over the course of the last three years, my family has lost 49 family members in Gaza. Their bodies were torn apart by shrapnel, crushed by falling buildings, and mutilated by bullets and munitions made and provided by the United States of America. Now, the U.S. is trying to dismantle the International Criminal Court, the only international court that can criminally prosecute U.S. officials for aiding and enabling genocide, by sanctioning the Court and attempting to intimidate anyone, including U.S. citizens, from working with them. So, in response, I joined others to sue this administration in order to take them to the very court they’re trying to destroy.

I’m a Palestinian-American organizer, and I helped establish Taxpayers Alliance Against Genocide (TAAG), which recently partnered with Democracy for the Arab World Now (DAWN) to sue the Trump administration so we can continue much-needed legal and advocacy work. Over the course of over a year, TAAG worked with an international legal team to prepare evidence against top U.S. officials for aiding and enabling the genocide of my people, but up until now, we haven’t been able to submit our evidence to the ICC because of this administration’s attacks and sanctions on the court and its judges.

Thankfully, that will now change after we successfully challenged the Trump administration in court. On October 13 we won a preliminary injunction that blocks this administration from being able to target our groups for working with sanctioned parties, clearing the way for us to proceed to the ICC. For the first time since the genocide started, I am beginning to see a glimmer of hope that justice will be found for the dozens of family members I have lost in Gaza.

Long before the Trump administration sanctioned the entirety of the International Criminal Court (ICC) on October 9, it first enacted Executive Order 14203 in February of 2025. This executive order granted administration officials the ability to sanction foreign nationals for supporting the ICC’s investigations into U.S. and Israeli parties guilty of committing war crimes and their complicity in genocide. Under this Executive Order (EO), the Trump administration also sanctioned leading Palestinian human rights groups al-Haq, al-Mezan, and the Palestinian Center for Human Rights (PCHR), as well as the UN Special Rapporteur for the Human Rights Situation on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, Francesca Albanese, along with other ICC officials.

What many people don’t know is that the EO that allowed the administration to sanction these parties doesn’t only go after foreign nationals, it also makes it a federal offense — punishable by a $1 million fine and/or 20 years in prison — for anyone, including American citizens, who provides or receives a “service” to or from a sanctioned party. This provision of the EO is exactly why TAAG and DAWN took this administration to court: Our lawsuit argued that the EO violates our First Amendment rights as American citizens to speak, associate, and engage in Palestine-related human rights advocacy with these parties. As a founding member of TAAG, I can tell you firsthand how these sanctions have prevented us and organizations like DAWN from being able to continue our work sharing evidence and advocacy ideas with people like Albanese and ICC officials, because the definition of “service” is so broad and undefined — the US can interpret it as being anything that confers a benefit to the recipient.

In an October 9 video of Marco Rubio announcing the actions against the ICC, he tries defending the administration’s actions by calling the ICC a “rogue court,” which the U.S. is “not subject to the jurisdiction of.” But Rubio leaves out a fundamental principle of international law: A country does not have to join the ICC for its nationals to fall within the Court’s jurisdiction.

If a country that is not a State Party to the Rome Statute commits a war crime on the lands of a country that is a state party, the perpetrator of that crime can be investigated. Given that Palestine is a State Party to the Rome Statute, and that Gaza (and the West Bank) are classified as Occupied Palestinian Territories by the United Nations …

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: U.S. Sanctions ICC in a Bid to Avoid "Criminal Liability": War Crimes Prosecutor Reed Brody
content:
The Trump administration on Friday placed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court that target the institution as a whole. This comes on top of earlier sanctions against individual

ICC

 judges and personnel. The administration has been escalating attacks on the

ICC

 since the court issued arrest warrants in 2024 for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant. It announced the sanctions just hours after former

ICC

 Judge Navi Pillay — the South African jurist who led the United Nations commission of inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza — was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.


“This is really an insurance policy against accountability for crimes that the United States and its ally Israel are committing in plain sight,” says war crimes prosecutor Reed Brody, a member of the International Commission of Jurists. The sanctions, which prevent U.S.-based banks and companies from transacting with the

ICC

, constitute an “existential attack” on the court, he says.

title: Gli espropri di Milano, i riot di Belfast, la guerra ibrida
content:
Riprendiamo da

Codice Rosso

 questo lungo approfondimento che analizza, in maniera comparativa, quanto accaduto durante e attorno ai riot milanesi e le mobilitazioni di Belfast dei mesi scorsi. Da più parti, in molti, evidenziano come la movimentazione sociale emersa il 17 ottobre in Italia, sia uno spartiacque significativo per molteplici ragioni. Crediamo che questo testo abbia, fra gli altri, l’utile pregio di “fare ordine” nell’analisi utilizzando categorie precise, mostrandoci un esempio concreto, quasi didattico, su come può essere impostata un’analisi orientata alla conricerca attraverso l’inchiesta. Buona lettura!


“

Tu sais ce que la rue m’a appris ? Si tu donnes ta joue, tu te fais niquer ta mère

”


La Haine,

 1995


1.


L’impiego inflazionato del concetto di «guerra ibrida» nel dibattito pubblico impone una chiarificazione. Nella dottrina strategica e nella sociologia dei conflitti, la guerra ibrida (

hybrid warfare

) non indica qualsiasi turbolenza sociale che transiti per le reti digitali, bensì una precisa architettura offensiva e deliberata in cui un attore statale o para-statale  combina operazioni informative, guerra psicologica e manipolazione computazionale per destabilizzare un sistema bersaglio mantenendosi sotto la soglia dello scontro militare aperto.


Tuttavia, il limite strutturale di ogni operazione ibrida o di guerra cognitiva (

cognitive warfare

) risiede nell’impossibilità di fabbricare dal nulla un’insorgenza materiale: nessun algoritmo e nessuna centrale di disinformazione possono spingere migliaia di persone a scendere fisicamente in strada se il messaggio non trova un terreno sociale ricettivo. Il momento teorico e operativo cruciale della guerra ibrida è dunque il

meccanismo di innesto

: il punto esatto in cui una regia esterna o superiore (

top-down

) riesce ad agganciarsi a tensioni sociali, frustrazioni economiche e fratture identitarie realmente esistenti sul territorio, piegandole ai propri fini strategici.


Lo strumento tecnico che realizza questa saldatura tra regia occulta e rabbia sociale è l’

astroturfing

 — termine derivato dal marchio di erba sintetica

AstroTurf

 per definire una mobilitazione artificiale progettata per simulare un’insorgenza spontanea dal basso (

grassroots

). Come dimostrato da report apparso proprio su

Codice Rosso

 e ripreso da

Contropiano

 (

«Astroturfing: accelerare la fascistizzazione delle classi popolari in Gran Bretagna»

), mentre l’astroturfing commerciale (storicamente impiegato da colossi come Microsoft, Monsanto o Walmart) mira ad alterare le metriche di mercato, l’astroturfing politico opera come il vettore d’innesco della guerra ibrida sul fronte interno. Esso costruisce quelli che Walter Lippmann definiva «pseudo-ambienti» cognitivi attraverso la sistematica «de-marcatura della fonte», arruolando basi sociali che agiscono fisicamente seguendo le linee di una strategia concepita altrove.


Il caso dei riot di Belfast, giugno 2026, rappresenta l’archetipo di come funzioni realmente questa strategia:


Il terreno sociale parassitato:

 L’operazione si innesta sulla devastazione socio-economica prodotta da decenni di deindustrializzazione neoliberista e austerità, accompagnata dall’abbandono della difesa materiale della classe lavoratrice da parte della sinistra tradizionale. In questo vuoto, l’ingegneria discorsiva della IA agentica ricodifica il proletariato in senso etnico come

«white working class»

 (classe lavoratrice bianca autoctona), deviando il conflitto verticale contro il capitale verso una guerra orizzontale contro migranti e richiedenti asilo.


Il dispositivo tecnico di aggancio:

 Per saldarsi al malessere popolare, gli operatori utilizzano profili fittizi (

sock puppets

) e avatar IA che mimano i codici linguistici ed emotivi della gente comune («populismo epistemologico»), sfruttando gli algoritmi di raccomandazione di TikTok, X, YouTube e Telegram. Questo meccanismo produce una «fascistizzazione post-organizzativa» che colpisce selettivamente i soggetti più fragili: come documentato dall’ESRC (

Vulnerability and Policing Futures Research Centre

), giovani maschi isolati o con difficoltà di attenzione e concentrazione risultano strutturalmente più esposti alla cattura in bolle di filtraggio (

filter bubbles

) xenofobe.

 La natura ibrida ed eterodiretta del fenomeno è certificata dalla triangolazione investigativa tra analisi ideologica …

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Does Wes Streeting Want Us Ready for War?
content:
Like many long-eyelashed men before him, Andy Burnham is sending mixed-messages. On the one hand, the prime ninister is keen to differentiate himself from his predecessor. Where Keir Starmer carried himself like a doctor who could only break bad news, Burnham is keen to stress that there is a role for the state in the improvement of people’s lives (even if it’s just capital punishment for playing reels without earbuds in). 


But how does the PM’s sunny disposition square with this Cabinet urging us to stock up for the apocalypse?


Wes Streeting – defence secretary, and creature hatched under a jar by the Labour Right – has urged Britons to

prepare for crisis

. The public has been advised to stock up with three days worth of water, food, non-mains light sources and stuff to keep warm, in case of disruption to supply chains caused by cyber-attacks, terrorism, or extreme weather events. You can find the government’s ‘Be Ready Checklist’

here

, and books you can burn in lieu of central heating

here

.


How big of a deal is this? Ordinarily, governments tend to prioritise the prevention of panic-buying. Readers may remember the toilet paper craze in the early days of the Covid pandemic, in which shoppers cleared shelves of loo roll because a rumour had gone round alleging that the Chinese had switched Andrex-production to the manufacturing of paper masks. It doesn’t take huge swings in consumer behaviour to put a dent in just-in-time supply chains – and the sight of depleted aisles can send people scurrying to buy even more. If ministers are advising people to stock up, it’s a sign that they sincerely think something scary is on the horizon.


The government’s resilience programme wasn’t a brainchild of Andy Burnham. It got going during

Keir Starmer’s time in office.

 Some critics say that Burnham hasn’t actually made

enough

 noise about it, pointing to

the lack of a big, shiny rollout

. But regardless of its prominence in No. 10’s grid, the instructions to the public to stock up in case of crisis is dominating the headlines today – and it’s perhaps meaningful that Wes Streeting’s public comments about the issue were made at the opening of a

new weapons manufacturing site

 in Shropshire.


As FT journalist Gideon Rachman noted on Newsnight last night, the language used by leaders in the West has been markedly hawkish on the prospects of World War III. Keir Starmer warned of a Nato war with Russia

as soon as 2030

; Mark Rutte, head of Nato, has said that we have to be prepared for wars of the scale that

our grandparents fought in

 (that’s the Second World War, not

the 2005 Ikea riots

). Rachman has warned that we could be

sleepwalking into World War III

 – I can’t help but wonder if some of our leaders are tapdancing there.


Threats to food supply – not least due to the

‘Godzilla’ El Niño

 superpowering extreme weather events – are real. But it might be the case that the government’s urging of preparedness is both a prudent message to the public in the face of an increasingly chaotic global order, and part of an effort to normalise the prospect of the UK being pulled into a brutal, meat-grinding war. It’s worth minding some of the lessons of the 20th Century: you can only manufacture so many weapons before they get used.

title: Guerra alla guerra! Verso le mobilitazioni internazionaliste contro la guerra indette dalla CIT
content:
Siamo di fronte ad uno scenario di guerre in continua espansione, dall’Ucraina al genocidio palestinese, all’Iran e in tanti luoghi nel mondo. Guerre che stanno provocando migliaia e migliaia di morti, distruzione di intere città e interi territori, producendo una economia di guerra che è causa principale del peggioramento delle condizioni di lavoro e di vita delle classi lavoratrici e della parte più povera della popolazione.


Ormai tutti i governi parlano di prospettive di guerra, di aumento delle spese militari, di reintrodurre il servizio di leva militare per fornire carne da macello per i nuovi conflitti, di trasformazione di aziende civili in produzioni di armi per incentivare il commercio di una merce sempre più richiesta e che sta realizzando enormi profitti.


Tutto ciò ci sta portando verso il baratro di una terza guerra mondiale che potrebbe essere l’ultimo atto di autodistruzione dell’intera umanità, per le potenti armi distruttive in mano ai vari governi, se non riusciremo a fermare questa corsa suicida.


È in considerazione di tale quadro disastroso che all’interno della CIT (Confederazione Internazionale del Lavoro), su sollecitazione di USI, le varie organizzazioni anarcosindacaliste aderenti hanno deciso una mobilitazione contro la guerra, con uno sciopero generale internazionale nella giornata del 30 ottobre e con manifestazioni nella giornata del 31 ottobre. Come USI CIT ci siamo mossi già da giugno convocando per due volte le varie sigle del sindacalismo di base per allargare la partecipazione allo sciopero contro la guerra proposto dalla CIT. Abbiamo fatto presente che USI ha aderito a tutti gli scioperi unitari contro la guerra e che i contenuti dello sciopero proposto erano ampiamente condivisi dalle varie componenti in quanto obbiettivi di scioperi precedenti. Inoltre si trattava di uno sciopero internazionale per cui era stato indispensabile stabilire già una data concordata con le varie componenti sindacali dei vari paesi che compongono la CIT. Al primo incontro hanno partecipato Sgb e Sgc, mentre interesse è stato dimostrato dalla rappresentanza del SiCobas, nella loro prospettiva di uno sciopero generale contro l’introduzione della 146 nella logistica in quei settori dove c’era la presenza, anche parziale, di materiali deperibili.


A questo punto USI CIT aveva la necessità di proclamare lo sciopero per il 30 ottobre per occupare quella giornata prima che le norme restrittive sulla regolamentazione degli scioperi non la rendessero più praticabile. La piattaforma dello sciopero è la seguente: contro tutte le guerre, taglio delle spese militari, ritiro delle missioni militari all’estero, aumento dei salari, più spese per sanità, scuola, edilizia pubblica, stop militari nelle scuole, stop sfratti e affitti calmierati, no al petrolio causa di inquinamento e di guerre ma sviluppo delle energie alternative e pulite, stop genocidio del popolo palestinese. Una proclamazione di cui diversi organi d’informazione hanno dato notizia e lo stesso canale 1 della RAI ne ha dato l’annuncio.


Il 25 settembre è stato promosso da Cub, Sgb, AdL Varese un incontro del sindacalismo di base con la proposta di uno sciopero generale. Nella stessa giornata in cui si svolgeva il Congresso della CIT a Massenzatico. In quell’incontro la nostra proposta è stata quella di convogliare unitariamente nello sciopero generale del 30 ottobre, ma si è preferito convergere nella prima data utile per lo sciopero che, per la regolamentazione in materia, li ha portati a proclamarlo il 4 dicembre, contro la finanziaria.


Nel frattempo Usb, nell’ambito del coordinamento dei sindacati internazionali di cui fa parte, comunicava la decisione del blocco dei porti a livello internazionale, contro la guerra e il transito delle armi, nella stessa giornata del 30 ottobre, con l’adesione del sindacato ORSA di Gioia Tauro. In un secondo momento, il 6 ottobre, anche Usb proclamava lo sciopero generale nella giornata del 30 ottobre, con l’adesione del Cobas Poste Usb. Successivamente anche il Cobas Scuola Sardegna proclamava lo sciopero nella giornata del 30 ottobre. Nel momento in cui si scrive inoltre è arrivata la comunicazione che la CUB Sanità italiana ha aderito a livello nazionale con il settore pubblico e privato allo sciopero generale USI del 30 ottobre. author: Amadou Diarra
title: Wood for War: How Wagner Was Paid in Central African Forest
content:
On 9 February 2021, as government troops and Russian mercenaries pushed rebels back from Bangui, the Central African Republic (CAR) signed Decree No. 21.044. It gave a young company called Bois Rouge a forestry permit covering 186,596 hectares in the south-western Lobaye region –

roughly 1,866 km² of tropical forest, an area larger than Greater London

.


Bois Rouge had never logged a tree. What it had, according to the

US Treasury

, was a patron: the concession was granted in exchange for services the Wagner Group provided to the CAR, at about the same time Wagner fighters and government forces were recapturing territory from the rebels.


Pieced together from sanctions files, customs data and transparency reports, the story shows how Wagner turned battlefield gains into commodities – and why timber proved a poor currency for a sanctioned militia.


A Russian Company with a Central African Face


Flag of the Central African Republic


Bois Rouge SARLU was

registered in Bangui in March 2019

. On paper it was a local firm with a Central African boss.

By October 2019

, at a forestry forum in Shanghai, Bois Rouge was listed under ‘Russia’, represented by Russians Artem Tolmachov and ‘Mike’ Vdovin.


A

UK parliamentary inquiry into the Wagner network

 later named Tolmachov as Bois Rouge’s commercial director. The research group All Eyes on Wagner

found he was also paid

 by two other companies tied to Wagner founder Yevgeny Prigozhin: Service K, which also financed the diamond firm Diamville, and Ferrum Mining, active in Madagascar. The pattern is familiar: a local shell in front, Russian managers behind.


The paperwork moved fast. The

CAR’s 2021 report to the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI)

 and a

forestry sector review

 record the permit, PEA 193, with 137,585 exploitable hectares and a management plan approved on 28 April 2021 – less than three months after the decree. The terms were generous: the newcomer received a moratorium on concession rent and export tax, which researchers consider unlawful and which cost the state and communities revenue.


The company built its sawmill in Boda, a town

government forces and Wagner had cleared of rebels

 shortly before the permit was issued. This sets the case apart from ordinary illegal logging. The wood was not smuggled out of a lawless forest. It was licensed by the state, as payment for war.


From Boda to Douala


The export route, as reconstructed by the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC), ran from Boda to the ‘Kassaï’ military base in Bangui, then by road through Cameroon to the port of Douala. A GI-TOC photograph from 7 June 2023 shows a loaded company truck at Kassaï. That logs were staged at a military base says much about who ran the business.


The Treasury lists the species exported: azobé, iroko, mukulungu, tali and, above all, sapele. Supplies flowed the other way through Broker Expert, a St Petersburg firm long used by Prigozhin, which made dozens of deliveries for Bois Rouge and, according to the Treasury, also moved the network’s money. Trade data showed

hundreds of imports

 of Russian machinery and logging equipment.


Most timber went to Turkey, the UAE and China, but some reached Europe.

Earthsight found

 that in 2022 the Danish firm WoodGroup ApS, a subsidiary of London-based Woodbois, took six shipments – 465 m³ of sapele worth an estimated €3.4 million at retail. One shipment was recorded as going to France’s Tropica-Bois, whose manager

told Earthsight

 the company had never bought the wood – a discrepancy, not proof of complicity.


New Names, Same Wood


After All Eyes on Wagner began publishing in 2022, Bois Rouge became Wood International Group (WIG) and

hired a new Central African director and a new Russian commercial director

. It did not help. In 2023,

CBS News filmed

 timber convoys heading from a Wagner-linked base to Cameroon and obtained about 100 WIG export documents whose details matched those of Bois Rouge.


OFAC, the Treasury’s sanctions office,

designated the company in September 2023

. In March 2024 the Treasury detailed its Wagner ties and sanctioned Broker Expert, after a joint probe with

Homeland Security Investigations

. Britain followed on 13 June 2024 (

UK sanctions list

; notices in the

Isle of Man

 and

Guernsey

). In Douala, WIG cargo was already being held up in June 2023.


GI-TOC counts 839 m³ exported in 2022 and a peak of 5,810 m³ …

title: Elisée Reclus - The Vivisection of China
content:
Author

: Elisée Reclus

Title

: The Vivisection of China

Date

: 1898

Notes

: From the September 1898 issue of The Atlantic

Source

: Retrieved on October 22, 2026 from an archived copy of https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/1898/09/the-vivisection-of-china/636369/


 THE great events which are creating such an excitement in the West Indies over the last shreds of the ancient colonial empire of Spain will undoubtedly have consequences of extreme importance, and become, in the fullest sense of the term, a part of history. But, however intense their interest, and however marked the change which they are certain to occasion in the equilibrium of the world, they remain altogether inferior in real significance to the revolutions which are taking place in the Far East.


 War of some sort between America and Spain on the subject of Cuba had long been unavoidable. No less than a century ago, — at the time when France lost her plantations in San Domingo, and the republic of Hayti was born, — it was easy to foresee the rupture of the ties which had bound to the Spain of Cortez and Pizarro the insular fragments of the great hemisphere appropriated by Pope Alexander VI. The various colonies were sure to break away, one by one, from their metropolitan stepmother, set up for themselves, and live their own life. Cuba and Porto Rico, sucked into the whirlpool of war, are but accomplishing their “manifest destiny,” and fulfilling the prophecies repeatedly uttered by the historians of the last generation but one.


 The progress of events in the eastern portion of the Asian continent had by no means been so fully anticipated. One might certainly have ventured to predict that there, also, populations long crushed by civil and military oppression would one day lay claim to the rights of free men; but it could never have been foreseen under what amazingly dramatic conditions the claim would be asserted. Our ancestors, at the beginning of the nineteenth century, would never have harbored, in their wildest dreams, the fantastic notion that Japan, the empire of the Rising Sun, would spontaneously transform itself into a “European power;” European, at least, if not in language, history, and traditions, in the complete recasting of its administration, institutions, customs, and theories, in its devotion to science, and in its entire and unreserved acceptance of a policy based on observation and experience.


 This is the great event of the century, — one which casts into the shade all the other occurrences of an epoch which has nevertheless been rich in memorable events. And it will be no solitary

avatar;

 there are unmistakable signs that other transformations of the same character are about to take place in the vast empire of China, and in all those countries where inhabitants of different race, yellow, red, or black, are brought into close contact with the men of our own Aryano - Greco - Latin civilization. So vanishes that oft-repeated assertion of the ethnologists, that

race

 is a final and irreducible fact, and that no possible progress in the perception of scientific or moral truths can ever prevail against it. It is from this point of view that the recent history of the Far East presents phenomena to which it behooves us to devote our most serious attention.


 There are those, of course, who tell us that all these events are illusory; that the prodigious changes which have taken place in the Japanese world are a lying phantasmagoria and a vain show; that the national mind and character have undergone no real modification; and that the Japanese are sure to escape, sooner or later, from the sphere of European attraction. We hear them compared to savages, who, having learned in the schools of London or Paris the customs of civilization, make haste, as soon as they get back to their forests and savannas, to cast aside their conventional garments, and array themselves in the toggery consecrated by ancestral instinct and hereditary custom.


 Such assertions appear to us to rest on a complete misconception of indisputable facts. The Japanese have most certainly entered into that realm of civilization on which Bacon and Darwin have set their seal; for if imperial caprice and the spread of bourgeois fashions have power to alter the external aspect of a nation, such influences can have but little effect on its underlying moral sense, its religious beliefs, its educational theories, and the essential principle of its …

title: HORROR AS FLEEING HUNTED STAG COLLIDES WITH CAR CARRYING WOMAN AND CHILD
content:
On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds met in West Bagborough, an area which falls within the constituency of Liberal Democrats MP Rachel Gilmour. Rachel has recently spoken publicly about her support for “trail” hunting, presenting what is a grim and violent reality as something that reads like a Disney fairytale.


MP Rachel Gilmour at last year’s BHSA “trail” hunting day, reported in the West Somerset Free Press.


Although stag hunts do not profess to “trail” hunt, like their fox hunting counterparts, they too manipulate the current law, exploiting loopholes to ensure the continuation of barbarism that brings terror to the countryside.


Rachel’s comments come at a time when sickening reports of hunting in the area are piling up, and you would think someone who has previously worked as Head of Strategy at the Environment Agency, would have a greater understanding of the countryside and the views of those that live there.


12th of October 2026


North Dorset Hunt Sabs and Mendip Hunt Sabs were joined by Holford Against Hunting as they sabbed the Quantock Staghounds.

Reports and video footage

 from the day detail how a hunted stag crossed the path of sabs and was subsequently seen to safety, thanks to them calling the hounds off.


More stags were chased throughout the day, with one seeking refuge on land owned by the League Against Cruel Sports. Reports also detail how two pairs of hounds were out at the same time; only two hounds are permitted to be used under the relevant legal exemptions within the Hunting Act.


However, since the reports were published there has been a disturbing update.


A stag crosses the path of sabs as he desperately tries to escape the Quantock Staghounds.

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


At 4:30pm, two members of the public were travelling along the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford when they came across the hunt. As we continue to see, rabid hunt supporters will line roads, making as much noise as possible to prevent stags from crossing as they seek safety. This incident was no different, except that what was described as a “gigantic stag” ran across the road and collided with a vehicle.


A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”


The driver of the vehicle was a young woman with a small child on board, and thankfully, neither of them sustained any injuries, but both were badly shaken up. The hunt, showing absolutely no concern or regard for the members of the public who had been involved in or witnessed this horrific incident, fled the scene as police were called.


The witness went on to say that, despite looking for the stag, they couldn’t see him. Sabs have since reported that it is believed the stag did get away and was not killed by the hunt. However, after being hit by the car, there is no way of knowing what injuries he sustained or whether or not he ultimately survived this horrifying ordeal.


Quantock Staghounds causing chaos and terror in an area of “outstanding natural beauty.”

© North Dorset Hunt Sabs


Excuses, excuses


Stag hunts often try to use the excuse of dispatching an injured or sick deer to justify their barbaric actions. However, on this occasion, when there was clearly an injured stag, albeit as a result of their actions, they were quick to flee the scene. 


In her recent defence of “trail” hunting, Rachel Gilmour has claimed that hunt meets offer “

companionship to retirees and widowers who might otherwise face isolation and loneliness.”

 She also added that hunting “

forms part of a long and richly woven rural social fabric that binds farms, villages and families together through shared work, ritual, and memories.”


Her comments are a far cry from the realities of hunting. Many people living within these communities are not only opposed to it but are also put in grave danger every time these hunts go out.


It’s not just stag hunting taking place under Rachel’s nose


As well as stag hunts operating in Rachel’s constituency, the Tiverton Foxhounds’ kennels are also located within it.

 of October 2026 they met in Rackenford, an area represented by Rachel’s Liberal Democrats’ colleague Ian Roome. A Devon County Hunt Sabs

report

 from the day details how “

one fox after another”

 was chased as they kept watch from the ground and used their drone.

title: Lies the Fur Industry Tells!
content:
Mink and fox killers and their apologists often say the most ridiculous things to try and mitigate their losses after raids like the two we have seen in the last couple of months, in which 3000 or more captive mink were liberated from horrific captivity. Sample absurdities spouted as fact include:

Lie #1: Many or most of the escaped animals were run over and killed by cars.

– The absurdity of this statement is that before liberation, death was 100% certain. Every animal on the farm was bred to die by the end of November. While it is true a small number may be hit by cars after being released, most will not, and if nothing else they have been given a chance at freedom. In reality, fox and mink farms are located in rural areas with little traffic, the animals are quick and solitary animals, and it beggars belief to imagine them aggregating in the road waiting to be run over by the rare passing vehicle.

– Mink are in fact only a few generations removed from their wild cousins and have not yet had their wild instincts bred out. The “Mink Rehabilitation Project” led by convicted ALF liberator Rod Coronado proved this decades ago. Mink legally purchased from a fur farm were released into the wild and shown through observation to retain natural survival instincts and thrive in the wild after a lifetime in a cage. Studies with radio-collared mink demonstrate clearly the animals are capable of surviving in the wild. No, they won’t starve or freeze to death or die from dehydration. Most areas where mink are imprisoned are actually native habitat for American mink.

Lie #3: Most of the mink are recaptured

– Mink normally travel several miles a day. Most mink have dispersed into the surrounding fields before the liberation is even complete. A few may be recaptured, but only a handful at most. Its absurd to imagine hundreds of wild animals being recaptured by lunkhead farmers running around looking for them. Our hearts go out to those few recaptured who were given a shot at life and now have only suffering ahead.

– Captive, now free and wild fox and mink have no desire to be anywhere near humans and their “livestock” or pets. There may be some minimal impact on the local ecosystems temporarily while the animals disperse and learn their way around, but no habitats are decimated or overrun or rendered free of other small animals. And no, the animals do not kill wantonly and more than they need to survive, and they certainly don’t attack human bystanders, as some apologists have had the audacity to suggest.

Liberationists break the law in adherence to a higher law – one which states animals are not commodities, not objects, but sentient creatures with a right to live. They will fight for the lives of these animals “as if they were our own.”

The Animal Liberation Front and other anonymous activists utilize economic sabotage in addition to the direct liberation of animals from conditions of abuse and imprisonment to halt needless animal suffering. By making it more expensive to trade in the lives of innocent, sentient beings, they maintain the atrocities against our brothers and sisters are likely to occur in smaller numbers; their goal is to abolish the exploitation, imprisonment, torture and killing of all innocent, non-human animals.

Join the ALF – Historically, those wishing to participate in direct action have either acted alone or gotten together with others they could trust of like mind and just started doing actions. ALF cells of 1 or more persons operate independently, and typically are begun locally by like-minded individuals who decide to take action against animal abusers. To begin learning about direct action, start here and follow the links where they may take you. Only you can decide what action to take, when to get started, and how much longer the animals must wait for liberation.

The number of fur farms in America has dwindled from more than 300 in the 1990s to less than 100 today, as the fur industry continues its steady decline into oblivion. A listing of all known fur farms in North America, is available here: https://finalnail.com/

author: Sylvie Bunz
title: Nach Aufdeckungen: Rumäniens grausamste Hundetötungsstation schließt
content:
Update vom 21. Oktober 2026


PETA und seine Partnerorganisation sind schockiert über die behördliche Entscheidung, die Wiedereröffnung der Tierheime VetMedan und Daeni zu genehmigen. Seit Monaten kämpfen unsere NGO-Partner vor Ort gemeinsam mit PETA und anderen Tierschützenden sowie Organisationen mit aller Kraft dafür, dass diese Einrichtungen dauerhaft geschlossen bleiben.


Gemeinsam mit unseren Partnern prüfen wir nun erneut, ob es juristische Möglichkeiten gibt, gegen diese Entscheidungen vorzugehen und die Umsetzung der Beschlüsse auszusetzen. Solange mit Hunden erhebliche finanzielle Gewinne erzielt werden, stoßen Tierschutzbemühungen immer wieder auf massive Widerstände und es wird deutlich, wie stark das System ist, das an dem Leid der Hunde viel Geld verdient.


Update vom 22. Juni 2026


PETAs Partner im Einsatz gegen Rumäniens Hundetötungsstationen: Uzunu von Aspa Ivets für immer geschlossen


Nach Jahren voller Leid, Gewalt und systematischer Tötungen wurde das von einem Privatunternehmen geführte Tierheim Uzunu im Juni 2026 dauerhaft geschlossen. Die Entscheidung markiert einen Wendepunkt – für die Tiere, für die Tierschutzbewegung und für alle Menschen, die sich unermüdlich gegen diese Grausamkeiten eingesetzt haben. PETAs Partner in Rumänien, der Verein Eduxanima, hat sich zusammen mit weiteren lokalen und internationalen Vereinen dafür seit Monaten intensiv eingesetzt.


Das Tierheim Uzunu im Kreis Giurgiu war über Jahre hinweg ein Ort des Schreckens: Hunde wurden auf den Straßen eingefangen, in der Tötungsstation unter widrigsten Bedingungen eingesperrt und grausam getötet. Die jüngsten Pathologieberichte bestätigen, was Tierschützer:innen seit Langem vermutet haben: Viele der Tiere starben durch Vergasung – ein qualvoller Tod.


Hintergrund: Aufdeckungen über massives Tierleid


Erst als die Polizei des Kreises Prahova im März 2026 eingriff, kam Bewegung in den Fall. Die Ermittlungen führten zur Entdeckung von über 105 Hundekadavern, die trotz eines Tötungsverbots im Kühlcontainer des Lagers aufbewahrt worden waren. Die anschließenden Untersuchungen der toten Hunde belegten eindeutig, dass die Tiere an schwerer Methämoglobinämie und Hypoxie starben – ein klarer Hinweis auf Vergasung.


Auf Grundlage dieser Ergebnisse ordnete die Veterinärbehörde schließlich die endgültige Schließung der Einrichtung an.


Das derzeitige massive Tierschutzproblem ist, dass an diesem Ort weiterhin rund 240 Hunde vor sich hin vegetieren und kaum versorgt werden. Nur zwei Mitarbeiter kümmern sich um die Hunde, die an diesem Ort an Krankheiten leiden, sich gegenseitig verletzten und sterben. Es gibt weder medizinische Hilfe noch Unterstützung für die Vierbeiner. Unser Partner vor Ort setzt sich für die Hunde ein und fordert von den zuständigen Behörden, dass diese dringend und sofort die Verantwortung übernehmen müssen. Die Behörden und die Polizei sind nach der offiziellen Schließung für die Hunde verantwortlich.


Tierfreundliche und nachhaltige Lösungen sind erforderlich


Einrichtungen wie Uzunu existieren, weil Gemeinden weiterhin Verträge mit kriminellen Firmen abschließen, die Hunde einfangen und töten – finanziert mit öffentlichen Geldern, ohne nachhaltige Wirkung. Die einzige wirksame Lösung gegen Überpopulation bleibt: Kastration, Aufklärung und Bildung. Seit vielen Jahren hat unser Partner ein entsprechendes Konzept, welches immer wieder Gemeinden und Behörden vorgelegt wird und mit dem Rumänien innerhalb von zehn Jahren – statistisch berechnet – nahezu keine heimatlosen Hunde mehr hätte.


Dieses Konzept fußt auf ethischen Maßnahmen und weist geringere Ausgaben auf. Es ist an der Zeit, dass dieses Konzept Beachtung findet und das „System Hund“ sich endlich zum Positiven verändert. Die Schließung von Uzunu zeigt, dass Veränderung möglich ist, wenn Behörden handeln und die Öffentlichkeit hinschaut.


Hundetötungsstation Rumänien: So arbeitet PETA weiter


Nachdem wir von PETA Deutschland uns mit einem nachdrucksvollen Brief an die zuständigen Politiker, die Polizei und die oberste Veterinärbehörde gewandt haben, ist klar: Der Fall ist noch nicht abgeschlossen. Wir werten aktuell die Antworten mit allen Informationen aus, um weiter in den Austausch mit den Behörden zu gehen. Wir erhöhen den Druck und bleiben weiter an dem Fall Uzunu dran und kämpfen für die verbleibenden Hunde und deren Versorgung.

author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.
