title: Söke Ekmek ve Gül açıklaması: Her çocuğa okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı yemek istiyoruz
content:
Aydın - Söke'de Belediye Meydanı’nda Söke Ekmek ve Gül "Bir Öğün Ücretsiz Sağlıklı Yemek Güvenli Okul Güvenli Ulaşım İstiyoruz” diyerek basın açıklaması yaptı.

Söke Ekmek ve Gül’ün çağrısıyla yapılan açıklamaya veliler, Söke Kadın Dayanışma Derneği ve Söke Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri de destek verdi. "Bir öğün ücretsiz sağlıklı yemek güvenli okul güvenli ulaşım istiyoruz” pankartının açıldığı basın açıklamasıni Söke Ekmek ve Gül adına öğrenci velisi Huri Abrinç okudu.

Çocukların okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek yiyebilmesi için yıllardır ülkenin dört bir yanında ve Söke’de aralıksız mücadele ettiklerini belirten Abrinç; “Söke Ekmek ve Gül olarak imza kampanyaları düzenledik, stantlar açtık, çocukların beslenme hakkını kararlılıkla savunduk. 2022 yılında Ekmek ve Gül tarafından başlatılan, 2023’te Kocaeli Ekmek ve Gül Kadın Dayanışma Derneği’nin çalışmalarıyla büyüyen, Esenyalı Kadın Dayanışma Derneği üyesi bir kadının hukuki mücadelesine kadar uzanan bu talep; bugün Türkiye’nin her köşesindeki kadınların, velilerin, öğretmenlerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin ortak talebidir. Toplanan binlerce imza, yapılan basın açıklamaları ve dayanışma ağları bu ihtiyacın ne kadar hayati, acil ve vazgeçilmez olduğunu defalarca kanıtlamıştır.

Çünkü biliyoruz ki derinleşen ekonomik kriz ortamında çocukların okula aç gittiği, ailelerin beslenme çantalarını doldurmakta zorlandığı, temel gıda ürünlerinin dahi lüks hâline geldiği bir ülkede; sağlıklı beslenme bir lütuf veya yardım değil, en temel insan hakkıdır. Çocuklar açken eğitimde fırsat eşitliğinden ya da nitelikli bir eğitimden söz edilemez” dedi.

Yürütülen bu haklı mücadeleler ve yükselen kamuoyu baskısı sonucunda Millî Eğitim Bakanlığının 5-19 Ekim tarihleri arasında ücretsiz okul yemeğine ilişkin velilerin görüşlerini almak amacıyla bir anket süreci yürüttüğünü hatırlatan Abrinç: “Yıllardır dile getirilen bu yakıcı ihtiyacı anlamak için çocukların açlığının bu kadar derinleşmesini bekleyen Bakanlığa soruyoruz: Velilerin ve kadınların sesi neden bugüne kadar duyulmadı” sorusunu sordu.

Bakanlığın adım atması önemli olsa da, yürütülen anketin kapsamı, erişilebilirliği ve yöntemi ciddi soru işaretleri doğurduğunu vurgulayan Abrinç anketle ilgili eksiklikleri sıraladı:

İnternet üzerinden yürütülen ankete pek çok veli eşit biçimde katılamamıştır. Veliler ankete ulaşmaya çalıştıklarında "yetkiniz yok" uyarılarıyla, sistemde yaşanan teknik sorunlarla karşılaşmış; internet ve telefon imkânı bulunmayan ya da dijital araçları kullanmakta zorlanan aileler süreçten tamamen izole edilmiştir. Ayrıca anket hakkında velilere yeterli bilgilendirme yapılmamıştır.

Edindiğimiz bilgilere göre ilkokul öğrencileri anket kapsamı dışında tutulmuş, süreç yalnızca ortaokul ve lise düzeyine sıkıştırılmıştır. Oysa en temel gelişim çağındaki ilkokul ve okul öncesi çocukların beslenme hakkı nasıl göz ardı edilebilir?

Servis imkânlarının kaldırılması veya kısıtlanmasıyla mağdur edilen taşımalı eğitim kapsamındaki aileler, bu anket hakkında da yeterince bilgilendirilmemiştir. Çocukların ulaşım ve beslenme ihtiyaçları birlikte değerlendirilmelidir.”

“İnternete erişemeyen, yetki engeline takılan ya da anket kapsamına alınmayan çocukların sağlıklı beslenmeye ihtiyacı yok mu? Çocukların en temel hakkı, teknik aksaklıklarla dolu bir anketin sonucuna ya da hangi eğitim kademesinde olduğuna indirgenebilir mi?” sorularını soran Abrinç, “Bir ankete katılamamış olmak, ücretsiz yemek ihtiyacının olmadığı anlamına gelmez! Çocukların açlığı anket sorularıyla giderilemez; beslenme sorumluluğu yalnızca ailelerin ve kadınların omuzlarına yıkılamaz” ifadelerini kullandı

Mıllî Eğitim Bakanlığına ve yetkililere çağrı yapan Abrinç şu talepleri sıraladı

Eşit ve Koşulsuz Hak: Okul öncesinden liseye kadar, kamu okullarındaki tüm öğrencilere ayrım yapılmaksızın her gün bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek derhal sağlanmalıdır.

Anket Sonucu Beklenmemelidir: Ücretsiz okul yemeği bir anketin sonucuna bağlanmadan, bütçe bahanelerinin arkasına sığınmadan kalıcı bir kamu hizmeti olarak uygulamaya konulmalıdır.

Şeffaflık ve Hesap Verilebilirlik: Yapılan anketin kaç veliye ulaştığı, hangi kademeleri kapsadığı ve sonuçların nasıl değerlendirildiği kamuoyuyla açık ve şeffaf bir şekilde paylaşılmalıdır.

Erişilebilir Katılım Yöntemleri: Dijital araçları kullanamayan veya erişim sorunu yaşayan veliler için yüz yüze görüşmeler, basılı formlar ve okullar aracılığıyla katılım kanalları oluşturulmalıdır.

author: Kodao Productions
title: The Political Economy of Healthcare and the PhilHealth Dilemma: Social Insurance or Socialized Medicine?
content:
By

Prof. Sarah Raymundo


Angelo V. Suarez

’s sharp intervention in response to Cielo Magno’s senatorial campaign line brings a vital structural issue into the public sphere. Credit must be given to Magno: her platform draws directly from a concrete social issue plaguing the vast majority of Filipinos—a crisis of public health and economic vulnerability that demands urgent collective attention. Unlike the posture of mainstream politicians running on empty campaigns, abstract pledges of service, and hollow soundbites, Magno brings a substantive issue to the table that gives the citizenry something real to evaluate and debate.


It is precisely this substance that prompted Suarez—a poet, creative industry worker, and staunch peasant advocate for the Unyon ng mga Manggagawa sa Agrikultura (UMA)—to respond, participate, and rally his friends and comrades around this critical issue. While one might be tempted to label this response as a “new politics” brought forward by figures from late Generation X and early Millennial cohorts, its core is rooted in a fundamental class politics challenging mainstream governance in the Philippines. This intervention offers an opportunity to build on our collective arsenal of knowledge and critique regarding the current Philippine health system. It aims to foster a well-informed, critical citizenry whose stakes in national elections must be elevated to what the working people truly deserve. What is at stake in this counter-critique is the necessity of deepening public deliberation on genuine reforms—and examining how these immediate struggles can advance more systemic, transformative aspirations for society.


Dissecting the Policy Platform and the Critique


In her published academic research—such as her study on pharmaceutical competition for the Philippine Competition Commission—Magno approaches the issue of expensive medicines through neoclassical market regulation. She does not advocate for breaking away from foreign drug monopolies or building a state-owned pharmaceutical industry. Instead, she identifies high medicine prices as a symptom of insufficient market competition, brand bias, and distorted prescribing behaviors. Her proposed remedy relies on market regulation: using antitrust oversight to encourage generic competition, alongside using PhilHealth as a bulk purchaser to negotiate lower prices from private pharmaceutical suppliers and absorb outpatient drug costs.


Angelo Suarez’s critique dismantles this reformist premise at its structural foundation. Suarez’s actual text makes four direct arguments:


First, policy directions that prioritize a “stronger” PhilHealth obstruct the creation of a strong public health system. Second, PhilHealth fosters and entrenches an insurance system that welcomes and relies upon the private health sector. Third, the state must directly fund the supply side by hiring health workers with security of tenure and reasonable wages, building accessible facilities staffed by well-trained personnel, and establishing a nationalized pharmaceutical industry grounded in a program of national industrialization. Fourth, health services can and should be made entirely free, funded directly out of general state taxes without resorting to PhilHealth as an insurance middleman.


While Suarez articulates these core demands, this analysis extends his critique by placing it within the broader frameworks of international political economy, World Bank policy history, and Samir Amin’s theory of imperialist value transfer. Suarez identifies the political demands; this intervention maps the structural mechanisms behind them.


The core dispute between Magno’s platform and Suarez’s counter-position is not over whether Filipinos deserve access to medical care, but over the mechanism through which that care is delivered.


Magno advocates for demand-side financing, where the state acts as an insurer buying health services and imported medicines on behalf of citizens within a market economy. Suarez advocates for supply-side direct provision, where the state directly owns, operates, and funds the physical, human, and industrial infrastructure of health as an unmediated public good. #


 


The post

The Political Economy of Healthcare and the PhilHealth Dilemma: Social Insurance or Socialized Medicine?

 appeared first on

Kodao Productions

title: Immer nur Behindertenwerkstätten: Warum verdienen Menschen mit Behinderung so wenig? Und wo bleibt die Inklusion?
content:
Dossier


„

In der Pandemie sind beinahe unbemerkt Löhne in Behindertenwerkstätten gekürzt worden. Schon vorher ließ sich von den Geld kaum leben. (…) Der Lohn der Beschäftigten in Behinderten-Werkstätten setzt sich in Deutschland aus mehreren Teilen zusammen: Ein sogenanntes Arbeitsförderungsgeld von 52 Euro wird aus Töpfen des Landes gezahlt. Dazu kommt ein Grundlohn von 89 Euro und ein individuell festgelegter Steigerungsbetrag. Diese beiden Posten müssen die Werkstätten selbst erwirtschaften. Als die Corona-Pandemie Deutschland erreichte, schlossen die Betreiber ihre Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung. In der Folge konnten viele Aufträge nicht mehr erfüllt werden. Der Steigerungslohn entfiel. (…) 19 Prozent der Werkstätten, die an der Umfrage teil nahmen, gaben an, Löhne gekürzt zu haben. Weitere 18 Prozent gaben an, dass Kürzungen absehbar sind. Insgesamt hat sich in der Umfrage gezeigt, dass die Auswirkungen der Krise verzögert in den Werkstätten ankommen

…“

Artikel von Fabian Hillebrand vom 14.11.2020 im ND online

 

 und auch dazu:


Gerechtigkeit statt Almosen: Die GFF geht mit Jürgen Linnemann gegen das diskriminierende Entgeltsystem in „Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen“ (WfbM) vor Gericht


Mindestlohn in Werkstätten: Der sitzende Leistungsträger


„

Jürgen Linnemann hat 40 Jahre in Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung gearbeitet. Jetzt zieht er für den Mindestlohn vor Gericht. (…) Sie klagen vor dem Arbeitsgericht Münster darauf, dass die Werkstatt ihm die Differenz zwischen seinem bisherigen Arbeitsentgelt und dem Mindestlohn zahlt. Linnemann sei Arbeitnehmer und habe dementsprechend Anrecht auf den Mindestlohn, so die Begründung. Der gesetzliche Mindestlohn müsse zudem auch in Werkstätten gelten. Anfang September soll das Arbeitsgericht eine Entscheidung treffen. Falls es beides verneint, will die GFF das derzeitige Entgeltsystem auf Vereinbarkeit mit Verfassungs-, Unions- und Völkerrecht überprüfen lassen. Bislang fehlen entsprechende Gerichtsentscheidungen. Das könnte sieben bis zehn Jahre dauern, wie Linnemanns Anwältin schätzt. Bis dahin ist er bereits in Rente. (…)


Das Sondersystem der Werkstätten hat der Bundesrepublik bereits zwei Rügen durch den UN-Fachausschuss für die Rechte von Menschen mit Behinderungen beschert. Reformpläne gibt es zahlreiche. Erst 2023 kam eine Studie im Auftrag der damaligen Ampel-Regierung zu dem Ergebnis, dass ein steuersubventioniertes Mindestlohnmodell besser funktionieren und zu mehr Gerechtigkeit führen würde. Andere fordern für einen inklusiven Arbeitsmarkt die Abschaffung der Werkstätten

…“

Artikel von Sarah Yolanda Koss vom 15.10.2026 in ND online

 


Nur 200 Euro Monatslohn. Jürgen Linnemann will per Musterprozess erreichen, dass in Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen Mindestlohn bezahlt wird. Er klagt gegen Lohndumping.


„

Der Mindestlohn von 13,90 Euro pro Stunde gilt fast überall – nicht aber in Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen. Jürgen Linnemann will das ändern. Er arbeitet in den Freckenhorster Werkstätten (NRW). Beim Arbeitsgericht Münster hat er auf Bezahlung von Mindestlohn geklagt. Es ist ein Musterprozess von bundesweiter Bedeutung.


Jürgen Linnemann arbeitet 24,3 Stunden pro Woche und erhält nur einen Stundenlohn von rund 2 Euro. Im Monat macht das knapp 200 Euro. Der 57-Jährige ist Teil eines Teams, das Dokumente digitalisiert. Bevor die Papiere gescannt werden, entfernt Linnemann die Tackerklammern. Für seine Tätigkeit im Werkstattrat – einer Art Betriebsrat – hat er bereits das Bundesverdienstkreuz erhalten.


Jetzt klagt Linnemann für eine bessere Bezahlung. Mit Unterstützung der Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte (GFF) und der NGO Sozialhelden hat Linnemann Klage beim Arbeitsgericht Münster erhoben. Er will 1.300 Euro zusätzlich pro Monat, den Mindestlohn eben. Die Klage hat große praktische Relevanz. Bundesweit arbeiten rund 300.000 Personen in rund 700 „Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen“ (WfbM), so der offizielle Titel. Voraussetzung ist, dass man zwar arbeitsfähig ist, aber auf dem normalen Arbeitsmarkt keine Chance hätte. title: Sağlık Bakanlığı: Eşitsizlikleri devam ettirmekte kararlıyız!
content:
Sağlık Bakanlığı İstatistik Yıllığı (SBİY) 2025 Haber Bülteni, 30 Eylül 2025, çarşamba günü, saat 17:00’de 

(!)

 yayımlandı. İlki 12 yıl önce, 2014 yılında yine eylül ayının son günü SBİY 2013 Haber Bülteni olarak yayımlanmıştı. Bülten, istatistik yıllığından yaklaşık üç, dört ay önce daha az sayıdaki veri grubunu kapsayacak şekilde yayımlanıyor. Bununla birlikte, ölümlülük, aşılama ve hizmet kullanımıyla ilgili bir önceki yılın verilerine 9-10 ay sonra da olsa ulaşabilmiş oluyoruz. Ve Türkiye’nin dokuz ilinin bulunduğu coğrafyada yaşayanların, AKP’li yılların bundan önceki 16 yılında olduğu gibi, 17nci yılında da değişmeyen bir biçimde sağlık ve sosyoekonomik eşitsizlere mahkûm edilmiş olduğunu görüyoruz. Bu haftaki yazıda söz konusu durumu ve AKP’li Sağlık Bakanlığı’nın verileri kendine saklamak gibi bir özelliğini kendilerinin sunduğu kaynaklar üzerinden ele alacağım.


ERİŞ BİLALOĞLU YAZDI


Yeni Bir Sıfırlama Çabası mı: Türkiye’de Bebek Ölüm Hızı


29 Ocak 2015


AKP’li bakanlık verileri kendine saklıyor


AKP tarafından 2002 yılında kurulan 58. Hükümet’e kadar sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili veriler yıllardır istatistik yıllıklarıyla düzenli olarak kamuoyuyla paylaşılıyordu. Ancak

58. Hükümet ve o kabinenin Sağlık Bakanı Recep Akdağ ile birlikte, sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili veriler kamuoyundan 2011 yılına kadar saklandı,

paylaşılmadı. Dünya Sağlık Örgütü başta olmak üzere, Türkiye’nin üyesi olduğu uluslararası kuruluşların talebi üzerine, bir AKP Hükümeti ve Sağlık Bakanı olarak ilk defa 2011 yılında, 2008 yılına ait veriler “Sağlık Bakanlığı Sağlık İstatistikleri Yıllığı 2008” başlığında Bakan Akdağ’ın önsözüyle yayımlandı. O nedenle Türkiye’nin 2003-2007 yıllarına ait sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili verileri diğer yıllar gibi düzenli bir biçimde bugüne kadar paylaşılmadı.


Sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleriyle ilgili istatistikler, 2011 yılından sonra, Sağlık Bakanlığı ve Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu (TÜİK) tarafından düzenli olarak yayımlanıyor. TÜİK, özelikle doğurganlık ve ölümlülükle ilgili verileri Merkezi Nüfus İdaresi Sistemi (MERNİS) üzerinden iller düzeyinde, sağlık harcamalarıyla ilgili verileri Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı ile Sosyal Güvenlik Kurumu (SGK) ve yerel yönetimlerden ve “Hanehalkı Bütçe Anketi” çalışması üzerinden, hastalıklarla ilgili verileri de “Türkiye Sağlık Araştırması” üzerinden sağlıyor. Sağlık Bakanlığı da bu verileri kullanıp yaptığı hesaplamaları ve sağlık kurumları, sağlık emekçileri, ilaç, sağlık hizmetleri kullanımı vb. verileri Türkiye’nin makro düzeyde ekonomik ve sosyo-ekonomik yapıya göre gruplandığı 12 bölge, İstatistiki Bölge Bilgileri Sınıflaması-1 (İBBS-1), üzerinden paylaşıyor. Bununla birlikte, 

Sağlık Bakanlığı kaynakları üzerinden 81 ilden herhangi birinin sağlık ve sağlık hizmetleri verilerini, durumunu öğrenebilmek mümkün olamıyor.

Çünkü Sağlık Bakanlığı illerin verilerini yayımlamayı uzun zamandır tercih etmiyor.


Tabip Odası Bebek Ölümlerine Önlem Paketini Açıkladı


25 Eylül 2008


Bebek ölüm hızı önemli bir toplumsal sağlık düzeyi göstergesidir

Bunlar aynı zamanda, ülkelerin gelişmişlik düzeyi göstergeleri arasında da yer almaktadır. Çünkü, bu üç gösterge bir ülkede, bölgede, ilde vb. öncelikle beslenme, barınma, alt yapı ve eğitim başta olmak üzere, sosyoekonomik koşulların durumu ve sağlık hizmetlerinin ulaşılabilir olup olmamasıyla sağlık hizmetlerinin niteliğinden doğrudan etkilenmektedir.

author: Elizabeth Weill-Greenberg
title: Tablets Make Communication Easier Behind Bars – But Deaf People Are Left Behind
content:
This story was co-published with


Truthout

.


Tablet computers have revolutionized communication inside prisons for hearing prisoners. Prison systems from across the country — including in

New York

,

California

, and

Illinois

 — have

distributed tens of thousands

 of tablets to incarcerated people, which they can use to call home, watch movies, message loved ones, or attend virtual classes (although they are often

charged predatory fees

 for accessing these benefits). As of 2022,

25 state prison systems

 had tablet distribution programs, according to the Electronic Privacy Information Center. 


But as the rollout of such tablets continues, many deaf incarcerated people have been left behind. 


Disability justice organization HEARD points out that

it’s

unknown

 how many deaf people are incarcerated in U.S. prisons, but a

2015 report

 by the Bureau of Labor Statistics estimated that 6.2 percent of incarcerated people in

state

 and

federal

 prisons have a hearing disability, which would equal about 71,000 people.


Daniel Valenzuela, who is deaf, is incarcerated at Danville Correctional Center in Illinois. Last year, the Illinois Department of Corrections (IDOC)

distributed tablets

 to all incarcerated people. But IDOC blocks videophone capabilities, preventing Valenzuela from communicating in his primary language, American Sign Language (ASL).  


In September, Valenzuela sued the IDOC director for violating the Americans with Disabilities Act.


“I have six kids, four grandkids, and one of my sons is in the military. I cherish and love my family so much,” said Valenzuela in a

press release

 announcing the lawsuit. “I just want to tell them happy birthday and I am so grieved when I can’t call because I don’t want them to think I forgot.”


There are at least three other deaf individuals at Danville who primarily use ASL to communicate, according to the

complaint

 filed by Disability Rights Advocates, Equip for Equality, and the law firm Much Shelist. 


“Across the Illinois Department of Corrections, people can use tablets to communicate with their loved ones, which has been a game changer in removing restrictions on communication,” Valenzuela’s attorney, Rachel Weisberg, the directing attorney at Disability Rights Advocates, told

Truthout

. “But for Mr. Valenzuela and other deaf people who use American Sign Language, that same access simply isn’t available.” 


IDOC did not respond to a request for comment by the time of publication.


Last year, in addition to distributing tablets to incarcerated people, IDOC

announced

 it would provide every incarcerated person with 775 free domestic phone call minutes per month. In a press release,

IDOC said

 that these initiatives, working in tandem, “enhance family connections and increase access to technology that supports rehabilitation.” 


But deaf prisoners are excluded from accessing these critical programs. 


Unlike hearing prisoners who can use their tablets to make calls from their cells, Valenzuela must get a guard’s permission to walk to another building to use the one videophone that’s available to him. In at least one instance, Valenzuela had to go out in the pouring rain to use the videophone, according to the complaint. 


“When prison officials don’t communicate with deaf/disabled people in ways they can understand, they may be written up for being ‘non-compliant.'”


The videophone is often unavailable because the unit itself breaks down, the prison is on lockdown, or a guard denies his request, according to the complaint. Last year, Valenzuela was unable to speak with his family during the holidays because the phone was not working for 54 straight days, from November 2025 to January 2026. However, if the tablets malfunction, there are several backup phones that incarcerated hearing people can use, the complaint says.


“We’re asking for equal access, as that’s what the law requires,” said Weisberg. “Equal access is not static — it must reflect the benefits currently offered to others and account for the needs of people with disabilities as technology and communication systems evolve.”


These issues are not limited to Illinois. Advocates say incarcerated deaf people have to contend with discriminatory communication practices in prisons throughout the country.


“In prisons where we’ve seen scores of deaf/disabled people, there may only be 2 videophones,” Kah Mendoza, the communications coordinator for

HEARD

author: Claudia Castillo
title: How can a “broken” body cross the world?
content:
How can a “broken” body cross the world?

 


(My experience participating in Women Deliver 2026)


By Gianna Agostina Mastrolinardo

 


(SCROLL DOWN FOR ORIGINAL TEXT IN SPANISH)


 

For me, as woman with a disability, participating in the last edition of Women Deliver in Melbourne, Australia wasn’t simply about attending a conference. This was an intense and transformative experience that tested my own limits, and it also meant that me and my body had to navigate structural barriers that restrict the participation of young women with disabilities in global events such as this one. 

 


 

One full day of traveling, three flights, more than 12,000 kilometers of flying. Never having traveled so far, the magnitude of the event, and not speaking English that fluently all could have been reason enough to justify saying no to this opportunity. However, I decided to say yes. Even though I was afraid, I said yes with the conviction that we must occupy those spaces, because our presence transforms them. 

 


 


My desire to cross the world and be part of what was happening in Naarm was not enough for me to stop thinking of it as something impossible. Support and collective effort were crucial to stripping that last word of the prefix that imprisons dreams. And now that I think of this experience again, an inescapable feeling comes to me: the relief of knowing I don’t have to think about disability in isolation. 

 


 


 I am a Latin American “lisiada” cripple from Córdoba, Argentina, I am 23 years old and I live my daily life fighting for the effective realization of the rights of people with disabilities with the certainty that every roll of my wheels is possible because there are many people who work with me, who accompany me, who care for me and who even believe and trust in me when I simply cannot.  

 


WEI not only generously approached me with this opportunity. They also worked with Women Deliver so that this experience did not become only about managing how to overcome barriers, but rather, that it could be about enjoyment, learning, and the wonderful opportunity to find each other regardless of our languages or the physical distances between the places we come from.

 


 


Without a doubt, this experience was challenging. However, the availability of support, the design of dialogue spaces, and the warmth that was present throughout the process reaffirmed my belief that there is something extremely political about spaces having to take steps to ensure accessibility. When facing barriers stops being an individual issue and instead creating ways in which everyone can participate becomes a collective responsibility, the world we dream of achieving becomes a reality. 

 


 


To be in Melbourne was to live for a few days in that world. I had never before experienced such an accessible city. Sidewalks, ramps, public transport, and a quality of life I thought existed only in my fantasies. I did not have to worry about managing how to move with my wheelchair or  do research ahead of time to make sure there were accessible bathrooms. Where I live, I cannot use public transportation because even when we manage to find accessible transport, getting to the bus stop is impossible. But in Australia, I even saw accommodations that I had never imagined (like a button that opens heavy doors! I definitely need that in my life). Having so many resources translates into immeasurable freedom, and I am aware that experiencing them was a great privilege.

 


 


The political support from my organization:

La Mesa de Trabajo en Discapacidad y Derechos Humanos

was another essential element to making this possible, because they accompanied me during the trip and in everything that came before it. They were there every step of the way; they helped me to practice my English and t

o gauge the implications of a convening of this nature, to understand the discussions, and to consider my own contributions. This helped me feel a sense of security and confidence. My colleague Bri put her body in every part of the process with me. She was there not only during the trip, but also when, out of nowhere, I was asked to take medical exams for my visa. She was there when we discovered that my wheelchair couldn’t come with me due to airline restrictions and when—during the trip— the wheelchair I did travel with broke. She listened to me and offered me her words and physical and emotional support when I felt nervous, anxious, or frustrated …

С большим удовлетворением мы объявляем о создании Либертарной Социалистической Организации (OSL), общенациональной анархистской политической организации, которая возникла как результат почти трех десятилетий развития эспецифизма в Бразилии.

OSL была основана 9 июля этого (2023) года в Сан-Паулу в результате первой сессии совместного съезда, проведенного активистами Федерации Анархистов Рио-де-Жанейро (FARJ), Анархистской организации либертарного социализма (OASL, Сан-Паулу), Rusga Libertária (Мату Гроссу) и Коллектива народных анархистов Минас-Жерайс (COMPA), а также активистами из других регионов Бразилии. Организации, ограниченные Бразильскими Штатами, распускаются, и мы приступаем к созданию единой анархистской политической организации, которая будет охватывать все регионы Бразилии.

Мы придерживаемся организационного дуализма, то есть участия анархистов в народных движениях (социальный уровень) и в специфически политических организациях (политический уровень). На социальном уровне мы близки к историческим формам революционного синдикализма; на политическом уровне к историческим формам цельных и программно-ориентированных организаций: платформизма и эспецифизма.

В OSL мы стремимся вкладывать силы в построение и в регулярное и постоянное участие в народных движениях, имея четкую и определенную программу, чтобы сформировать реальную политическую силу, которая сможет сделать анархизм снова инструментом вовлечения в борьбу угнетенных классов. Мы также выступаем за отказ от принципизма, конкретно подходя к реальности, действуя как «рыба в воде» среди рабочего класса. Кроме того, мы предлагаем окончательно отказаться от Синтеза в пользу программа-ориентированной организационной позиции, с теоретическим, идеологическим и практическим единством, с коллективной ответственностью и дисциплиной.

Мы с большим оптимизмом смотрим на этот новый этап и уверены, что OSL будет способствовать продвижению организованного анархизма и народной борьбы на территории Бразилии!

За продвижение организованного анархизма в Бразилии!

«Анархизм является не красивым воображением, не кабинетной мыслью философа, а социальным движением трудовых масс и уже по одному этому он должен сплотить свои силы в общую, постоянно действующую организацию, как того требует действительность и стратегия социально-классовой борьбы»[1].

По итогам первой сессии нашего Конгресса, состоявшейся в июле 2023 года в городе Сан-Паулу, мы объявляем о создании Либертарной Социалистической Организации (OSL).

title: Walter Benjamin - The Moon
content:
Author

: Walter Benjamin

Title

: The Moon

Source

:

Berlin Childhood around 1900


 The light streaming down from the moon has no part in the theater of our daily existence. The terrain it illuminates so equivocally seems to belong to some counterearth or alternate earth. It is an earth different from that to which the moon is subject as satellite, for it is itself transformed into a satellite of the moon. Its broad bosom, whose breath was time, stirs no longer; the creation has finally made its way back home, and can again don the widow’s veil which the day had torn off. The pale beam that stole into my room through the blinds gave me to understand this. The course of my sleep was disturbed; the moon cut through it with its coming and going. When it was there in the room and I awoke, I was effectively unhoused, for my room seemed willing to accommodate no one besides the moon.


 The first things that attracted my gaze were the two cream-colored basins on the washstand. By day, it never entered my head to dwell on them. In the moonlight, however, the band of blue that ran around the upper part of the basins was a provocation. It simulated a woven band encircling a skirt-hem. And in fact the brim of each basin was curled like a frill. Between the two basins stood pot-bellied jugs, made of the same porcelain with the same floral pattern. When I climbed out of bed, they clinked, and this elinking was communicated over the washstand’s marble surface to basins and bowls, glasses and carafes. As happy as I was to receive from my nocturnal surroundings a sign of life—be it only the echo of my own—it was nonetheless an unreliable sign, and was waiting, like a false friend, to dupe me at the very moment I least expected it. This was when I lifted the carafe with my hand to pour some water into a glass. The gurgling of the water, the noise with which I put down first the carafe and then the glass—it all struck my ear as repetition. For every spot on this alternate earth to which I was transported appeared wholly occupied by what once had been. Thus, each sound and each moment came toward me as the double of itself. And when I had endured this for a while, I would draw near my bed gripped by the fear of finding myself already stretched out upon it.


 This anxiety did not altogether subside until I once again felt the mattress under my back. Then I fell asleep. The moonlight withdrew slowly from my room. And, often, the room already lay in darkness when I awoke for a second or third time. My hand would necessarily be the first to brave emergence from the trench of sleep, in which it had taken cover before the dream. And just as one sometimes falls prey to a previously unexploded shell even after a battle has ended, so my hand was constantly expecting to be overtaken on its way by a previously delayed dream. When the nightlight, flickering, then brought peace to my hand and me, it appeared that nothing more remained of the world than a single, stubborn question. It may be that this question nested in the folds of the door-curtain that shielded me from noise. It may be that it was nothing but a residue of many past nights. Or, finally, it may be that it was the other side of the feeling of strangeness which the moon had brought on. The question was: Why is there anything at all in the world, why the world? With amazement, I realized that nothing in it could compel me to think the world. Its nonbeing would have struck me as not a whit more problematic than its being, which seemed to wink at nonbeing. The moon had an easy time with this being.“


 My childhood was already nearing its end when, at last, the moon seemed willing to assert its claim to the earth by daylight, a claim which previously it had made only at night.85 High above the horizon-—large, but pale-— it stood, in the sky of a dream, looking down on the streets of Berlin. It was still light outside. Gathered around me were the members of my family, their bearing a little stiff, like that of figures in a daguerreotype. Only my sister was missing. “Where is Dora?”I heard my mother exclaim. Suddenly, the full moon up in the sky began ever more rapidly to expand- Coming nearer and nearer, it tore the planet asunder. The railing of the iron balcony, on which we all had taken our places overlooking the street, broke into a thousand pieces, and the bodies which had been there flew apart in all directions. The funnel created by the moon’s approach sucked everything in …

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Pengarsipan Anarkis: Kritik & Kritik-Diri #1
content:
Belum selesai menghadapi permasalahan ekonomi yang bagai melempar api setitik ke padang ilalang itu, muncul permasalahan baru yang kini menghantui pengarsipan anarkis, permasalahan yang lebih halus dan bahkan tidak dipermasalahkan karena tidak tampak bermasalah di permukaan.

Kata-kata yang dicetak dan diterbitkan (atau bahkan yang tidak diterbitkan sekalipun), seperti buku, pamflet, leaflet, zine mendapat tempat yang signifikan di kalangan anarkis. Karena media tersebut terbukti mampu menyimpan berbagai pengalaman dan pemikiran banyak individu, yang bahkan dalam kasus tertentu, jika terdapat intervensi terhadap media cetak tersebut, eksistensinya akan tetap bertahan—untuk tidak menyebut abadi—lebih lama dari umur para individu yang mengalami pengalaman dan yang mencetuskan pemikiran tersebut. Dan individu-individu yang secara lengkap menyimpan kata-kata yang dicetak serta diterbitkan itu pun kemudian akan mendapatkan suatu manfaat, seperti dapat memiliki akses untuk melihat kembali “praktik untuk mencapai emansipasi” (gerakan dan perjuangan) yang terdahulu.

Itulah mengapa, menurut Baker (2023) ketika meneliti budaya tandingan—atau proses perubahan evolusioner—anarkis Spanyol, banyak perpustakaan anarkis dibangun untuk menyediakan akses terhadap koleksi lengkap kata-kata tercetak yang telah lama tidak diterbitkan kembali. Sayangnya, sejarah pertumbuhan budaya tandingan atau proses perubahan evolusioner anarkis ini tidak terjadi secara mulus atau bahkan macet di Indonesia. Karena Indonesia mengalami periode otoritarianisme—dalam artian paling kerasnya—yang berkepanjangan. Para anarkis tahun 1920-an habis dibuang ke Digul pasca pemberontakan 1926; sedangkan para individu berkecenderungan (anarkis-)sindikalis yang muncul pada tahun 1940-an disingkirkan secara paksa oleh rezim Orde Lama Karno dari pabrik-pabrik yang mereka swa-kelola dan disingkirkan secara perlahan dari arena pemikiran/intelektual oleh PKI; dan menjadi sama sekali tidak terlacak eksisensinya pasca genosida 1965 dan naiknya rezim Orde Bau Harto ke tampuk kekuasaan (Bima, 2018).

Walaupun, periode otoritarianisme berkepanjangan tersebut tidak khas dialami oleh para anarkis di Indonesia saja. Periode otoritarianisme keras yang berkepanjangan, yakni rezim Komunis Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej (1948-1965/17 tahun) dan Nicolae Ceaușescu, menjadikan para anarkis di Rumania dan di Indonesia memiliki—tanpa menafikan perbedaan dampak dari pasca-komunis di Rumania dan pasca-kolonial serta pasca-otoriter-militer di Indonesia yang menciptakan perbedaan yang kompleks—kesamaan dalam hal sejarah perkembangan budaya anarkis mereka. Karena ketika rezim komunis naik ke tampuk kekuasaan para anarkis disingkirkan mulai dari ditekan pergerakannya sampai dibunuh, dan sebagian yang hidup harus pergi mengasingkan diri ke luar negeri atau tetap di Rumania tetapi memilih untuk mengambil sikap tiarap total (Anarhiva, 2021). Situasi ini akhirnya, menurut Tataran (2026), membuat para anarkis yang bermunculan di Rumania pada masa-masa keruntuhan rezim komunis pada 1989 atau setelahnya, yang mayoritas bergerak di skena anarko-punk, hanya memiliki pengetahuan yang secuil atau bahkan tidak memiliki sama sekali pengetahuan tentang para anarkis yang eksis sebelum mereka, sehingga secara otomatis mereka tidak memiliki pengalaman kolektif yang dapat dijadikan rujukan ketika mereka menjalankan praktik anarkis/anti-otoritarian.

Sejalan dengan Adrian Tataran, Ucok (2026) dalam diskusi buku Unfinished Nation yang diselenggarakan di Perpustakaan Bunga di Tembok pun mengatakan hal yang nyaris sama. Menurutnya, sebelum buku Perang yang Tidak Akan Kita Menangkan karya Bima Satria Putra terbit—jauh setelah reformasi—pada tahun 2018, para anarkis yang bermunculan—dan sama seperti di Rumania, yang banyak pula bergerak di skena anarko-punk—saat masa-masa kejatuhan Harto beserta rezim Orde Baunya dan masa setelahnya tidak memiliki pengetahuan tentang gerakan anarkis terdahulu, sehingga sempat terbersit dalam pemikiran mereka kalau diri mereka adalah anarkis generasi pertama di Indonesia. Alhasil, tanpa pengalaman dan memori kolektif yang diwariskan dari para anarkis terdahulu, para anarkis yang hadir kemudian tersebut harus mulai membangun dari awal; berbanding terbalik dengan otoritarianisme yang walaupun dikatakan runtuh, mereka sudah memiliki birokrasi, struktur, militer, yang telah dibangun selama berdekade dan mapan serta siap diwariskan, sehingga bukan hal yang sulit untuk kembali ke tampuk kekuasaan …

¿QUÉ es el patriotismo? ¿Es el amor por el lugar donde uno nació, el lugar de los recuerdos y las esperanzas de la infancia, de los sueños y las aspiraciones? ¿Es el lugar donde, con ingenuidad infantil, contemplábamos las nubes fugaces y nos preguntábamos por qué nosotros tampoco podíamos correr tan rápido? ¿El lugar donde contábamos los miles de millones de estrellas centelleantes, aterrorizados ante la idea de que cada una de ellas fuera «un ojo» que traspasara lo más profundo de nuestras pequeñas almas? ¿Es el lugar donde escuchábamos el canto de los pájaros y anhelábamos tener alas para volar, como ellos, hacia tierras lejanas? ¿O el lugar donde nos sentábamos a los pies de nuestra madre, embelesados por maravillosos relatos de grandes hazañas y conquistas? En resumen, ¿es el amor por ese lugar, donde cada pulgada representa recuerdos queridos y preciosos de una infancia feliz, alegre y juguetona?

Si eso fuera patriotismo, pocos hombres estadounidenses de hoy en día podrían considerarse patriotas, ya que el lugar de juego se ha convertido en fábrica, molino y mina, mientras que los sonidos ensordecedores de la maquinaria han sustituido a la música de los pájaros. Tampoco podemos ya escuchar las historias de grandes hazañas, pues las que cuentan hoy nuestras madres no son más que historias de dolor, lágrimas y aflicción.

¿Qué es, entonces, el patriotismo? «El patriotismo, señor, es el último recurso de los sinvergüenzas», dijo el Dr. Johnson. León Tolstói, el mayor antipatriota de nuestro tiempo, define el patriotismo como el principio que justifica la formación de asesinos en masa; un oficio que requiere mejor equipamiento para el ejercicio del asesinato que para la fabricación de artículos de primera necesidad como zapatos, ropa y viviendas; un oficio que garantiza mejores beneficios y mayor gloria que el del trabajador medio.

Gustave Hervé [1], otro gran antipatriota, califica acertadamente el patriotismo de superstición —una mucho más perjudicial, brutal e inhumana que la religión—. La superstición de la religión tuvo su origen en la incapacidad del hombre para explicar los fenómenos naturales. Es decir, cuando el hombre primitivo oía un trueno o veía un relámpago, no podía dar una explicación a ninguno de ellos y, por lo tanto, concluía que detrás de ellos debía de haber una fuerza mayor que él mismo. Del mismo modo, veía una fuerza sobrenatural en la lluvia y en los diversos cambios que se producen en la naturaleza. El patriotismo, por el contrario, es una superstición creada artificialmente y mantenida a través de una red de mentiras y falsedades; una superstición que despoja al hombre de su autoestima y dignidad, y aumenta su arrogancia y vanidad.

De hecho, la vanidad, la arrogancia y el egoísmo son los elementos esenciales del patriotismo. Permítanme ilustrarlo. El patriotismo parte de la base de que nuestro planeta está dividido en pequeños rincones, cada uno rodeado por una verja de hierro. I den ungsocialistiska pressen hade så tidigt som år 1907 agitation förts för syndikalismen. I majnumret år 1910 av den fackliga tidningen Bageriarbetaren gjorde bagarnas förtroendeman, Anders Sjöstedt, som var redaktör för nämnda tidning, ett försök att hindra syndikalismens spridning bland bagarna, vilka i stort antal gripits av den syndikalistiska agitationen. Då skrev undertecknad ett genmäle mot den mäktiga förbundschefens angrepp under rubriken: **.."Man säger... Genmäle på artikeln i majnumret."*

"Man säger, att bagarna skola vara med då det gäller att upplösa förbunden och bilda Lokala Samorganisationer", inledde vår förtroendeman Anders Sjöstedt, och tillade sedan: "Tack för erbjudandet, men skall man då behandla bagarna på samma sätt som man vill göra nu, tycker vi synd om bagarna." På detta sätt vill jag svara att aggressiva kommer arbetsgivarna alltid att vara oavsett vilken organisationsform arbetarna har, tills dess de får så kraftigt mothugg så de lugnar sina rovdjurskänslor. Och då behövs det sannerligen syndikalistiskt försvarskraft. Därför kan inte en förtroendeman, om än med stor vilja, uträtta något ensamt - utan en vaken, handlingsfull och slagkraftig organisation.

Lusten att krossa arbetarnas organisationer har icke saknats av de privata arbetsgivarna - ej ens från styrelser och föreståndare för kooperativa bagerier i södra Sverge. Närmare angivet Skåne. Där har till och med öppna strider utbrutit.

Alla arbetsgivare vill ha utgifterna så små som möjligt. Men inkomsterna så stora som möjligt. Detta får ju främst arbetarna, producenterna, lida för.

Vidare hade Sjöstedt skrivit: "Lyssna på styrelserna för 'Föreningsbagerierna' och och för en del kooperativa bagerier vilka diskutera om bagarna på ett utmanande sätt, när det gäller deras avtal."

För min del tyckte jag att bagarna icke skulle bry sig om vad dessa konservativa styrelsemedlemmar pladdrar om. Och är det någon underhandling de ej vill bry sig om och önskar de icke vara med om någon överenskommelse som vi vet att de kan gå med på, behöver vi icke kompromissa och springa och berusa dessa herrar i all evighet, och tigga om rätt till mänsklig existens. Vi ha förmåga att slå till! Vi äro de starka! Gör slut på fegheten! Det är vi som är producenter!

Därför behöva att omändra organisationerna till kampduglighet och smidig anpassningsförmåga efter de förhållanden som kan uppstå. Vad de Lokala Samorganisationerna angår så äro de mest praktiska, och kan med heder avlösa de gamla tungrodda byråkratiska fackföreningarna, som äro i majoritet i detta land.

Att inte organisationsfrågan är ett aktuellt spörsmål just nu, bland bagarna, är en lögn av stort mått. Den är aktuell och skall bliva det ännu mer när tiden är mogen. Trots vad Sjöstedt skriver! Och hans ångest som så tydligt märks!

Allt sedan de reformistiska organisationernas början har i regel "förts de korslagda armarnas strid", som de gamla ledana är så förtjusta i - till borgardömets fromma!

Detta har visat sig odugligt. Vi har ju bagerier, som är bojkottade ända sedan den tid som "Svenska Bageri- och Konditoriarbetareförbundet" startades. Och det var inte i går!

Vi har exempel på detta i Göteborg och i Uddevalla, ja lite varstans i detta land.

Det skulle taga allt för stort utrymme i anspråk att räkna upp alla. Och när uppgörelse kommer att träffas vet ingen! Och ingen gör något för att ändring skall ske. Ingen delar ut så mycket som en bojkottslapp för att upplysa allmänheten om förhållandet, att konflikt råder. Därför behövs det pigga organisationer i vilka medlemmarna äro socialistiskt skolade och nyktra. Då kan vi marschera framåt och vinna något, trots det att arbetsgivarna göra allt för att slå ned vår frammarsch. Detta få ingen glömma!

Man skriver så ofta och påstår att folk är så egoistiska, att de ej vill betala avgifterna till föreningarna …

author: Unknown
title: Пётр Кропоткин - Профсоюзное движение и Парламентаризм
content:
Автор

: Пётр Кропоткин

Название

: Профсоюзное движение и Парламентаризм

Дата

: 13 октября 1906

Источник

: Les Temps nouveaux, год 12-й, №24


Эта статья из Les Temps Nouveaux (13 октября 1906) показывает, как Кропоткин обсуждает, каким образом марксистская социал-демократия пришла к признанию важности боевого профсоюзного движения. Он указывает на то, как профсоюзы, созданные как средство борьбы с эксплуатацией, могли бы стать строительными блоками социалистической экономики.


ПРОФСОЮЗНОЕ ДВИЖЕНИЕ

И ПАРЛАМЕНТАРИЗМ


 Телеграф сообщает нам, что на последнем съезде немецкой социал-демократической партии в Мангейме было принято важное решение. Приведём сначала дословно телеграмму агентства Рейтер:


 «Съезд принял затем 386 голосами против 65 вторую часть резолюции, которая объявляет, что профессиональные союзы (синдикаты) являются организациями,

необходимыми

 для улучшения социальных условий рабочего класса,

и что они не менее необходимы, чем сама социал-демократическая партия

. Следовательно, обеим организациям часто необходимо действовать по общему согласию в их борьбе. Для обеспечения этого единства мысли и действия объявляется абсолютно необходимым, чтобы профсоюзное движение было проникнуто духом социал-демократии».


 Итак, немецкая социал-демократическая партия, которая в течение долгих лет боролась – как мы сами здесь констатировали – против независимой организации профессиональных союзов, которая когда-то объявляла её бесполезной рядом с социал-демократией и долго стремилась её поглотить, вынуждена признать «насущную необходимость» мощной профсоюзной организации

рядом с социал-демократической партией

. Она доходит даже до того, что говорит, что профсоюзные организации

ничуть не менее

 «

необходимы, чем сама социал-демократическая партия

».


 Она добавляет, что абсолютно необходимо, чтобы профсоюзное движение было «

проникнуто

 духом социал-демократии», но это лишь благочестивое пожелание; и к тому же от этого пожелания далеко до прежних притязаний, которые состояли в том, чтобы сначала

поглотить

 профсоюзную организацию или, по крайней мере, управлять ею по указке.


 **


 Это понятно. Ведь какой бы крайне умеренной ни была профсоюзная организация в Германии, – а это достаточно показала её резолюция Кёльнского съезда, – она не захотела позволить парламентским вождям социал-демократии управлять собой. Есть профсоюзы, вдохновляемые авторитарными и парламентскими социалистами; есть проникнутые буржуазным духом; и есть, наконец, независимые, которые ненавидят своих хозяев и готовы яростно бороться против них на экономической почве. Но первые, вторые и третьи создались абсолютно отдельно от социалистических политиков. Число их членов чрезвычайно возросло в последнее время – в Германии, как и повсюду, – и последние цифры дают для Германии около миллиона профсоюзных рабочих, организованных вне политических партий.


 Это тот миллион людей, за которым социал-демократические вожди в конце концов признали право на существование. Они больше не требуют, чтобы те позволили себя поглотить политической организацией: они в конце концов признают, что профсоюзная организация

должна

 оставаться

отдельной и независимой от политической организации

. Всё, что они теперь от неё требуют, – это «действовать по общему согласию в их борьбе», – сотрудничать, когда представится случай.


 **


 Это, очевидно, лучший способ – единственный способ – установить действенное сотрудничество вместо конфликтов, которые продолжались до тех пор, пока вожди социал-демократии стремились завоевать профсоюзы и диктовать им законы.


 Но это еще не всё. То же явление происходит повсюду. Рабочие замечают, что они пошли по ложному пути, когда позволили социал-демократическим политикам вторгнуться в их профессиональные организации и сделать из них инструмент парламентской борьбы.


 Основная идея французских и английских рабочих, когда они первый раз встретились в 1864 году, чтобы основать Международное товарищество рабочих, действительно состояла в том, чтобы создать грозную рабочую силу, которая могла бы навязать свою волю промышленным предпринимателям. Добиться от них прежде всего лучших условий труда – лучшей заработной платы, сокращения рабочего времени, более здоровых фабрик, менее опасных машин и так далее. Но также – взять в конечном счёте в свои руки саму организацию промышленности.


 Ибо тут не может быть сомнений. Уже в 1830 году, когда Роберт Оуэн основал в Англии Великий союз профессий (который он уже тогда хотел …

author: Unknown
title: Marina St. James and Fíona Vivienne - The December Rupture
content:
Author

: Marina St. James and Fíona Vivienne

Title

: The December Rupture

Subtitle

: Luigi Mangione and the Revolt Against Reverence

Date

: 2025

Notes

: Essay from The Luigi Reader, Bacchus Editions 2025. bacchuseditions.net

Source

: Bacchus Editions, bacchuseditions.net


 I begin with appetite. Not the appetite that can be satisfied by acquisition, nor the domesticated desire that waits patiently for permission, but the appetite of the living individual who discovers that existence belongs to no abstraction. The appetite to think beyond inheritance, to desire without justification, to create without consecrating creation as duty. To encounter the world as something inexhaustible, terrible, sensuous, and gloriously unfinished.


 I want the pleasures of my own existence. The books scattered across a table. The intoxicating intimacy of an idea pursued beyond its respectable conclusion. The warmth of another body. The insolence of laughter when solemnity has become unbearable. The freedom to squander an afternoon upon something useless and beautiful, to love without making love an obligation, to refuse without transforming refusal into a universal commandment. There is no sacred cause concealed beneath these desires. They belong to the individual before she has been recruited into anything.


 Stirner understood the quiet degradation of an existence surrendered to abstractions. Humanity, morality, society, the common good: how readily these exalted words become creditors, presenting their invoices to the individual and demanding payment in obedience. Even freedom may become an idol when it is transformed from something lived into something worshiped. The egoist does not escape possession merely by changing masters.


 And Novatore, that irreconcilable enemy of resignation, carried this refusal into the dangerous territory of poetry. His creative nothing was no impoverished emptiness. It was the absence of a sacred foundation, the opening through which the individual might create without first obtaining permission from God, humanity, or history. I have no desire to exchange one altar for another.


 There is something almost indecently beautiful in an existence that refuses to justify itself before the world. The individual is not a preliminary arrangement awaiting completion through society. She is not an instrument whose value must be demonstrated by usefulness. She is not raw material for the ambitions of institutions. She is already alive. And this is precisely why domination disgusts me.


 Not because I have constructed an immaculate moral universe in which authority has been assigned the role of evil, but because authority presumes to subordinate this irreducible existence to purposes that are not her own. It arrives with its classifications, its permissions, its solemn explanations of necessity, and expects the living person to recognize herself in the categories imposed upon her. I recognize no such obligation. My hostility begins with something I love.


 There is something vile in the bureaucratic management of human suffering. A person becomes ill. Pain enters the body with an intimacy no institution can share. The frightened hours belong to someone particular, with a history, a face, private affections, unfulfilled desires, and a thousand small attachments that make her existence unlike any other. Somewhere else, a calculation begins. Coverage. Authorization. Medical necessity. Contractual exclusion. Utilization management. The vocabulary grows progressively cleaner as the circumstances become more desperate. Then comes the word:

Denied.


 What an elegant little instrument of authority. Six letters that can be delivered without anger, without visible cruelty, without the inconvenience of looking into the face of the person who must endure the consequences. The decision may be accompanied by a courteous explanation. There may be an appeal. There may be another appeal. There may be a telephone number, an automated menu, a recorded assurance that the call is important. The individual is invited to participate in the administration of her own distress.


 Here is a form of domination that rarely needs to announce itself as such. Its power lies partly in its impersonality. Responsibility passes through departments and procedures until the person who suffers can scarcely identify anyone to whom her suffering might be addressed. No one need hate her. No one need even know her. The arrangement can …

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire (II): The Illusion of National Economics and the Polarization of Political Economy【葡月的错位（二）国民经济学的幻象与政治经济学的极化】【A commentary on the French riots between September and October】
content: This essay, titled The Dislocation of Vendémiaire, explores the theoretical and practical contradictions within contemporary capitalist society, using the socio-political unrest in France as a backdrop. Grounded in Marxist philosophy and dialectics, the author critically examines the illusion of national economics and the polarization of political economy. By distinguishing between "national economics" (which obscures exploitation through material comfort) and "political economy" (which reveals the deep alienation of social relations), the text argues that modern digital capitalism has stripped workers of their "wealth of real relations" (现实关系的财富). The essay articulates a fundamental shift from the "first struggle" (economic demands for wages and welfare) to the "second struggle" (reclaiming the autonomy of labor production and resisting the reduction of human beings to mere production factors). Ultimately, it posits that the recent French protests represent a historical "dislocation"—an attempt at the second struggle without the necessary political foundation of the first.

title: Пётр Кропоткин - В память о чикагских мучениках
content:
Автор

: Пётр Кропоткин

Название

: В память о чикагских мучениках

Дата

: декабрь 1892

Источник

: Freeom, №72


 В ПАМЯТЬ о ЧИКАГСКИХ МУЧЕНИКАХ


В Лондоне


Эта речь была опубликована в газете Freedom (№72, декабрь 1892). В ней Кропоткин в общих чертах обрисовывает как обоснованность анархистских теорий, так и необходимость их применения в рабочем движении. В оригинальной статье был также текст, не принадлежащий Кропоткину, здесь он не включен.


 П. Кропоткин: Мы не можем лучше почтить память наших братьев из Чикаго, чем бросив взгляд на прогресс идей, ради которых они жили и погибли, после того как их так жестоко пытали в течение 18 долгих месяцев американские грабители земли и денег.


 Зарождение Анархистской партии было очень скромным. Она родилась из протеста, который вскоре превратился в ожесточённую борьбу против власти, утвердившейся внутри Международного Товарищества Рабочих. Однако это скромное начало скрывало великий принцип – принцип отрицания власти вообще, во всех взаимоотношениях между членами Общества, и высокий идеал – идеал Общества, основанного на полной свободе личности и свободном обединениии свободных личностей, свободных групп и свободных федераций групп.


 Партия находила поддержку своим идеям во многих кругах. Она оказалась в согласии с великой работой – критикой власти, которая шла в недрах трудящихся классов. И она оказалась в согласии с мыслью, которая в последнее время занимала всё более и более заметное место в трудах современных философов.


 Идея росла; она находила поддержку и в философии, и в науке; она развивалась. И как бы мало ни было число анархистов, анархистская идея настолько соответствовала современному прогрессу мысли, что в этот момент мы можем сказать, что она УЖЕ глубоко изменила существующие представления по многим жизненно важным вопросам, связанным с великой борьбой за человеческое освобождение.


 Представления о соотношении ролей Эволюции и Революции в прогрессе человечества в последнее время полностью изменились. Ни один разумный человек теперь не может противопоставлять Эволюцию Революции – ведь очевидно, что обе являются лишь двумя аспектами одного и того же прогресса. Заторможенная Эволюция вызывает Революцию, а принципы, провозглашённые Революцией, применяются к жизни последующей Эволюцией. Даже некоторые видные дарвинисты теперь признают, что революции были необходимыми частями прошлой органической эволюции. Тем более в человеческой жизни: Революция является необходимой частью человеческой Эволюции.


 Представления о власти также чрезвычайно изменились. Доверие к ней быстро теряется. Если двадцать лет назад противников власти социал-демократы считали глупцами, то теперь те же самые социал-демократы вынуждены склоняться перед неуважением к власти, которое ощущается в их собственных рядах. Государственные социалисты теперь вынуждены отрекаться от государственного социализма – по крайней мере, в своих программах – и они вынуждены каждый день расставаться с той властью, которую раньше считали необходимым условием успеха Социализма. Социал-демократические группы требуют свободы для каждой из них, и бывшие автократические лидеры обязаны признавать эту автономию групп. Старый аргумент о том, что автономные группы уничтожат друг друга своими распрями, просто показался бы смехотворным, если бы его выкопали из социал-демократических газет двадцатилетней давности и принесли на сегодняшние трибуны.


 Вы все помните злосчастную воображаемую Коммуну из аргумента авторитаристов, которой отказывали в любой независимости на том основании, что она – как говорили наши противники – будет противиться любому прогрессу остальной нации. Как часто мы слышали об этой фальшивой Коммуне в наших дискуссиях! Теперь этот аргумент показался бы просто смехотворным. Самые авторитарные социалисты вынуждены вписывать муниципализацию собственности в свои программы и признавать свободную Коммуну необходимым основанием свободной нации.


 В экономике идея полной реконструкции всей системы производства стала общепринятой. Тот, кто стал бы теперь утверждать, что Социальная Революция должна просто состоять в том, чтобы каждый рабочий вернулся в свою мастерскую и там получил свою долю прибавочной стоимости – тот, кто повторил бы теперь эту формулу старого марксизма – просто показался бы призраком из прошлого. Зло, как мы все знаем, не в несправедливом распределении прибавочной стоимости, не в низкой заработной плате и не в продолжительном рабочем дне – а в самой системе наёмного труда, в …

author: Unknown
title: Philippe Chanial - Proudhon, Sociologist and Activist of the Autonomy of the Social
content:
Author

: Philippe Chanial

Title

: Proudhon, Sociologist and Activist of the Autonomy of the Social

Date

: 2017

Notes

: Translated by Shaun Murdock.

Source

: “Proudhon, sociologue et militant de l’autonomie du social” Revue de la Société P.-J. Proudhon, no. 3 (2017): 9–16. Source in French:

https://www.proudhon.net/philippe-chanial-proudhon-sociologue-et-militant-de-lautonomie-du-social/


 If Proudhon can and should be read as a forerunner of sociology, is it not above all because he was one of the first to have systematically hypothesised the autonomy of its very object, the “social”? As everyone knows, this hypothesis is foundational to sociology. The late Pierre Ansart reminded us that the heart of Proudhon’s sociological thesis is an “essential heterogeneity of the social relative to the individual”.

[1]

 Before him, the Durkheimian Célestin Bouglé emphasised that if Proudhon’s work pertains to sociological theory, it is because it shares the premise that “the meeting of individual entities generates an original reality, something greater than and different to their mere sum”. And, he continued, “arguably no thinker has made greater use of this premise than Proudhon” because “he constantly opposes, to purely individual phenomena, the notions of collective force, collective being and collective reason”.

[2]


 However, this theory of the irreducibility of the social – of the collective – to the individual does not exhaust this hypothesis of the autonomy of the social. It raises another question: that of the relationship between the social, the political and the economic. In the war of the sciences, sociology was only able to assert itself as an autonomous science by rejecting the self-proclaimed status of both political philosophy and political economy as the science of society.

[3]

 It did so by refusing that the mystery of the social order – the fact that there is, among or between people, something rather than nothing (chaos, arbitrary violence, war of all against all, etc.) or, to put it another way, the fact that people manage to give a lasting form to their coexistence – can be resolved either by identifying society with a system of power, as if the heteronomy of its political establishment, even if it were legitimate, were the absolute condition for the possibility of human coexistence; or by reducing it to a market, as if commercial ties alone were sufficient to make society. But is it not this double refusal that also defines the unique anarchism and socialism of Proudhon? Is is not this hypothesis of an autonomy of the social that enables both sociology as a scientific discipline, and socialism or anarchism as paths for emancipation?


 Let us therefore attempt to unravel some of the simultaneously sociological and normative questions raised by this Proudhonian plea for an autonomy of the social.


The irreducibility of the social to the political and the economic


 In his Carnets of 1852, Proudhon said: “I do politics to kill it. To put an end to politics.” This confession summarises, in a particularly polemical tone, his well-known critique of governmentalism. But this desire to end the “governmental bias” should not be reduced to a purely negative injunction to abolish all powers. It is also an invitation to accede to a “constitution of society” that is no longer based on the hierarchy of political powers but on the free organisation of social forces. It is in

Confessions of a Revolutionary

, written, as Pierre Ansart also recalled, “in a sort of anger after the failure of a hoped-for social revolution”

[4]

, that Proudhon makes this fundamental distinction:


 “In every society I find the distinction between two kinds of constitution, one of which I call the

social

 constitution and the other the

political

 constitution; the first, inherent to humanity, liberal, necessary, the development of which consists above all in weakening and gradually eliminating the second, which is essentially factitious, restrictive and transitory. The social constitution is nothing but the equilibrium of interests founded upon free

contract

 and the organisation of

economic forces

, which are in general: Labour, Division of Labour, Collective Force, Competition, Commerce, Money, Machines, Credit, Property, Equality in transactions, Reciprocity of guarantees, etc. The political constitution has

authority

 as its principle. Its forms are: Class Distinctions, Separation of Powers …

author: Majid00
title: روش‌های سازمان‌یابی کمونیستی
content:
This essay is the second part of The Dislocation of Vendémiaire, following Part I, “The Disruptors of the 21st Century and the Ideological Collusion.” While Part I interprets the 2026 France-centered student-led protest wave as a politically dislocated movement—one misread by mainstream discourse as a multi-class coalition when it is in fact an expression of fragmentation within the proletariat—Part II develops the theoretical argument behind that claim. Drawing on Marx’s thesis of society’s polarization into two hostile camps, it distinguishes between “property” and “proletarianization” in the sense of national economics and in the sense of political economy. The essay argues that class should be analyzed through the actual control over the production of labor-power, and that digital capitalism increasingly enables capital to dominate labor-power directly, beyond the mediation of formal ownership of physical means of production. On this basis, it explains why many who appear as middle-class or petty-producer subjects in national-economic terms—scholars, franchise shopkeepers, senior programmers, platform creators—are in political-economic terms being proletarianized, while carrying petty-bourgeois habits of political compromise, individualism, hostility to centralized discipline, and identity- or interest-based linkage. The result is a form of struggle that is radical in appearance but conservative and spontaneous in its core: it completes the first step of linkage through identity and affinity, but fails to return to the common ground of class interests and to connect with the broader industrial working class.

title: Исмет Нахмедов - Обращение к примерным гражданам своих стран
content:
Автор

: Исмет Нахмедов

Название

: Обращение к примерным гражданам своих стран

Дата

: 19/10/2026


 «Закон суров, но он закон».


 Я не интересуюсь политикой – зачем это мне? Думать своей головой мне ни к чему, ведь для этого у человека в двадцать первом веке есть правительство. А все мои мысли должны устремляться лишь к зарабатыванию денег. Рутина и серость – мой удел.


 Современные люди по всему миру должны во всём слушать государство и, если подвернётся возможность, отдать жизни за него. Не это ли является смыслом жизни маленького человека? Но государство нам ничего не должно, упаси боже! Каждый современный человек должен гордиться тем, что родился на определённой местности, а не по другую границу. Вот и мне повезло! Я ассоциирую себя лишь с одной страной, но не с одной определённой группой лиц. Я не отношу себя ни к одной из групп людей. Поэтому, если хоть кого-то когда-то и будут притеснять, то меня это никак не коснётся. Разве думают все эти люди о том, как тяжело мне живётся? Вот пусть и от меня не ждут жалости и понимания. Эмпатия – для слабаков!


 Если настанет день, когда затронут мои интересы? Так у меня и нет никаких интересов. Мне главное поспать, поесть, выпить на выходных, посплетничать с пацанами по телефону, взять новое пальто, купить авиабилет в соседнюю страну, восхищаться политиками и миллиардерами. И конечно любить свою страну. Но не её народ. А если вы вдруг ставите под сомнение то или иное решение свыше, то вы иностранный агент, вы шпион и предатель! С вами у меня нет ничего общего и быть не может.


 Потому что страной, нашей уж точно, управляют только непогрешимые люди: умнейшие и сильнейшие из нас. Сомневаться в верности принятых ими решений подобно вере в плоскую землю или отрицанию существования гравитации. Так что, не занимайтесь глупостями – не размышляйте и ничего не анализируйте. Всегда принимайте на веру то, что слышите из телевизора, в особенности, из государственных телеканалов, а также не забывайте подписываться на официальные местные новостные порталы в социальных сетях.

author: Dottie Rosenbaum
title: SNAP Participation Losses Far Exceed CBO’s Estimates
content:
About 5.5 million people lost food assistance through SNAP in the year since enactment of the 2025 reconciliation law.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

About 5.5 million people lost food assistance through SNAP in the year since enactment of the 2025 reconciliation law. This includes about 2 million children, who were not targeted by the law’s eligibility restrictions.

These participation declines have resulted in a sharp drop in SNAP spending, since 90 percent of SNAP spending is for food assistance benefits. (The rest is primarily administrative expenses and Puerto Rico’s nutrition assistance block grant.)

SNAP spending in fiscal year 2026, which ended September 30, was nearly $11 billion lower than the prior year (-10.3 percent). Along with the 5.5 million people who have less money to purchase groceries, this also means people in communities across the U.S. had about $11 billion less for spending on food in fiscal year 2026.

The drop in SNAP participation and spending is considerably more than the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) predicted. The latest U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) data for July 2026 show that monthly SNAP participation in fiscal year 2026 is on track to average about 4.5 million fewer people compared to the average month in fiscal year 2025 — far greater than CBO’s prediction of 2.8 million fewer people in an average month in 2026 versus 2025. (See chart.) CBO projected that SNAP outlays would drop by about $6 billion in 2026; in actuality SNAP outlays dropped by nearly double that amount.

The most likely reason for the larger-than-expected cut is the impact of the 2025 reconciliation law shifting enormous new SNAP costs to states, which they owe starting in fiscal year 2028. CBO estimated the cost shift mandate would have no impact until 2028. But it has already led many states to erect barriers to people’s SNAP participation, such as more paperwork and other requirements that states often don’t have the staff to administer.

The reconciliation law granted a few states a two-year delay for this harmful cost shift. Congress should extend the delay to all states before the end of the year, given SNAP losses outpacing predictions and the high cost of groceries and other basic needs. CBO estimated the reconciliation law would cut SNAP by $187 billion (about 20 percent) through 2034, the largest SNAP cut in history. With far steeper cuts evident in fiscal year 2026, Congress should not further cut SNAP to offset the cost of a delay in the cost shift.

In its most recent February 2026 baseline, CBO projected that 39.3 million people would participate in SNAP in an average month of 2026, compared to about 42.1 million in 2025. But just shy of 36.1 million people participated in SNAP in July 2026, according to the most recent data from USDA, suggesting that fiscal year 2026 participation will average about 37.6 million people, or about 4.5 million below last year’s average.

SNAP spending was also substantially lower than CBO’s forecast. CBO’s most recent baseline assumed a 6 percent drop in SNAP spending between fiscal years 2025 and 2026. But SNAP spending for the fiscal year was more than 10 percent, or nearly $11 billion, lower than it was in 2025.

The outsized drops suggest that people not ostensibly targeted by the 2025 reconciliation law’s eligibility restrictions are losing SNAP anyway. That includes many children, seniors, and people with disabilities, yet another reason for Congress to delay the cost shift.

At the time of the reconciliation law’s enactment, CBPP explained that, based on CBO’s estimate, once the law had fully taken effect about 4 million people would be cut from SNAP entirely or lose a substantial amount of their benefits. Now, with nearly a year of USDA data since the law’s enactment, more than 5.5 million fewer people receive any SNAP. That figure does not include people whose benefits are lower as a result of the new law. More losses are almost certain as the law continues to phase in.

That the losses are coming faster than CBO predicted is likely in large part because CBO’s original estimates did not factor in any effects of the state cost shift mandate until 2028. author: India McKinney
title: Computer Security Is About to Get a Lot Worse, Here’s What You Can Do
content:
It is a commonly held truth among computer geeks that there is no such thing as bug free software, or a secure computer. Any piece of software that anyone actually uses

will have a security vulnerability somewhere in the code

. The more complex that software is, the more likely there will be a vulnerability. Fortunately for everyone, finding severe vulnerabilities was generally considered an expensive and difficult task requiring years of training and deep knowledge of how computers and software worked. Until recently there was a steady background hum of vulnerabilities being found and patched, with major vulnerabilities that could cripple the entire internet only happening every few years. Now that is no longer the case. 

 


You may have noticed your nerdiest friends freaking out about the “Vulnerability Apocalypse” this week and waving their arms in panic about something called PHP. You may have also noticed that some of your favorite websites were down for a bit. In the last two weeks of October alone, there have been multiple, potentially internet-breaking vulnerabilities reported and patched. Many of those vulnerabilities were in the open-source software that is the foundation of the vast majority of the internet.


For more detailed information on what happened, and why supporting open-source projects matters, 

check out our other blog

.


This is all because frontier AI models, such as those created by OpenAI, Anthropic, and others, have made it incredibly cheap and easy to find previously unknown vulnerabilities (zero-days) in open- and closed-source code.

Three percent of all software vulnerabilities ever found in history were found just in the month of October. This year alone researchers have found nearly a quarter of all software security issues which have ever been discovered.

 


If exploiting critical software is now cheaper and easier than ever, what does that mean for us as individuals and what does that mean for society as a whole?

TL; DR

: It’s going to get worse before it gets better. But you can protect yourself with basic digital security hygiene that is now more important than ever. 

 


What Do I Need to Do?

 


There absolutely needs to be a bigger conversation about how we got here and how to fix the systemic issues involved, including how corporations that depend on open-source code should contribute to their upkeep, and how big tech should be regulated. 

 


But for now, this news is a compelling reason to tighten up your digital hygiene.

A lot of computers are going to get hacked a lot more often, and unfortunately, it isn’t going to get better any time soon.

Thankfully, EFF has compiled a comprehensive set of security advice in

our Surveillance Self-Defense guides

.


To start

,

we recommend making sure your browser and all applications are

always up to date

 with the latest patches.  

 


You should also consider installing a tracker blocking tool, like EFF’s

Privacy Badger (now on Safari),

 and remain vigilant for

phishing attempts

. Additionally,

install a password manager

 and

use unique passwords

 for each website, so that if one site is compromised, the rest of your passwords are safe. You should also be aware that

data breaches

 may now be more likely, and the websites you visit may experience more attacks than usual, which means that some services may be disrupted.

 


If you host a blog or other website, make sure that either you or your hosting provider has

patched

 this particular issue. 

 


For additional tips on protecting yourself and others, head over to our

Surveillance Self-Defense site

. Additionally, if you’d like to support any of EFF’s open-source projects like

Privacy Badger

,

Rayhunter

, and

Certbot

, visit our

donate page

.
