author: Unknown
title: Martin H. - Barry Pateman: An Appreciation
content:
Author

: Martin H.

Title

: Barry Pateman: An Appreciation

Date

: 2026-10-21

Notes

: [First posted on the Kate Sharpley Library website]

Source

: https://www.katesharpleylibrary.net/c2ft1b


 It’s important to appreciate those who have come before us. I first met Barry through Albert Meltzer, probably at a bookfair. I’d learned to trust that if Albert thought well of someone, he was probably right. Barry was an impressive man, physically and mentally, with the sort of self-deprecating humour instantly recognisable to anyone brought up in a British working class environment. And he was able to talk to people, without the sort of academic language that can be so off-putting.


 The times I saw him were few and far between but they were always memorable. Barry was brimming with ideas, whether about anarchist history, theory and practice, sport or wider culture. Like Albert he had a high regard for the autodidacts – especially those miner militants whose self-education far outstripped those who had had a university education. He was good company.


 It was perhaps telling that I learned of Barry’s death a few days after returning from Ron Marsden’s funeral. Both had been intimately involved in the tension between organising as anarchists and remaining accessible to ordinary people. It’s a tension that runs through most of the anarchist organising and groups that I have been part of in my life, and one I kept promising Barry I would write something about – the organisations that can never get above Dunbar’s number

[1]

 in membership without splitting, the affinity groups claiming to be membership organisations, the strategies designed for different times, the insights from Stuart Christie’s autobiography about affinity groups. Sorry, mate, life always seemed to get in the way, I am way too easily distracted….


 He was generous with his time and his thoughts. He had many strings to his bow – as you would expect from someone who admired those self-educated working class militants – as was so warmly described by the guy who knew him from the New Zealand Cricket Museum at the memorial service.


 Barry would regularly talk about how militant young miners from South Yorkshire were interested in the Direct Action Movement, during the height of the 1984–5 strike. But as they weren’t fully formed anarchists, DAM couldn’t accept them, despite their hard won experience of class struggle. It was this discussion that led DAM to become the Solidarity Federation (alongside other struggles like the Ardbride dispute 1986–87). Unfortunately, with a fabulous sense of timing, SF’s orientation towards labour movement militants happened at exactly the time the pool of labour movement militants shrank, following the catastrophic defeats of the 80s and early 90s. Barry saw the effects of these defeats first hand, as the mutual aid of the strike gave way to desperation and the destruction of former mining areas by a vengeful government. There were successes, most notably the Workmates group on the privatised part of the Tube, but that also swerved the same organisational question by staying independent – it wasn’t part of SF and as far as I know no one outside the originators ever joined SF. The arguments around SF’s industrial strategy, of building trust and organisation in a workplace and then tackling issues from that base are not new

[2]

 – but the obstacles to winning over new people to an anarcho-syndicalist project through this activity remain substantial.


 One of the commitments of the KSL has always been to uncover the motivations and actions of the unknown militants, who didn’t leave piles of writings for posterity. Barry was assertive that we hear the true voices of our forebears, not mediated by what we think now and what we want to bolster our own current views. We are much richer for that approach. The histories published by KSL are accessible to the general reader. The context is there. The achievements are many: Recognising the importance of Guillamon’s work on the Spanish revolution and ending the myth of the spontaneous uprising in 1936, achieved without any groundwork. And his work on the early 20

th

 century movement and Emma Goldman stands out.


 He kept looking for ways to spread the ideas of anarchism, and always in an outward-facing way. Whether through solidarity with strikers and others in struggle, through engaging with younger anarchists, or through the achievements of the Kate Sharpley Library he …

author: Kodao Productions
title: Sara’s impunity killed her case
content:
Can Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio still refuse to testify in her defense as the deluge of evidence requires her to take the witness and debunk what she insists are fabricated documents that prove her amassing enormous wealth even before she got married? Press releases do not win impeachment cases and not even the pompous statements of Malou Tiquia or the strained legal *legerdemain of Michael Wesley Poa could dent the facticity of the evidence laid down in open court.


The brutal truth is that her 16-member defense panel cannot act as her surrogate since not one of them is competent to answer the questions posed by the prosecution. They are lawyers but not one of them can claim that signatures were forged, or that bank accounts were opened in her name but without her knowledge. Only Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio can answer the prosecution’s queries. Legal doppelgangers are prohibited.


If Sara were the only competent witness to disprove or affirm the validity of bank accounts, manager’s checks, credit memos and other records, why can’t she be woman enough to take the cudgels for her own self and declare before the whole world that she is being persecuted and slapped with manufactured charges? The fact is, Sara always enjoyed Duterte’s impunity and practiced it, and no matter how many times the Commission on Audit (COA) questioned her disbursements as Davao City mayor, she made mincemeat of all of them.


Her playbook is copycat from Donald Trump, who learned it from Roy Cohn: Deny everything, do not pay, deflect and project all the crimes to the accusers and refuse to apologize. For all his mentoring of Trump, what Cohn got was a pair of “diamond” cuff links that turned out to be worthless **yags, or imitation diamond. Cohn died a lonely death, disbarred and forgotten, from the scourge of humanity called AIDS. Are we hearing that the 16 defense lawyers are not getting paid? Not yet, but with the impeachment case now down to Article II on ill-gotten wealth, maybe a discount is in order.


Sara is a businesswoman who even tried to do some catering for her own people in the course of the trial, charged to the Senate. A deadbeat VP? Not an impossibility. She can do a Trump, a confirmed grifter who never paid 3,500 contractors and forced them to file cases and get swamped with legal fees. She is indolent, which explains why she delegated the disbursements of her confidential funds to non-bonded military officers in violation of COA regulations. By doing so, she betrayed public trust and punished with double impeachment cases.


DepEd officials also confirmed that Sara was known better for being absent from the job and her rudderless leadership at the DepEd. And in the few times she ever visited schools, she had a dispute with walls decorated with educational materials, promoting the doctrine of high tech education. Sweden just threw away gadgets from classroom, and pupils will now have to work with paper and pencils, not tablets and laptops. That’s the culture of learning giving the prophets of high tech a whack on the chin.


Sara will not testify. Not because she is ***faineant, or work-shy, or indolent, or even a ham of an actress. Being asked questions by people she regards as her inferiors is beneath her dignity. During the congressional investigation, she even wanted former Rep. Stella Quimbo to be sacked as panel member, accused former ACT Teachers Rep. France Castro of being a convicted criminal and slammed others for persecuting her to thwart her march to Malacanang accompanied by the Richard Wagner’s “Ride of the Valkyries.”


By not testifying, she, in ham-fisted fashion, will simply rely on a forensic analyst to “destroy” the contention of Atty. Alex Cabrera about Sara’s conservatively estimated P818-million ill-gotten wealth from 2022 to 2025. Some of those approached to do the job purportedly rejected the overtures. Her hubris, her firm belief that she is above the law and destined to be president of this country through her corruption, sloth and ignorance should eventually convict her. To be honest,

binitbit lang siya ng tatay niya ngunit naniwalang kaya niyang maging pangulo. Mahirap mangarap nang gising kahit practitioner ka ng

 impunity. #

author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Ministério Público encurrala Meta para barrar bloqueios e restrições nas eleições
content:
Em dois movimentos distintos, um judicial e outro extrajudicial,

o Ministério Público Federal (MPF) quer barrar bloqueios, suspensões de contas e restrições de alcance promovidos pela Meta no Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp e Threads.


Na Justiça Federal do Rio Grande do Sul, o MPF ajuizou nesta quarta-feira, 21 de outubro, uma ação civil pública, com pedido de urgência. Em outra frente, a Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão (PFDC) enviou recomendação à Meta, cobrando providências imediatas.


A ação lida especificamente com as denúncias que fazem parte da representação feita pelas organizações Ctrl+Z, Artigo 19, Conectas e Sleeping Giants Brasil, que mostram que a Meta bloqueou conteúdos políticos pró-Lula e contra Flávio. A

Agência Pública


mostrou

 que além dos bloqueios,

a plataforma derrubou perfis com acusação de terrorismo e nudez, mesmo não havendo conteúdos nesse sentido.

 A Procuradoria pede o restabelecimento imediato de contas, páginas e conteúdos afetados pelas restrições apontadas na representação.


A ação pede ainda que a Justiça Federal proíba o uso exclusivo de algoritmos para decisões de bloqueio de conteúdo e que as futuras reavaliações e análises de recursos sejam conduzidas obrigatoriamente por equipes humanas especializadas

, com a fixação de multa diária de R$ 500 mil por conta afetada, em caso de descumprimento.


O MPF apurou que as restrições arbitrárias impostas pela companhia foram operadas por meio de algoritmos automatizados, sem notificação clara sobre as supostas violações ou oportunidade de contestação por canal efetivo com revisão humana. Essa prática provocou o enfraquecimento do engajamento de conteúdos cívicos e o cerceamento do debate democrático.


Ao público, no dia 16, a Meta

reconheceu

 que “a conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula foi desativada por engano por pouco mais de 1 hora”, mas afirmou que não se tratou de “razões políticas”.


Após pedir para ‘Flávio abrir o sigilo’, dona de comunidade é bloqueada pela Meta


Uma das vítimas das restrições foi a arquiteta Carolina Martins, 43, de Brasília. Ela criou um grupo e uma comunidade visando angariar apoio para a candidatura de Lula no segundo turno. O grupo chegou a ser derrubado, acusado de “terrorismo” sem fundamentação pela empresa. Ela teve a conta de WhatsApp derrubada e ainda está sofrendo outras restrições da Meta.


Ao divulgar esta semana a proposta do presidente Lula para que ambos os candidatos abram seu sigilo bancário, feita após o

debate

 da rede Bandeirantes,

Martins postou uma imagem que dizia “Flavio Abra o Sigilo”. Na segunda-feira, dia 19, ela foi suspensa pela Meta de postar links em suas publicações no Instagram até 16 de novembro sob a acusação de “práticas comerciais proibidas”.


Recomendação quer resposta da Meta em 48 horas


Já a recomendação, que é uma medida extrajudicial para uma empresa ou ente público realizar medidas para corrigir uma ilegalidade, foi expedida pela Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão, em Brasília, e direcionada diretamente à Meta para que a companhia adote medidas urgentes de transparência e proteção à liberdade de expressão nas redes Facebook, Instagram, Threads e WhatsApp durante o período eleitoral.


À empresa foi dado prazo de 48 horas para responder se acatará as recomendações do MPF e para detalhar as providências que serão adotadas durante o segundo turno das eleições, além de 30 dias para apresentar um relatório conclusivo.


A medida da PFDC vem depois da instauração de investigação no último dia 13 na qual o MPF pediu à Meta uma série de informações. A companhia enviou uma resposta ao MPF no dia 19 de outubro, complementada ontem, 20. 


Nas respostas, segundo a PFDC, a Meta teria alegado, em síntese, que a sua moderação se basearia nos Padrões da Comunidade e na legislação local, que não levaria em conta a orientação política ou ideológica dos usuários.


As respostas foram consideradas genéricas pelo MPF e não abordaram as moderações indevidas e não esclareceram caso a caso no que se baseou cada restrição, conforme demandado no ofício da semana passada.


A manifestação da Meta não mencionou as suspensões fundadas em enquadramentos graves (como terrorismo e abuso sexual), nem das remoções que teriam ocorrido após denúncias em massa. A recomendação à Meta é assinada pelo Procurador Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão, Paulo Thadeu Gomes da Silva, e mais cinco procuradores do MPF que atuam na área de direitos humanos.

author: Jéssica Ribeiro
title: Bet Blaze funcionou em endereço de empresas ligadas a Willer Tomaz, investigado pela PF
content:
Um relatório de análise da nuvem associada ao celular do advogado Willer Tomaz de Souza, produzido pela Polícia Federal (PF), revela que a Foggo Entertainment Ltda, empresa responsável pelas operações da plataforma de apostas Blaze no Brasil, utilizou o mesmo endereço comercial que já havia sido registrado anteriormente por empresas ligadas a Willer Tomaz e a seus ex-sócios. Tomaz ganhou manchetes de todo o país em agosto devido a seu processo contra a própria Blaze, tentando reaver R$ 163 milhões que teria apostado na plataforma, o que chamou a atenção da PF e do Ministério da Fazenda por suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro.


O imóvel localizado na Alameda Prudente de Moraes, nº 86, no bairro Mercês em Curitiba, consta nos registros cadastrais da Foggo Entertainment — CNPJ que recebeu transferências milionárias enviadas por Willer — e já havia sido sede da RioPag S/A, processadora de pagamentos de apostas da Loterj, além de outras sociedades vinculadas a um ex-sócio de Willer.


A análise do iCloud do aparelho celular e Willer Tomaz foi possível a partir de quebra de sigilo autorizada pela Justiça após operação de busca e apreensão contra o advogado e empresário no âmbito da

operação Sem Desconto, que investiga as fraudes no INSS

. A apuração da PF aponta que o advogado realizou diversas transferências bancárias fracionadas e sistemáticas de R$ 100 mil para a conta da Foggo Entertainment. Ao rastrear a estrutura societária e operacional da empresa de apostas, os investigadores identificaram a sobreposição de endereços entre a operadora da Blaze e a Riopag S.A.


Para os investigadores, a coincidência de endereços “reduz a força de uma leitura puramente casual e justifica aprofundar a investigação sobre eventuais vínculos societários, comerciais ou operacionais entre o investigado, antigos parceiros e a estrutura responsável pela atividade de apostas”.


Uma das suspeitas da PF é que a plataforma de apostas não fosse utilizada apenas para apostas recreativas, mas como meio de circulação intensiva, pulverização do dinheiro e eventual retorno de capital. A análise dos extratos de Willer Tomaz revelou movimentações diárias na plataforma que chegaram a superar R$ 35 milhões em dias específicos, acumulando registros contábeis de perdas na ordem de R$ 40,83 milhões entre junho e outubro de 2025.


Com o cruzamento do endereço em Curitiba e a identificação de saques em cassinos no exterior, as autoridades buscam determinar se as perdas registradas na conta de apostas eram efetivas ou se retornavam ao patrimônio do grupo por meio de estruturas empresariais interpostas.


Dinheiro que circula em várias etapas/empresas


Até o momento, o “

amigo advogado

” de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tem negado ser sócio ou acionista de várias empresas, inclusive as ligadas à operação de bets que funcionavam legalmente no estado do Rio de Janeiro até a primeira semana de outubro. No entanto, um email extraído do iCloud do aparelho celular do empresário, enviado pelo próprio Willer Tomaz para a instituição Magnum Bank, indicam, segundo a PF, “o controle ou vínculo de fato” de Tomaz sobre uma longa lista de empreendimentos, incluindo a RioPag S/A, que opera o meio de pagamento de prêmios da Loterj desde 2023.


Na mensagem em questão, Willer “declara ser sócio ou acionista” de uma lista de companhias, incluindo Rio Pag S/A e Embrasis. “Inclusive daquelas em que seu nome não consta formalmente do quadro societário”, escreve a PF.


Materiais obtidos pela

Agência Pública

 e o relatório da PF ajudam a desenhar a estrutura entre as companhias ligadas à RioPag até chegar a Tomaz, um arranjo que envolve empresas atualmente registradas no Distrito Federal e no Rio de Janeiro.


Certidões emitidas pelas Juntas Comerciais do Distrito Federal e do Rio de Janeiro mostram que a RioPag tem uma única acionista, uma empresa atualmente chamada Capital Pretium S/A (antes chamada de Pixs Holding SA). Por sua vez, a Capital Pretium também possui apenas uma sócia, a Empresa Brasileira de Sistemas de Computação (Embrasis S/A). Até 6 de outubro de 2026, quando houve alteração de diretoria e do estatuto social da empresa, os dois únicos acionistas da Embrasis S/A eram Willer Tomaz (82,5%) e sua irmã, Christine Tomaz de Souza (17,5%).


Oficialmente, o advogado amigo de Flávio Bolsonaro não exerceu papel de gestão ou direção em nenhuma delas. A PF conseguiu estimar o fluxo financeiro entre a teia de empresas até que o dinheiro chegasse a Willer Tomaz. Segundo a …

author: Thorin Klosowski
title: Introducing Our New Surveillance Self-Defense Guide: Online Privacy for Parents and Youth
content:
The internet is a vast and confusing place no matter your age. Trying to help youth engage with it safely and privately is a complicated topic that touches on many different skillsets and ideas. But just because it’s complicated doesn’t mean it’s impossible. We’ve launched our

Online Privacy for Parents and Youth

 Surveillance Self-Defense guide in hopes to provide a framework for finding solutions that work for you. 


EFF rolls out this crucial resource as state and local governments consider

ill-advised laws

 that cut young people off from essential information and experiences. This particularly harms vulnerable youth and marginalized groups who often find safety in supportive online communities they can't access offline. Such laws also entail age gating, which compromises the privacy of all internet users and stifles young users’ ability to

learn, grow

, and

express themselves

.


Young people have unique needs and those needs change over time. Trying to protect from everything all the time is an exhausting process, but the security community has long had a solution for this:

security planning

 (also called threat modeling). The idea is to provide a series of questions designed to help you focus on what’s truly important. When it comes to online privacy, this is as applicable for youth and parents as it is for anyone else. 


We used a security plan as our foundation for this guide because deciding what is and isn’t important is the first step we should all take when assessing our privacy risks. But this isn’t a place for quick fixes, and every young person has their unique needs and considerations. There is no single tool or technology fix that can substitute for spending time learning, and then teaching a young person, how the internet works, how to use it, what sorts of harms exist, and how to navigate those harms.


Solutions are rarely about the tools or software you use. It’s about understanding the threats and concerns you have, and then determining what steps you can take to mitigate those risks. We hope our

Online Privacy for Parents and Youth

 guide can help provide the outline to get the conversation started.

author: thecollective
title: Getting Involved
content:
Getting Involved


In this time of reduced anarchist projects, we’re seeing if there’s energy for us to expand a little. So this is us officially opening up to folks who want to be involved. Here are some of the projects that would be fun and simple to engage in. A list of more-involved options follows.


1. Writing one, or some, opinion pieces for the podcast. You can read it yourself or have one of our regular voices read it for you.

2. Writing a, or some,

Topic of the Week prompts

.

3. Re-starting the ANews weekly digest (ATUBES) for printing out, leaving about, starting conversations with new people.

4. Recording readings from The Anarchist Library for possible airing on the ANews podcast.

5. Signing up to be one of the weekly conversants for the Topic of the Week prompt featured on the ANews Podcast.

If any of these appeal to you, get in touch via emai at: thecollective at anarchistnews dot org


For the future, maybe. (If there is one!)


We’d like to have a radio project. Imagine 24/7 radio stream that is at times live on air and at other times recorded. This would take probably at least a couple people who are consistent and dedicated. Is that you and a friend? You and an interesting enemy? You and a friend and an interesting enemy? Let us know!

 


We'd like to have more regular feedback and report backs from the various events that anarchists attend and/or organize. Finding and encouraging these report backs would be a potentially easy starting project that could get more involved as it goes along, or just remains checking in with folks you know to give us their (un)biased opinions on what went down, or didn't.

author: Rory Mir
title: Interoperability vs. Security: Why not both?
content:
An open internet where people can freely build, share, and remix each other's work is a powerful engine of grassroots innovation we’ve all benefited from. In recent decades, however, corporations have taken control of an increasing share of this work, giving them a greater ability to stifle challengers and limit our choices. When regulators address this by mandating that  tech giants play fair by requiring interoperability, the gatekeepers respond with a tired refrain: Playing fair puts users’ security at risk.


Unfortunately for these trillion-dollar companies, this

gotcha

 isn’t the end of the conversation. Regulators can ensure that meaningful choice

and

 security thrive.


Lawmakers have been catching up, recognizing that the best way to rein in big tech is to require these

oligopolies

 to open up their platforms to independent developers. As we

explained six years ago

, mandating interoperability helps prevent the misuse of people’s data and enables more privacy-respecting alternatives. Tech giants, in contrast, have been arguing that our data is safer when they have exclusive control.


Tech Giants Claim Interoperability Means Insecurity


The European Union’s

Digital Markets Act

 (DMA) put interoperability into law under Article 6(7): “gatekeeper shall allow providers of services and providers of hardware, free of charge, effective interoperability with” a designated

Core Platform Service

 they operate. The language describes an unambiguous requirement to remediate vendor lockouts and anti-competitive behavior of the major service operators—it is not optional.


Apple

claimed

 that enforcing this obligation in mobile app stores would put their customers at risk and do irreparable harm to trust in their brand. It’s an argument reminiscent of Apple’s fight against the

right to repair

, and in both instances the company is fighting to maintain its restrictive ecosystem to stop people from finding better deals elsewhere. Apple has long cultivated a more corporate-controlled experience with the iPhone, but this argument is now also being used for the relatively-more-open Android devices from Google.


In the same year Apple argued against the DMA, Epic Games

sued Google

 for its restrictive terms of service and extractive policies for revenue generated in apps. Google predictably

alleged

 that opening up its platform to other app stores it couldn’t vet would allow harmful apps to be installed. The case was ultimately decided this year in the U.S. federal appeals court for the Ninth Circuit, with the court rejecting this argument, dealing a blow to  Google’s

feudal security

 arrangement, and paving the way for

third-party app stores to be delivered as apps via the Google Play Store

.


Interoperating Secure Systems Can (and Should) Exist


Policymakers cannot take tech giants’ claims at face value. Companies have every incentive to resist interoperability requirements, because interoperability lowers practical barriers and reduces

switching costs

 for consumers adopting competing services. 


Even where companies offer credible claims from internal technical and security experts, independent experts rarely have the access and information they need to test those claims. Companies have

selectively made arguments

 that security is harmed by interoperability, often in contexts which are to their advantage. These companies are happy to let a general misconception flourish which frames security as

inherently opposed

 to interoperability.


This narrative is wrong. We’ve seen that when interoperability and information security are both set as essential and non-negotiable criteria, secure interoperable systems result—systems that don’t sacrifice the rich features we’ve come to expect of the services we rely on. 


The cross-platform rollout of

Rich Communication Services

 (RCS), and now

Message Layer Security

 (MLS) on top of it is a perfect example of this, creating end-to-end secure messaging by default between Android and iOS. For RCS and MLS, Google was conveniently on the other side of the interoperability argument,

campaigning Apple to adopt the standard

 to overcome the diminished “green bubble” experience iPhone users had when texting non-iPhone users. Once

Apple finally agreed

 to interoperate by implementing common standards, all users benefited from improved messaging security. In cases where legitimate security concerns are raised, these can be assessed and remedied on a …

author: Veridiana Alimonti
title: EFF to Brazil’s ANPD: Data Privacy and Free Expression Must Underpin Platform Regulations
content:
The Brazilian National Data Protection Agency (ANPD) plays a pivotal role in the regulation of digital platforms according to new legislation approved in Brazil. Throughout this year, EFF has presented comments, filed submissions, and met with the agency to emphasize crucial guardrails that the enforcement of new regulations should ensure.

 


ANPD is responsible for detailing and applying obligations set in Law n. 15.211/2025, which established rules for the protection of children and adolescents in the digital space. While some provisions establish important privacy safeguards, like prohibiting advertising based on profiling of underage users, the law created mandatory age assurance mechanisms for accessing digital products and services.

 


We have

raised alarms

 on the privacy and free expression issues around age-gating the internet.

Age verification technology is often

inaccurate

 and

privacy-invasive

.

Examples also show

 how it’s prone to enforcement overreach, resulting in sites blocked beyond legal requirements. In the UK, providers disproportionately restricted

several

 counseling, support and mental health sites under the Online Safety Act. Current age assurance methods risk wrongly walling off adults with

no valid IDs

,

facial differences

,

physical disabilities

, among others.

 


We highlighted these concerns in our

comments

 and

submissions


underscoring that ANPD should avoid a blanket approach to age assurance obligations. Following the legislation, restrictions should apply only to products and services that are inadequate or prohibited to children and adolescents according to categories already set in regulation, with robust protections against subjective and overbroad interpretations. Guarantees such as access to information, freedom to participate in society and meaningful access to technologies also compound what constitutes the best interests of the child. 

 


Moreover, we stressed that

zero knowledge proofs

 alone fail to ensure strong user privacy, including safeguards that the law itself sought to secure. Our submission explains why other requirements, such as

unlinkability, selective disclosure, batch issuance

 and processing on device, are crucial for achieving greater levels of protection and mitigating privacy harms. Minimum information being shared to the verifier and

no “phoning home”

 to the issuer of a user’s accepted credentials are conditions that prevent actions like collusion and data sharing about the user.

 


We also shared

inputs

 about the scope of the law, asking more clarity on which providers are covered by its obligations and the importance of treating differently non-dominant players like federated networks and free software applications. Without that clarity, this could negatively impact beyond gaming and major platforms that are the main target of these regulations. We elaborated on the agency’s regulation of prevention duties, the relevance of modulating them according to the type and structure of providers, and alerted them that their interpretation should not result in general monitoring obligations.

 


On another but related front, we sent

comments

 regarding Brazil’s

new internet intermediary rules

. Here too, ANPD has a critical regulatory role after a

Supreme Court’s decision

 and presidential decrees changed the liability regime initially set in the law known as “Marco Civil.” 

 


With the turn to notice and takedown mechanisms and duty of care obligations, we emphasized measures to prevent censorship of protected content. These involve ensuring solid means for appeals of restricted posts, avoiding overreliance on

AI-based content moderation

, strictly tailoring the application of concepts like duty of care and systemic failure, and not normalizing the blocking of platforms and websites. 

 


We raised concerns about a trend reflected in the new regulation requiring platforms to proactively report user to authorities with unclear guarantees. Finally, we urged the agency to advance essential transparency and accountability measures for enabling greater public oversight over the application of the new regime.

 


As we

said

 before, platform accountability under the new rules ultimately hinges on how accountable its enforcement will be by platforms and state institutions. Rigorous commitment to fundamental rights, including freedom of expression, privacy and data protection, is required so that intended …

author: Andrés
title: “Justicia es que no vuelva a pasar”: el juicio por el triple lesbicidio de Barracas se acerca a su final
content:
Foto: Sol Erazo


El juicio por el triple lesbicidio de Barracas se acerca al final y convocan a seguir las audiencias. El 6 de mayo de 2024 Justo Fernando Barrientos lanzó un explosivo a la habitación de Barracas donde dormían dos parejas de mujeres lesbianas: Pamela Cobas, Roxana Figueroa, Andrea Amarante y Sofía Castro Riglos. Sofía es la única que sobrevivió. La causa judicial derivada de ese ataque lesboodiante y misógino llegó a Tribunales el pasado 18 de mayo caratulado como “homicidio”. Fue por  impulso de las querellas que ahora se juzga más precisamente como lo que fue: un triple asesinato cometido por el “odio a la orientación sexual de las víctimas, mediando violencia de género”.

Por Sol Tobia, para ANRed. 


Ahora el juicio está por llegar a su fin.

El jueves 15 de octubre declaró el lesbofemicida y restan tres audiencias de alegatos. El lunes 26, protagonizada por las representantes de las víctimas; el miércoles 28, con declaración de la querella colectiva que impulsó la FALGBT, y la tercera con fecha a definir, donde se presentará la defensa del asesino.

 Después, los jueces darán su veredicto y la expectativa es que dicten prisión perpetua. “Sin embargo, más allá de la pena en números, lo que está en juego acá es que se consideren los agravantes por odio a la orientación sexual y por razón de género, además de la alevosía”, explica

Miriam Djeordjian, integrante de la Coordinadora Lesbicidios Nunca Más.


“Se demostró que hubo premeditación para lanzar el artefacto incendiario, que aparentemente fue algún tipo de pintura con un acelerante, y

la saña con la que el agresor, después de arrojar el objeto, bloqueó la puerta para evitar que las compañeras pudieran escapar. Las golpeó para que volvieran a quedar encerradas, y trabó la puerta.

Si no hubiera sido por la intervención de los vecinos, no hubieran ni siquiera logrado salir de la pieza”.


La Coordinadora que integra Djeordjian se formó poco antes del comienzo del juicio y, desde entonces, las mujeres que la integran

concentraron frente al Palacio de Tribunales durante cada audiencia

y realizaron otras actividades de visibilización, tales como llevar la causa al reciente Encuentro Plurinacional que se hizo en Córdoba

. Una de sus principales consignas es que este crimen de odio no se repita más, entendiendo que

 justicia es que no vuelva a pasar

”, detalla la activista.


Foto: Miriam Djordjian


El triple lesbicidio en contexto: misoginia, lesboodio y precarización


Los crímenes como el triple lesbicidio nunca son casos aislados. La misoginia propia de la cultura patriarcal se materializa, entre muchas otras maneras, en los femicidios que los hombres cometen todos los días, y suele tener un agregado específico contra las lesbianas: el odio que despierta en los agresores el hecho de que las mujeres rechacemos el mandato de la heterosexualidad, pilar fundamental del patriarcado.


“

Existió otro ataque en Cañuelas, unos seis o siete meses después

”, recuerda Miriam. Se refiere a lo ocurrido el 29 de enero de 2025, cuando

Orlando Alcides Lutz Fogar, “un nazi que venía amenazando a dos madres lesbianas con una niña”, terminó incendiándoles la casa.

Aquel día “ellas, por sentir miedo, decidieron no pasar la noche en la casa y por eso salvaron su vida”, recuerda la activista y añade que

el juicio por este otro caso está por comenzar en La Plata.


Destaca también

 el asesinato de la Pepa Gaitán en Córdoba, en 2010.

Entonces “no existían en el Código Penal las agravantes que hoy sí existen. El padrastro de su novia, 

Daniel Torres, que la fusila con varios disparos a corta distancia, fue condenado a 14 años de prisión, de los cuales terminó cumpliendo solo ocho, y hoy está libre”. A continuación, menciona

 “el ataque que sufrió Higui”, quien estuvo presa por defenderse de “una violación correctiva”,

 y salió en libertad gracias a la lucha de las organizaciones que la acompañaron.


Sofía Castro Riglos, única sobreviviente de la masacre lesboodiante, presenciando la audiencia virtual de la defensa del asesino frente a Palacio de Tribunales el pasado 15 de octubre. Foto: Sol Erazo


El anhelo de quienes integran la Coordinadora es que el triple lesbicidio de Barracas se reconozca como parte de un continuo de violencia lesboodiante, sirviendo además para el futuro: “

Se pretende sentar antecedentes judiciales que puedan servir de jurisprudencia, inspirar fallos

. Ojalá que no sean necesarios, pero que se pueda nombrar, porque lo que …

title: Smart işçileri sesini duyurmak için Meclis'e doğru yola çıktı
content:
İzmir - Smart Solar Aliağa’da atılan 83 işçinin geri alınması ve enflasyon zamlarının verilmesi için başlatılan direniş 16. gününde devam ediyor. Gece vardiyası giriş ve çıkışında işçiler sloganlarla halaylarla atılan işçileri Ankara’ya uğurladı.

İşçiler fabrikadan “Atılan işçiler geri alınsın”, “Ölmek var dönmek yok”, “Birleşe birleşe kazanacağız” sloganları ile çıkış yaptı. Fabrika önünden, meydanlardan, meclisten her yerden sesimizi duyurmaya, haklılığımızı göstermeye devam edeceğiz diyen işçiler mücadelenin süreceğini yineledi.

Atılan işçileri meclis basın toplantısına uğurlarken “Emek Partisi’nin davetiyle gerçekleştireceğimiz bu basın toplantısına diğer siyasi parti temsilcilerinden ve emekten yana tüm güçlerden destek bekliyoruz” dedi.

İşçiler sloganlarla, halaylarla ve meşalelerle arkadaşlarını yolcu ettikten sonra çadırda direniş devam etti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Alevi Bektaşi Federasyonu'ndan Kıraç Cemevi için tahliye tepkisi: Alevi toplumunun bu tahliye kararına rızası yoktur
content:
Alevi Bektaşi Federasyonu, İstanbul Esenyurt’un Kıraç semtindeki Kıraç Cemevi’ne yönelik tahliye sürecine tepki gösterdi. Federasyon, cemevinin halkın emeğiyle var edildiğini belirterek, "Alevi toplumunun bu tahliye kararına rızası yoktur. Alevilerin ibadethanelerine antidemokratik kararlarla kayyım atamaktan vazgeçin. Cemevlerimiz ticarethane değildir" açıklamasını yaptı.

Alevi Bektaşi Federasyonu, Kıraç Cemevi’ne yönelik tahliye süreci hakkında yazılı açıklama yayımladı. Açıklamada şu ifadelere yer verildi:

"İstanbul Esenyurt ilçesinin Kıraç semtinde bulunan Kıraç Cemevimize yönelik başlatılan tahliye ve gasp sürecini büyük bir endişe, öfke ve kararlılıkla yakından takip ediyoruz. İnancımızın en temel ilkesi olan rızalık esasını yok sayan, toplumsal barışı ve inanç özgürlüğümüzü hedef alan hiçbir dayatmayı kabul etmiyoruz. Bu cemevini var eden; taşına, toprağına emeğini veren, lokmasını paylaşan, çerağını uyandıran, cemini yürüten, hizmetini gören Kıraç halkıdır. O bölgede yaşayan canların rızası olmadan yürütülen hiçbir hizmetin Hak katında da toplum vicdanında da karşılığı yoktur, olamaz. Alevilerin inançsal ve toplumsal sorunları, kamu zoruyla ve devlet mahkemelerinin koridorlarında değil, yüzyıllardır süregelen tarihsel ilkelerimiz ve Alevi hukuku temelinde çözüme kavuşturulmak zorundadır.

Kamu gücünü arkasına alarak atılan her hukuk dışı adım, yalnızca toplumsal huzursuzluğu tırmandırmakla kalmayacak, Yol'a ve adalete olan inancı da derinden sarsacaktır. Cemevleri, resmi evraklarda hangi kurumun üzerinde görünürse görünsün taşını döşeyen, kapısını açan, aşını pişiren Alevi toplumunun öz mülküdür. Alevilerin binbir emekle, helal lokmayla ve alın teriyle var ettiği cemevlerimizin geleceği kamu gücünü arkasına alan vakıfların, bürokratik makamların, mahkeme kararlarının ya da herhangi bir kişinin tasarrufuna bırakılamaz. İbadethanelerimiz rantın, tahakkümün ve siyasi hesapların alanı değildir.

Kıraç halkının büyük özverisi ve gönüllü hizmetleriyle bugüne taşınan Kıraç Cemevi, halkın iradesi ve rızası dışında, başka hiçbir kuruma devredilemez. Alevi toplumunun bu tahliye kararına rızası yoktur. Bu vahim hatadan derhal dönülmelidir. İnancımızı, birliğimizi ve ibadethanemizi kirli çatışmaların içine çekmeye çalışanlara açıkça sesleniyoruz: Alevilerin ibadethanelerine antidemokratik kararlarla kayyım atamaktan vazgeçin. Cemevlerimiz ticarethane değildir. İnancımız pazarlık konusu yapılamaz. Yolumuza, erkanımıza mekanımıza ve geleceğimize sahip çıkacak, halkın rızalığı olmayan hiçbir dayatmaya boyun eğmeyeceğiz."

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Arezu Fayyazi
title: Domestic Violence and Femicide in Afghanistan: Women Are Denied Protection and Justice
content:
Domestic violence has intensified under Taliban rule since August 2021, as the regime has imposed more than 160 edicts and directives restricting the rights and freedoms of women and girls. By barring women from education and employment, severely limiting their freedom of movement, and denying them meaningful access to justice, the Taliban has deepened women’s dependence on their families and left many with fewer ways to escape abuse or seek protection. In this climate of systemic oppression and impunity, domestic violence can go unchallenged, while women and girls face the devastating risk of femicide.

Reports from The Guardian and Zan Times have recorded 231 cases of femicide across just ten provinces -there are 34 provinces – in Afghanistan since 2021. However, it is important to note that these reports emphasized the fact that these cases of femicide do not represent all of the cases in the country since 2021, given the fact that it’s difficult to record these instances of domestic violence after the Taliban has removed avenues to report these crimes.

The Taliban has dismantled the Ministry of Women’s Affairs, the prosecutor’s office that handled violence against women, and women’s shelters all together. Additionally, women judges and men judges that were trained on domestic violence issues and supported women, have all been removed. With the Taliban’s return to power, roughly 250 female judges lost their jobs and were banned from practicing. All those positions were filled with Taliban members, most of whom have no official training in law. The complete dismantling of all legal protections for women in Afghanistan has contributed to the increased rates of domestic violence in addition to a lack of legal accountability for men who commit domestic violence.

Even worse, the victims of just the recorded cases ranged from 5 to 65. Of these 231 cases, only 58 cases resulted in arrests of the suspect committing violence, only roughly 25% of cases. The lack of accountability for domestic violence is reinforced by the Taliban’s astonishing new Criminal Procedure Regulation of the Courts released in February 2026. In these regulations, it “allows husbands to physically punish their wives as long as the violence does not result in ‘broken bones or serious visible injuries.’” This regulation is evidence of the Taliban’s disregard for the rights, safety, and wellbeing of women. This new regulation just allows domestic violence to occur with no repercussions, and women are left paying the consequences with their dignity and lives. Liza Shams, a victim of domestic violence, passed away after going to the hospital for “being severely beaten” with “multiple fractures to her facial bones.”

The systematic oppression of women has left a huge burden on Afghan women not just physically, but also mentally and emotionally. With the lack of support or possibility to leave a relationship of domestic violence, there has been an increase in suicide due to psychological pressure. According to data from the UN, 7 in 10 women “describe their mental health as ‘bad’ or ‘very bad.’” Hasina, a young woman who was just 22 years old, took her own life after experiencing domestic violence from her husband and his family. Her uncle spoke out and said her death was “a killing caused by violence and oppression, even if the final act was carried out by her own hand.” He goes on to say “at such a young age, she had already gone through so much. She should have been studying, growing and preparing for a brighter future. Instead, she found herself in circumstances where, from her perspective, ending her life appeared to be the only escape.”

There is enough evidence to demonstrate that domestic violence is not just a household issue, but one compounded by a political system that strips women of their autonomy, protections, and opportunities. When women are banned from going to school, earning an income, seeking justice, or becoming independent – escaping an abusive situation is incredibly difficult. The consequences leave women isolated, psychologically distressed, and in the most tragic cases – dead.

Afghan women have repeatedly made clear that they deserve more than expressions of international concern. Their suffering must not remain hidden behind the closed doors of abusive households and be further obscured by the Taliban’s systematic efforts to erase women from public life and silence their voices. Without access to legal protection, education …

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 21 octobre
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 21 octobre, comme toutes les autres, sert à se nourrir des luttes passées pour comprendre celles que nous menons au présent et au futur. L'Histoire est une matière qui peut être modelée, alors souvenons-nous de notre histoire, ou de nos histoires.


1894 :

 Révolte des forçats du bagne des Îles du Salut : "

En septembre 1894, au bagne des Îles du Salut, un surveillant tue le forçat anarchiste François Briens. Celui-ci déclare, avant de mourir :"Je meurs pour l'anarchie, les anarchistes me vengeront".


Le 21 octobre 1894, le surveillant est tué à son tour, à coup de poignard, ainsi que trois autres gardiens. La révolte se propage, mais la répression ne tarde pas. Le lendemain, 22 octobre 1894, 11 forçats seront tués dont des anarchistes connus comme Jules Léauthier, Pierre Meyrveis, Benoît Chevenet, Simon (dit Biscuit), réfugié dans un arbre, abattu après avoir crié "Vive l'anarchie". Edouard Marpeaux, sera tué au matin du 23 octobre

".


Repris de l'éphéméride anarchiste.


1902 :

 Aux USA, une grève de mineurs prend fin après cinq mois de mobilisation.


1928 :

 Naissance à Milan de Giuseppe Pinelli, cheminot anarchiste qui sera accusé en décembre 1969 d'avoir posé la bombe de Piazza Fontana, qui avait en réalité été placée par un groupe néofasciste. Pinelli mourra jeté par la fenêtre du commissariat de Milan, le 15 décembre 1969.


1964 :

 A Copenhague, une bombe explose dans l'ambassade espagnole pour lutter contre la dictature franquiste. La FIJL et le groupe anarchiste Primero de Mayo sont derrière tout ça.


1967 :

 A Washington, plus de 100.000 personnes participent à une marche contre la guerre du Vietnam. Celle-ci sera suivie d'une marche sur le Pentagone, où de durs affrontements auront lieu contre la garde nationale.


1970 :

 En Argentine, les FAR (

Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias

) incendient un patrouille de police à l'aide d'un lance-flammes.


1972 :

 - Dans la banlieue de Barcelone, le Mouvement Ibérique de Libération (MIL, entre anarchisme et conseillisme) braque la Caisse d'Epargne de Mataro et repart avec un million de pesetas, qui serviront à alimenter une imprimerie clandestine.


 A Latina, des explosifs sautent sur les marches du Palais de Justice.

 A Roccella Jonica en Calabre, deux répétiteurs téléphoniques sont endommagés par des explosifs.


1976 :

 A Rennes, le Front de Libération de la Bretagne/Armée Révolutionnaire Bretonne (FLB/ARB) fait sauter une bombe au centre des impôts.


1977 :

 - A Paris, plusieurs manifestations de soutien à la Fraction Armée Rouge (RAF) ont lieu suite à la mort

quelques jours plus tôt

 de plusieurs de ses militants en prison. Le soir, des groupes autonomes incendient des bus de tourisme allemands. Enormément d'actions ont eu lieu les jours précédents (

19

 et

20

 octobre).


 A Trento, un concessionnaire Volkswagen est attaqué au cocktail molotov. Dans l'après-midi, un bus de touristes allemands est incendié dans le centre-ville.

 A Vicenza, une bombe fait sauter les locaux du concessionnaire Mercedes, tandis qu'un magasin de Volkswagen est attaqué de 3 molotov.

 A San Sebastian/Donostia, un groupe anarchiste fait sauter deux bombes contre le consulat d'Allemagne de l'Ouest.

 Les NAPAP (Noyaux Armés Pour l'Autonomie Populaire) font sauter un hangar Mercedes dans la nuit.


1979 :

 Dans l'Aude, en Haute-Garonne et dans l'Hérault, trois futurs pylônes de THT sont endommagés par des charges d'explosif (à La Gaudière, Lanta et Saint-Gélydu-Fesc).


1992 :

 A Bangor en Irlande du Nord, l'IRA fait sauter une grosse bombe dans une des rues principales, causant de gros dégâts alentours. La rue avait été évacuée avant explosion.

title: Buchlesung: Land und Freiheit von Aurélien Berlan
content:
Warum und wie sollen wir uns gegen ein System auflehnen, das Freiheit verspricht, von dem wir aber für den eigenen Lebensunterhalt abhängig sind?


Dieser Frage geht Aurélien Berlan in seinem Buch nach. Dafür kritisiert und analysiert er den kapitalistischen Freiheitsbegriff und stellt diesem ein Verständnis von Freiheit als kollektive Autonomie gegenüber.


Kollektive Autonomie bedeutet u.a., asymmetrische Abhängigkeiten abzulehnen, sich vom blinden Glauben an technische Problemlösungen zu befreien und das eigene Leben möglichst mit den Ressourcen der eigenen Region zu gestalten.


Aurélien Berlan ist Philosoph, Gärtner und Teil der „Soulèvements de la Terre“-Bewegung. Er hat sich in den vergangenen zehn Jahren mit Digitalisierung und der ZAD-Bewegung auseinandergesetzt.


Kurzweilig und auf Deutsch liest Aurélien aus seinem nun auf Deutsch herausgegebenen Buch „Land und Freiheit“.

author: Andrea DiP
title: Que a injustiça não te entristeça, que te radicalize
content:
Cerca de 500 mil pessoas foram às ruas em protestos na França nos últimos dias, em atos que começaram pedindo reformas no sistema educacional e evoluíram para reivindicações sociais mais amplas, que já influenciam outros países da Europa.


Os protestos começaram em setembro, quando estudantes bloquearam o acesso a uma escola na região de Paris para exigir mais recursos para a educação. Rapidamente, alunos de outras escolas aderiram, e as manifestações se espalharam pelo país, reivindicando mais professores, mais recursos e a melhora da estrutura dos prédios.

A demanda escalou, e se transformou na manifestação de uma insatisfação generalizada com o alto custo de vida, a queda na qualidade dos serviços públicos e com o governo.


O governo tem falado em atos de violência, depredação de patrimônio e incêndios. As autoridades francesas detiveram mais de 6,8 mil pessoas – mais de 5 mil menores de idade.


As manifestações inspiraram levantes na Itália, Albânia e Portugal.


Na Grécia, os estudantes reclamam do custo de vida e do aumento de mensalidades e taxas. Na Espanha, professores exigem melhores salários. Na Albânia, estudantes protestam contra as condições nas universidades, os custos do ensino superior e a falta de apoio financeiro. Em Portugal, a demanda é também por custos mais baixos de taxas nas universidades. 


Na Argentina, milhares de estudantes e professores foram às ruas na última quinta-feira, 15 de outubro, em protesto contra o governo de Javier Milei.


Essa onda de protestos também tem sua contrapartida no Brasil. “Estamos na rua contra a extrema direita e, sobretudo, contra o que ela representa de retrocesso no nosso país” me disse em entrevista

no último Pauta Pública

 o vice-presidente da União Nacional dos Estudantes, Gutemberg Rodrigues, sobre os atos e assembleias que têm sido organizados de forma espontânea por todo o país desde o dia 5 de outubro, sobretudo em apoio à reeleição de Lula, e que têm levado milhares de pessoas às ruas.


É sempre muito bonito ver os estudantes ocuparem os espaços públicos, e o Brasil tem momentos históricos importantes nesse sentido – seja na época da ditadura militar, com a Passeata dos Cem Mil em 1968, o movimento pelo Passe Livre em 2013, ou quando os secundaristas ocuparam as escolas de São Paulo em 2015.


Neste momento, em que tanto está em jogo no futuro do país dependendo do resultado das eleições que acontecem em poucos dias, e que ouvimos apenas que a juventude tem se radicalizado à direita, que há uma apatia na GenZ, que o elo de rebeldia com a esquerda se desfez e que não há mais pensamento crítico ou pautas coletivas, esse levante jovem no mundo é um alívio para nossos corações cansados.


Que esse levante dos estudantes, no Brasil e pelo mundo, nos sirva de inspiração  e nos dê energia nestes poucos dias que faltam para o segundo turno, em que nossas cabeças estão cheias, nossos corações estão pesados e parece que a energia vai acabar a qualquer momento. 


Mas que nos inspire também para além destas eleições, porque a luta não acaba com a apuração de votos, seja qual for o resultado.


Tem aquela frase bonita que o artista mexicano Enrique Cedillo criou para o Partido Comunista Mexicano e que eu gosto de lembrar sempre: “Que a injustiça não te entristeça, que te radicalize”.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Casual student support staff approvals in Nunavut drops from 75 to 15
content:
Nunavut’s Education Department approved 15 requests for casual student support assistants this school year, one-fifth of the number it approved the school year prior.


Of those 15, a total of 11 have been hired, according to figures the department provided Nunatsiaq News Wednesday.


The department is recruiting workers for the remaining four positions, spokesperson Kuthula Matshazi said in an email.


He said some positions couldn’t get filled despite recruiting efforts. Others remained vacant due to relief employees filling in or workers going on leave.


Student support workers join classroom teachers to help them deliver the curriculum. They work with individual students who require accommodations and those who follow unique education guidelines. School leaders can submit requests for casual support staff when they don’t have enough permanent staff to meet demand.


There is currently 206.5 support positions allocated to the territory, Matshazi said, 161 of which are being filled indeterminately. The department has also hired 164 on-call relief employees this year, to fill in for support workers who are on leave.


In the 2025-26 school year, the department approved 75 requests for casual support staff, resulting in 36 hires.


There are fewer casual support staff

assigned

 to Nunavut’s classrooms this year after Inuit Child First Initiative policies changed in February 2025.


That’s when Indigenous Services Canada disqualified funding requests through the initiative for student support assistants. Requests can still be submitted, but they are now considered on a case-by-case basis and approved only in exceptional circumstances.


During the 2024-25 school year, the funding program allowed district education authorities to hire 88 casual student support assistants, adding an extra number to those the Government of Nunavut regularly employs.

author: Chris Walker
title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump Bid to Halt Care for Incarcerated Trans People
content:
The decision is a rare win for transgender rights at the conservative-leaning Supreme Court.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The U.S. Supreme Court has denied an emergency petition from the Trump administration, which sought a stay on a lower court’s injunction on a policy that would have denied gender-affirming care to federally incarcerated transgender people.

That policy was implemented by the Bureau of Prisons (BOP) after President Donald Trump signed an executive order in January 2025 that denied the existence of transgender people. The order also directed federal agencies to take steps that would be consistent with that view, and included specific instructions for the BOP.

“The Attorney General shall ensure that the Bureau of Prisons revises its policies concerning medical care to be consistent with this order, and shall ensure that no Federal funds are expended for any medical procedure, treatment, or drug for the purpose of conforming an inmate’s appearance to that of the opposite sex,” the order reads.

After the BOP conformed to the order, a group of incarcerated trans people who had been receiving gender-affirming care sued the administration. The group is being represented by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), which argued that their Eighth Amendment protections against cruel and unusual punishment were being infringed upon.

A federal judge agreed, and, in August, ordered the policy to be blocked. The Trump administration challenged that finding, but the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit upheld it, prompting Solicitor General John Sauer to submit an emergency appeal to the Supreme Court.

The court has regularly ruled against transgender people, allowing state bans on trans athletes’ participation in sports, ruling in favor of a ban on transgender people in the military, and upholding state laws that bar gender-affirming care for trans children and teens. Yet on Wednesday, the court denied the Trump administration’s request.

“The application for stay presented to The Chief Justice and by him referred to the Court is denied,” the order read, giving no further explanation. Two justices for the court — Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas — would have granted the Trump administration’s request for a stay, the document said.

The ACLU heralded the high court’s denial of the emergency petition, stating, “This ruling affirms that federal prison officials can’t deny transgender people essential health care.”

Around 1,000 federally incarcerated trans people have also been diagnosed with gender dysphoria. The ruling means these individuals can continue receiving gender-affirming care while they remain in federal prisons or jails and the case moves forward in the lower courts.

author: labor4pal
title: As More Unions Oppose ICE and Israel, the Right Is Cracking Down (Truthout)
content:
The right is trying to gain access to labor unions’ minutes, membership lists, and Zoom chats.By Blanca Missé , Truthout Published October 21, 2026

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

On September 22, The Free Press attacked the California Faculty Association (CFA), which represents about 29,000 faculty, librarians, counselors, and coaches across the California State University (CSU) system. Drawing on private discussions about a proposed Jewish caucus, including communications from a union Zoom meeting, the article accused CFA of antisemitism. How those communications reached the publication remains unclear. Two days later, the Jewish Journal amplified those allegations, urging Gov. Gavin Newsom to consider them as he weighed California Assembly Bill (AB) 2551, CFA-sponsored legislation challenging campus protest restrictions imposed after the 2024 Palestine solidarity encampments. Less than a week after The Free Press story was published, Newsom vetoed the bill.

Pro-Israel and Jewish advocacy organizations had already campaigned against AB 2551 before the union’s internal deliberations were targeted, arguing that greater scrutiny would weaken rules needed to protect Jewish students from harassment and intimidation. Newsom’s veto does not prove coordination, but the campaign portraying CFA as hostile to Jewish students had become entangled with the union’s fight against campus protest restrictions.

The CSU’s systemwide policy prohibits encampments, overnight demonstrations, and unauthorized structures. The CSU Academic Senate immediately condemned the restrictions as undermining academic freedom when it was instituted in 2024, while CFA warned that vague definitions of disruption threatened constitutionally protected speech, assembly, protest, and future strike activity. A major 2026 ACLU-Amnesty study, investigating 80 campuses over two years, documented sweeping repression of Palestine solidarity protests. As the report found, universities “have imposed sweeping restrictions on student speech, initiated disciplinary actions against students, and imposed severe punishments, including expulsions and suspensions.” The ACLU has insisted that even legitimate time, place, and manner restrictions “must leave ample room for students to express themselves.”

The controversy reaches beyond CFA and CSU. Unions and rank-and-file organizations committed to Palestine solidarity have been forced to relitigate, again and again, whether anti-Zionism and solidarity with Palestinians constitute antisemitism — and whether such organizing should be systematically policed, investigated, or surveilled. At stake is a more fundamental right of the exploited: Can workers democratically connect economic struggles with Palestine solidarity, resistance to anti-immigrant and anti-Black racism, and the defense of civil liberties without exposing their organizing and deliberations to external pressure or repression?

We already have a word for the use of legal process as a political weapon: lawfare. You do not necessarily have to win. Investigation, expense, compelled disclosure, and possible sanctions can exact their own price.

Call its media counterpart pressfare: leaked material, selective or doctored quotations, and public identification can turn people into political targets and invite pressure on employers, universities, or government agencies.

The leaked CFA meeting should not be adjudicated through fragments selected for publication, especially when CFA’s statewide record contradicts the portrayal of a union indifferent to antisemitism. During the 2024 encampments, CFA opposed antisemitism and Islamophobia “in all forms” while supporting the encampments. Amid a 2025 federal antisemitism investigation, it stated that “as CFA members, we are united against antisemitism; it has no place in our communities,” while defending members’ academic freedom. CFA’s Palestine, Arab, and Muslim Caucus likewise defines its mission as confronting racism “in all its manifestations,” explicitly including antisemitism. The Free Press story — a clear example of pressfare — sought to overwrite this legacy with weaponized accusations, undermining the trust that workers place in the sanctity of their union spaces and processes.

Antisemitism demands to be taken seriously — which is why accusations of anti-Jewish discrimination should not be …

author: admin
title: Latest Essay by Maksym Kryvosh (Plokhoi), Liberation Prisoner in Ukraine
content:
I was taken from my cell to a room to participate in a court hearing remotely, via video conference. The court was considering a petition from the prison guards to place me in solitary confinement for two months. (For the kleptocracy known as Ukraine, it wasn’t enough that I’ve been in solitary for seven years, or the 13-year sentence I was awarded for fighting for Justice; they also had to throw me into the punishment cell for periods ranging from 14 days to three months—bringing my total to 18 stints in the punishment cell over three years).

The judge was reading out the ruling, but I wasn’t listening anymore, nor was I looking at the monitor. I was looking at the window—a large moth was beating its wings against the glass. It was unclear how it had gotten there; the windows were sealed shut. I told the guards: I won’t go back to the cell until I set it free… It worked! Outside, I opened my palms; it was a Peacock butterfly—the most beautiful butterfly I had ever seen—its colors shimmering and mesmerizing in the sunlight. It felt at ease on my palm and didn’t want to fly away. For a whole minute, we were happy.

*** July 21, 2020, Lutsk, Ukraine: the “Anti-System Day” protest action; the president of a nation of forty million people fulfills my main demand—recording and publishing a video message titled “EVERYONE MUST WATCH THE FILM ‘EARTHLINGS’.” No one was hurt. (I don’t count). The result?! What did I achieve?

Let me quote two online publications; let facts and figures answer my question. “27,000 views in a single day—in the Ukrainian language alone.” This refers to the Wikipedia page for the film *Earthlings*. This means that millions of people across all languages viewed the page over the course of a few days. It means that some of them watched the film itself.

This is discussed in a second report titled “The Plokhoi Got His Way”: The film *Earthlings* saw a surge in global popularity thanks to the Lutsk “terrorist”… in a single day, search queries for the film within the Ukrainian segment of Google hit peak popularity—a score of 100… the movie became the most popular title on the KinoPoisk service. It climbed 4,265 places in the rankings in just 24 hours, achieving a rating of 8.7 based on 12,700 votes…

According to Google Trends data from the last day, interest in the film spiked in the USA, Canada, Brazil, most of Asia, and across the entire European Union (July 22, 2020, “Kommentarii COMMENTS.UA”). “Following the events involving the Lutsk terrorist, the film *Earthlings* saw record-breaking popularity on Wikipedia… The article, published in 2015, received three times fewer views over five years than it did in a single day—July 21…” (July 27, 2020, “Korotko Pro”)

Unfortunately, it is impossible to track statistics on how many people had their conscience regarding animals awakened by the “Lutsk terrorist”—people around the world who, after watching *Earthlings*, paused—even for a moment—to reflect on the Meaning of Life.

*** The “Anti-System Day” performance took place in Lutsk’s central square—Teatralna Square—near the monument to Lesya Ukrainka. She authored a philosophical parable-novella titled *The Butterfly*. It is a parable about the yearning for the light of true life, and the choice between a “safe” existence in the darkness of insignificance versus a dangerous life—a striving toward the light of Truth. “He sought the light”—that is how the novella ends. …about the life of a moth. Fitting words for an obituary, for an epitaph… A butterfly would not be a butterfly if it did not fly toward the flame that kills it. It flies to prove that DEATH DOES NOT EXIST. It flies to be resurrected as Truth.

So it is with man: he is not truly Human if perishing—being crucified—for the sake of Truth is not a source of happiness for him. By surrendering our mortal shell, we attain our immortal essence. The moth teaches us the wisdom of living each day—this very day—to the fullest. Of fearlessly celebrating Life in the here and now. The butterfly is a living Philosophy!

*** Anton Chekhov wrote: “With insects, a butterfly is born from a caterpillar, but with humans, it is the opposite: a caterpillar emerges from a butterfly.” We, “political animals,” arrive on this beautiful planet to be human—that is, beings possessing both the capacity and the duty to realize and give meaning to Life through All-Encompassing Love-and-Justice; yet, while we come here to be human, we exist and depart as something less than …
